fr75bd.title: Экс-глава МОК Бах: Россия должна участвовать в чемпионате мира по хоккею в Германии
fr75bd.content:
Бывший президент Международного олимпийского комитета (МОК) Томас Бах (Thomas Bach) высказался в поддержку участия сборной России в чемпионате мира по хоккею, который пройдет в 2027 году в Германии. Об этом он заявил в субботу, в интервью изданию Sport1.

Бах считает, что "от государств и правительств не должно зависеть, кто может принимать участие в спортивных соревнованиях". По его мнению, спорту необходимо сохранять автономию и нейтралитет, поскольку "значение имеют спортивные квалификационные показатели, а не политические взгляды". Экс-президент МОК также добавил, что всегда придерживался такой позиции.

Тем не менее он выразил обеспокоенность возможными последствиями для Украины, если РФ и Беларусь будут допущены к участию в чемпионате мира по хоккею. В таком случае Международная федерация хоккея на льду (IIHF) будет вынуждена пересмотреть систему распределения мест и состав участников. Соревнования в 2027 году рассчитаны на 16 сборных. Последнее место в элитном хоккейном дивизионе получила Украина. И именно ее участие может оказаться под угрозой, если организаторы решат допустить РФ к чемпионату.

"Решающим фактором должна оставаться спортивная квалификация. Лишать кого-либо уже постфактум права на участие, заслуженного по спортивному принципу, я считаю крайне сомнительным шагом, вызывающим серьезное беспокойство", - подчеркнул Бах.IIHF пытается оспорить решение арбитражного суда

Следующий чемпионат мира по хоккею среди мужчин запланирован на май 2027 и должен пройти в Германии. В конце октября Спортивный арбитражный суд (CAS) обязал IIHF допустить российские сборные на чемпионаты мира сезона 2026/27, несмотря на продолжающуюся полномасштабную войну РФ против Украины. В IIHF выразили несогласие с этим решением и указали на проблемы с получением виз, обеспечением безопасности, логистикой и изменением формата соревнований в короткий сроки.

Накануне стало известно, что IIHF подала апелляцию на решение CAS, обосновав иск тем, что двое из трех членов арбитражного суда, ответственных за принятие решения о допуске российской сборной к международным соревнованиям, не раскрыли информацию о деловых связях с РФ.

Сборные Норвегии, Швеции, Латвии, Финляндии, Дании и Чехии уже объявили, что не будут играть против России на чемпионате. Несколько крупных спонсоров IIHF также пригрозили отозвать финансирование турнира в случае допуска РФ.

Власти ФРГ также раскритиковали решение CAS, однако сообщили, что отказ в визах российским хоккеистам (такую меру выбрала Канада, чтобы не допустить молодежную сборную России к соревнованиям) не решит проблему их участия в чемпионате, а лишь приведет к переносу турнира в другую страну. Берлин поддерживает дальнейшие переговоры федераций.

gh-1424470601.title: GitHub - elipp/ctr-rs: An online-oriented Rust reimplementation of the CTR Native project (PS1, 1999)
gh-1424470601.content:
ctr-rs is an online-focused reimplementation of Crash Team Racing (PS1, 1999), written in Rust.
What's here

Exact, reference-checked physics - Kart physics/collision follow the original tick for tick. We check them against the C decompilation, ctr-native. The weapons, crates and the level's objects follow the original closely.
Truly native performance, framerates/aspect ratio - The original look definitely has its own charm to it, but the reimplementation has no need for PGXP or other (awesome) emulator hacks, since we have full-precision vertices and a real depth buffer.
Cross-platform - The project runs and builds on any system that Rust builds on, and on the browser too!
Hassle-free online play - No patched ROMs, emulator builds or launchers required.
Peer-to-peer networking - Players are directly connected to each other over QUIC, using iroh.
No network setup - No port forwarding, DMZ or dedicated servers. Connections punch through NAT automatically, and fall back to a relay when they can't.
30 Hz simulation, hi-FPS rendering - The game state advances at the original's 30 ticks/s, independent of the rendering frame rate.
Custom tracks - Just drag and drop an .xdelta (from e.g. CTR Custom Tracks) to the client window, and immediately play them with your friends.

What's not here (not currently planned)

Adventure mode
Time trial
Relic race
Battle mode

Running it
You provide your own legally obtained disc image of Crash Team Racing. The client asks for it with a file dialog the first time; or point CTR_BIN at it, or put it at assets/ctr-u.bin.
cargo run -p client

A build from the releases asks for the disc image the first time it starts. The macOS build is not signed, so macOS refuses to open it at first: allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security ("Open Anyway"), or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ctr-rs.app. On Linux, the .AppImage runs as it is once it is executable (chmod +x).
The client has no command line options. ] and [ switch the level, . and , switch the racer, and Enter opens the in-game console for / commands and chat.
ctr-query (crates/query) looks up a level's data from the disc, and ctr-map (crates/map) imports and describes custom tracks.
Running the tests
cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast

Some tests need files that are not in the repo, and without them they skip and pass without checking anything. Their names say which:

needs_disc_…: the disc image (assets/ctr-u.bin, or CTR_BIN), or the folder prepared from it (assets/disc, or CTR_DISC_DIR).
needs_reference_…: ctr-native at the commit in docs/ctr-native.rev, checked out at reference/ctr-native (git-ignored). Most of them also build the C side with gcc -m32 (x86-64 only), which on Debian and Ubuntu is the gcc-multilib package.
needs_disc_needs_reference_…: both.

Filters match anywhere in the name, so cargo test --workspace -- --skip needs_disc skips every test that needs the disc (those that need both as well), and --skip needs_reference every test that needs ctr-native.
A new test that needs either must start with its prefix, needs_disc_ before needs_reference_ when it needs both, and no other test or module may have either word in its name. CI relies on the names: it skips the needs_disc tests, and runs the rest with ctr-native checked out. A test that reads the disc without the prefix skips there and passes without checking anything, and one that reads ctr-native without it still runs, but is not skipped by --skip needs_reference where there is no ctr-native.
git clone https://github.com/CTR-Tools/ctr-native reference/ctr-native
git -C reference/ctr-native checkout "$(cat docs/ctr-native.rev)"

Another commit of ctr-native may not match what the tests expect (they fail to link, or differ by a field), so bump docs/ctr-native.rev together with the tests that need it. Run cargo test --workspace -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -i skipping to see which tests skipped. CI has no disc, so it skips those tests (--skip needs_disc); it checks out ctr-native and sets CTR_REQUIRE_REFERENCE, which makes a test that finds no reference fail instead of skipping.
Prior work
This project stands on the work of the CTR community, and absolutely could not exist without it:

ctr-native, a native PC port of the game built on the decompilation. It is our first reference for how the game behaves, and the oracle our physics tests compare against.
CTR-ModSDK, and the decompilation, symbols and headers that came out of it. We use them for the layouts of the game's data and for what ctr-native lacks.
The CTR-Tools community, whose years of reverse engineering of the game's formats and code made both of those possible.
PsyCross and REDRIVER2, whose GTE (the PS1's geometry coprocessor) implementation is ported in crates/gte.

ctr-rs is a Rust port that works from these projects. It is not a fork of any of them.
Notice
ctr-rs is an independent fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment, Activision Publishing, Naughty Dog or any other rights holder. It ships no game content: no art, models, textures, sounds, music, levels or disc contents. You provide your own legally obtained copy of the game, and everything is read from it at runtime. Custom tracks are not shipped either: you import them yourself from patches you have obtained.
Crash Team Racing was developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment. Crash Bandicoot and Crash Team Racing are trademarks of Activision Publishing, Inc. PlayStation is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc.
Our own code is licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3, which is the license of ctr-native and CTR-ModSDK, the projects it is ported from. crates/gte is also derived from MIT-licensed code, and its notice is in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Also, LLM-based tooling was heavily used in the construction of this project.

gh-1335797829.content:
A native PC port of Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball (Windows, macOS & Linux), built by static recompilation, with the goal of rewriting it into readable source.

Download ·
Changelog ·
Status ·
Controls ·
Report a bug

ImportantThis project ships no game files. You need your own legally obtained copy
of the USA Xbox release. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
rights holders.

About
The original Xbox executable is lifted to C with a static recompiler, then
linked against a hand-written runtime that replaces the Xbox kernel imports,
audio output and key Direct3D 8 and DirectSound APIs with native Windows
equivalents. The rest of the game, including its statically linked libraries,
still runs as generated code. The plan is to replace game logic with readable,
hand-written source one data-structure cluster at a time while the game keeps
running; so far the startup thread entry and the girls' per-frame joint bend
and morph blend have been rewritten.

Captured from the native port at 2560x1440.

Remaining work is tracked in the
offline acceptance tracker.
Development results do not guarantee every route works in the packaged beta.
Play the beta
Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, a supported USA game ISO and internet
access. The release ZIP bundles Python, Capstone, Git, CMake and the ISO
extractor. Setup compiles the game with the free
llvm-mingw clang compiler. On first
run it downloads it into the setup folder (190 MB, about 715 MB extracted). This
needs no administrator approval, Visual Studio or Windows SDK (#115).
Setup also downloads Microsoft's DXC shader compiler (32 MB) for ray-traced GI.
Release ZIPs up to 0.6.0 RC1 instead offer to run Microsoft's C++ Build Tools
installer, which needs administrator approval and several GB of disk space.

Download the ZIP from the
latest release and
extract it into a new folder with a short path.
Open Launcher.cmd (after setup, Launcher.exe opens the same window),
open Build, choose your ISO and press Build game. Wait for Build
complete. (Dragging the ISO onto BuildGame.cmd does the same.) With a
release ZIP up to 0.6.0 RC1, first follow any Microsoft installer prompts.
Pick resolution, MSAA, SMAA and sun shadows in the launcher, then press
Play. Afterwards DOAXBV.exe starts the game with those saved
choices without opening the launcher. Running RunGame.cmd directly uses
the defaults.

On macOS:

Install the prerequisites in docs/building.md.
Run ./build_game.sh /path/to/game.iso and wait for setup to complete.
Run ./launcher.sh to select resolution, volume, and soundtrack options, then press Play (or run ./run_game.sh directly).

On Linux and Steam Deck, follow docs/building.md;
the scripts are the same as on macOS.
Setup extracts your ISO and builds a native Release runner locally; the package
contains tools and source, never a prebuilt runner or game data. When updating,
build in a new folder and keep your previous install and saves. GitHub's
automatic source archives are source only; see the
source build guide for their prerequisites.
New and older saves start in Digital control mode until you pick a PC
control mode; later Analog or Digital choices are remembered. See the
controller guide.
Xbox and PlayStation 4/5 controllers work directly. Do not run DS4Windows
with the game: it adds an emulated Xbox controller, so one pad appears twice
and takes two player ports. If you launch through Steam, turn Steam Input off
for the game.
Build the tests from source
The runtime tests build without any game files or submodules:
git clone https://github.com/NoRain211/doaxbv-re.git
cd doaxbv-re
cmake -S recomp-runtime -B build/recomp-runtime -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"
cmake --build build/recomp-runtime --config Release --parallel 2
ctest --test-dir build/recomp-runtime -C Release --output-on-failure
To run the same tests with the llvm-mingw clang that setup uses, see the
source build guide.
This produces test executables, not the game runner. For ISO setup from source,
follow the source build guide. Passing tests does not
establish full game accuracy.
Repository layout

Path
Contents

recomp-runtime/
Runtime, kernel and input adapters, audio, D3D8 replacements, presentation, tests

xbe/
XBE parsing and hashing

tools/
Extraction and launcher scripts, lifter submodule, source patches, export checks

docs/
Build guide, controls, saves, graphics, status and research

third_party/
Pinned rbengine and recomp-net dependencies (notes)

private/
Ignored local game inputs, generated output and run evidence

Contributing
Read the contribution guide first. Translation defects are
fixed in the lifter and regenerated; generated game C is never patched by hand.
When reporting a bug, include
your build version, steps to reproduce, what happened, your hardware and
controller, and the stop or crash message
(how to read logs).
Remove private paths from logs, and never upload game binaries, generated game
C, assets, extracted filenames, saves, BIOS data or private run evidence.
Contributors

Tommy McLeroy (@tmcleroy): creator of the
macOS and Linux ports (#99, #103).

AI assistance
This project uses large language models and AI coding agents extensively for
code, reverse-engineering analysis, debugging, tests and documentation. Their
output can contain mistakes; changes are reviewed and tested, and unverified
behavior is tracked as such.
License
Original code and documentation are licensed under
GPL-3.0-or-later; see also NOTICE. Third-party components
keep their own licenses. The license grants no rights to the game or its assets.

gh-1358365242.title: GitHub - JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp: Native Windows, Linux, macOS and Android (beta) port of Pokémon Snap (N64) by static recompilation. Plays like the cartridge by default; every enhancement is opt-in. Bring your own dump; no game data is included.
gh-1358365242.content:
Snap64 Recomp
Snap64 Recomp is a native PC port of Pokémon Snap (Nintendo 64, US release)
for Windows, Linux, the Steam Deck and macOS. It is made with
N64: Recompiled, which translates
the game's own code so that it runs directly on a PC. The method is called
static recompilation. RT64 draws the picture.
A beta of the same port runs on Android phones and handhelds.
Out of the box it plays like the cartridge. Widescreen, higher frame rates,
mouse and gyro aim, button rebinding, fast forward, photo export and the
Snap Station's printer are there when you want them, and each stays off
until you turn it on.
Download the latest release
This repository and its releases contain no game assets. You need your own
ROM of the US cartridge to play. Only the US cartridge's ROM works: the
Japanese, European and Australian releases are different builds of the game,
and the port is made from the US one.
NoteSnap64 Recomp is released only on this repository's
Releases page.
Copies posted anywhere else are not the project's. On Windows the port is
a ZIP holding a folder with Snap64Recomp.exe, and nothing has to be
installed. It opens no network connection and asks for no account or
password. Each file has a .sha256 beside it, and SECURITY.md
says how to check a download.

Contents: Get it running ·
Screenshots ·
System requirements · Features ·
Faithful by default · Controls ·
Linux and Steam Deck · macOS ·
Android (beta) ·
FAQ · Known issues ·
What's next · Reporting a bug ·
Contributing ·
What has been verified ·
Building · How it was made ·
Thanks · Documentation · License
The manual has every control, page, hotkey and setting.
The rest of the documentation is listed near the end.
Get it running

In a hurry? The download holds a START HERE.txt with the short
version. The one thing to know: this port has no launcher and no overlay.
Everything it adds is inside the game's own Options screen. Press Esc,
or Select on a pad, and it opens over the screen you are on: the title,
the lab, the course map, a paused course. Widescreen, the frame rate and
the other enhancements are under Options > Graphics. They all start off,
set to what the console did.

These steps are for Windows. Linux and the Steam Deck are further
down.

Download Snap64Recomp-1.1.7-win64.zip from the
Releases
page and unpack it anywhere. It holds one folder,
Snap64Recomp-1.1.7-win64, with Snap64Recomp.exe inside. Nothing has
to be installed.
Have your ROM of the US cartridge ready. (A ROM is the cartridge's
contents, read out into one file.) Put it next to Snap64Recomp.exe
with the name pokemonsnap.z64, or just start the program. If no ROM is
there, the program asks for the file, checks it, and copies it into
place under that name. It only asks once. You do not have to check the
file yourself: a wrong one is refused, with a message that says why.
Start Snap64Recomp.exe. The program is not signed, so Windows may
first show a "Windows protected your PC" box (SmartScreen). Click "More
info", then "Run anyway", and it will not ask again. The first start
takes a little longer than later ones, because the renderer builds the
shader programs your GPU needs. They are kept in cache/, so the next
start is quick.

A few keys to know first:

Esc opens the port's Options on almost any screen, and closes them
again. On a pad it is Select. The Graphics and Sound pages are in there.
In-game pages in the manual names the few
screens where the key does nothing.
Enter is the game's Start. In a course it opens the pause menu:
Continue, Quit Course, Retry, Options.
F11 switches fullscreen on and off, in a course or anywhere else.
The window's maximize button fills the screen with the window itself,
and the port opens it that way again next time.
To quit, choose Game, the last row of the game's Options
screen, then Exit Game: A asks, a second A closes, B stays. Or hold Esc for a second
and let go. A box asks first, and Enter or Esc keeps you playing, so a
hand resting on the key cannot end a run.

Saves live in saves/ next to the program, so keep that folder when you
update. Keyboard and controller mappings are under Controls.
If something goes wrong, Running in the manual
says what Windows or an antivirus may object to, and what to attach to a
bug report.
Screenshots

Every picture is the port's own render at 1440p, with Render Scale and
Anti-Aliasing both at 8x on the Graphics page, cropped to the game's
picture. The full set, with a caption for each, is in
docs/SCREENSHOTS.md.

System requirements

Windows: 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or newer) or 11, and a GPU
whose driver supports Direct3D 12 with Shader Model 6.3. A driver from
before late 2018 is too old, and the port says so at start.
Linux and Steam Deck: a Vulkan 1.2 driver, and either Flatpak or the
system's SDL2 and GTK 3; x86_64, or ARM64 for the tarball built for it.
The Linux builds are experimental.
macOS: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer, on Apple Silicon or Intel; one app
runs on both. The Mac build has run on GitHub's virtual Mac and not yet on
a physical one (see macOS).
Android (beta): Android 10 or newer on a 64-bit (arm64) phone or
handheld, with a Vulkan 1.2 driver. It has run on one phone, with a
Snapdragon 8 Elite (see Android).
CPU: a 64-bit x86 processor with SSE4.1. That is Intel from 2008
(Penryn), AMD from 2011 (Bulldozer), or anything newer.
Your own ROM of the US cartridge. Its SHA-1 checksum is
edc7c49cc568c045fe48be0d18011c30f393cbaf, the value the
decompilation project
publishes. .z64, .v64 and .n64 files all work. The port checks the
file for you, and refuses a wrong one with both checksums shown.

Nothing has to be installed. The download holds everything but the game.
No one has tested how old a graphics card can be and still run the port.
Zelda 64: Recompiled,
which uses the same renderer, names the GeForce GT 630, the Radeon HD 7750
and the Intel HD 510 as the oldest that should work. This port has run on an
AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti Super, an Intel UHD 630
and the Steam Deck. If it closes at start, update the graphics driver
first. The detail is in
the manual.

Features
Each of these is a row on the game's own Options screen, or a key. Each
starts off, or at the console's setting. The manual has
every one in full.

Settings inside the game. The port adds Graphics, Sound, Controls,
Mods and Game pages to the game's own Options screen, drawn in the game's own
font. The Graphics page has seventeen rows in three groups, the
display, the picture and the fixes, from Render Scale to Jynx Recolor.
Widescreen shows more of the course: a wider field of view that
fills the window's own shape, 16:9, the Deck's 16:10 or an ultrawide 21:9,
not a stretched picture. The title, the lab and the menus stay 4:3.
Higher frame rates, matched to your display or set to a rate you
choose. The game's own logic still runs at its thirty frames a second;
the renderer draws the frames in between (frame interpolation).
Keyboard and mouse. W A S D and the mouse aim the camera in a course,
the way a mouse does in any first-person game.
Controllers and gyro. Anything SDL has a mapping for works, and the
community's list of more pads ships beside the program. A DualSense, a
DualShock 4, a Switch Pro controller and the Steam Deck can aim by gyro.
Button rebinding in the game. Every key, mouse button and pad button
can be changed on the Button Setup page, or in the settings file.
Fast forward and slow motion, each while a key is held. The console's
own clocks run faster or slower, so the game steps through the same
frames it would have anyway, with the same scores and the same saves.
Photo export. P, or the pad's right stick pressed in, saves the photo
on screen as a PNG at the game's own resolution.
Photo Detail shows Oak's photos and the album from the renderer's
full-resolution render, instead of the console's 320x210 pixels.
The Snap Station was the 1999 kiosk that printed your photos as a
sheet of sixteen stickers. The port emulates it on controller port 4,
from the cartridge's own code for it, and Print gives you the sheet as
PNG files (SNAP-STATION.md).
Two things the re-releases changed, reproduced and off by default.
One is the Virtual Console's Jynx recolor. The other is a Cutscene Fix
for the one frame the console drew from inside the player model, at the
end of two intros.
Linux and the Steam Deck. A native Linux build, played on a Deck in
Desktop Mode and in Gaming Mode. The Windows build also runs under Proton
(STEAM-DECK.md).
Mods and texture packs. The runtime's .nrm mod loader and RT64's
texture-pack loader are built in, and the Options screen has a Mods page
for them. A
mod template
and the game's symbol files
let anyone write a mod (MODS.md). No mods or packs ship
with the port; three mods are published in the
mods repository.

Faithful by default
The port behaves like the console by default, and every enhancement is
something you turn on. Frame rate, aspect ratio, anti-aliasing, overscan,
texture filtering and dithering all start as the console had them. Only
what you turn on changes.
Three defaults are not the console's own. The 3D picture is drawn at the
window's resolution. 2D content that would be scaled anyway is drawn sharp.
The finished frame is scaled with anti-aliasing. Each is one setting away
from the original, and
Faithful by default in the manual
names the setting for each. It also says how higher frame rates sit with
the game's photo scoring.
Controls
Keyboard and mouse, as the port ships them:

N64
Key
Mouse
In a course

Control stick
W A S D
moving the mouse
aims the camera

A
X
left button
the photo when zoomed, an apple when not

B
Z
middle button
the pester ball

Z
Left Shift
right button
zoom (hold or switch, the game's own option)

R

dash

L
Q

C-Down
K
wheel down
the Poké Flute

C-Up
I
wheel up
turn to face behind

C-Left / C-Right
J / L
side buttons (back / forward)
turn left / right

Start
Enter

pause

D-pad
Arrow keys

A pad works as soon as it is plugged in:

N64
Pad

Control stick
left stick

A
A

B
B or X

Z
left shoulder button

L and R
the triggers

C buttons
right stick

On a pad, the right stick pressed in saves the photo on screen, and Select
opens the port's Options.
Hold Tab, or the right shoulder button, for fast forward. Hold Space, or
press the left stick in, for slow motion. A tap on Esc opens the port's
Options on almost any screen. Esc held for a second and released asks
whether to quit. From a pad, Exit Game, on the Game page of the Options
screen, quits.
Every binding can be changed in the game, on the Controls page's Button
Setup row, or in the settings file's keys table. The mouse's speed, the
gyro, the dead zone, the pad's stick layout and which controllers work are
in the manual.
Linux and Steam Deck
The release page has three native Linux builds, marked experimental,
beside the Windows one: a tarball for x86_64, a Flatpak for x86_64, and a
tarball for ARM64. On a Steam Deck either the tarball, the Flatpak or the
Windows build through Proton works; players ran Proton on the day of the
first release, and the x86_64 tarball has been played on a Deck, in Desktop
Mode and in Gaming Mode. The tarball needs the system's SDL2, GTK 3 and a
Vulkan 1.2 driver; the Flatpak brings its own and installs with one
command, flatpak install --user Snap64Recomp-<version>-linux-x86_64.flatpak,
keeping everything it writes under ~/.var/app/io.github.jackandbeans.Snap64Recomp/.
Rendering is Vulkan only. The Flatpak and the ARM64 build are made and
started on GitHub's machines and have not been played on any; the first
report from a Deck or an ARM machine would be welcome.
STEAM-DECK.md has the steps for each route, the
Deck's controls and gyro, its screen, quitting from a pad, and the icon.

The release page has a Mac build, Snap64Recomp-<version>-macos-universal.zip:
one app for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, macOS 14 or newer. Unzip it and
move Snap64Recomp.app anywhere. It is signed by nobody, so the first start
is a right-click and Open, or on macOS 15 a double-click, then System
Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway; once is enough. The port asks
for your ROM on the first start and keeps everything it writes in
~/Library/Application Support/Snap64 Recomp/ (the ROM, saves, photos,
settings, the log and the mods folder); nothing goes inside the app.
Rendering is Metal. Mods load as on the other platforms.
What has been seen: GitHub's own Mac builds the app and runs it on every
release candidate, and on it the game boots to the intro, plays the Beach
with photos scored, loads a mod, and quits cleanly, natively and through
Rosetta 2. No physical Mac has run it yet; the first report from one would
be welcome, with snap64.log from the folder above.
Android (beta)
The release page has an Android app, Snap64Recomp-<version>-android.apk,
for Android 10 or newer on arm64 phones and handhelds. Install it from the
file, give it your ROM, and play with a pad or with the touch controls it
draws beside the picture. It keeps everything it writes in Internal
storage > Snap64. Rendering is Vulkan. Mods load as on the other platforms.
It is a beta. It has run on one phone, a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra with a
Snapdragon 8 Elite, and on Google's Android emulator. No real pad has been
tried yet, and no other GPU. ANDROID.md has the steps,
the touch controls, and what was run where. A report from any phone or
handheld would be welcome, with snap64.log from the Snap64 folder.
FAQ
What is static recompilation?
The game's own program code is translated into C and compiled for the PC.
The translation is done once, ahead of time, and not while you play.
N64: Recompiled does it.
N64ModernRuntime stands in
for the console's operating system, RT64
draws the picture, and SDL2 provides the window, the input and the sound.
How is this related to the decompilation project?
The game's code is recompiled from the ROM, not built from the
decompilation's source. The port
still depends on that project. The functions the port changes are copies of
their decompiled source, compiled against its headers and symbols, and what
is known about the game's code was learned there.
Where is the settings menu? Is there a launcher?
There is no launcher. Everything is inside the game's own Options screen:
press Esc, or Select on a pad. In-game pages
in the manual shows every page.
Where are my save and my settings?
Next to the program. The save is saves/pokemonsnap.bin and the settings
are snapsettings.json; keep both when you update. Everything the port
writes is in that folder, so the folder can be moved as it is. On Linux, if
the folder cannot be written, the files go to ~/.config/Snap64Recomp.
How do I use a different ROM file?
The port uses pokemonsnap.z64 next to the program. Remove or replace that
file. With none there, the port asks for one at the next start.
How do I set up gyro aim on a Steam Deck?
In Desktop Mode, or with Steam Input off for the shortcut, turn on Options >
Controls > Gyro Aim. In Gaming Mode the game cannot read the Deck's gyro
itself. Set Steam's Gyro Behavior to As Mouse there, and the port's mouse
aim follows it. STEAM-DECK.md has the steps.
Windows warns me about the program. Is that normal?
Yes. The program is not signed, so SmartScreen may show "Windows protected
your PC" the first time: "More info", then "Run anyway". Download it only
from this repository's Releases page, where each file comes with a SHA-256
checksum. The port opens no network connection at all.
Can I use mods or HD texture packs?
Yes. Mods go in mods/ and texture packs in texture_packs/, and Options >
Mods turns mods on and off. MODS.md says how to install
them, and how to write one.

Known issues

A few 2D pictures still move at the game's rate when the frame rate is
raised: one that slides past the side of a menu in a wide window, and one
that jumps a long way in a single frame.
Parts of the Snap Station printer's look are estimates: its lettering,
and the timing of its passes.
A Pokémon can pop out of the picture before it has fully left it. The
console does the same, and the port keeps the cartridge's rule.
A Nintendo pad over Bluetooth may answer a moment late after a pause.
This is read from SDL's code and has not been seen on such a pad; a
report from one would settle it.
Vulkan on Windows is lightly tested. It is there for a machine whose
Direct3D 12 path fails.
With Overscan Crop off, a thin light strip shows at the left of the lab's
panel. The console drew the same pixels; Overscan Crop (F2) is the
television's view.
Android is a beta: one phone and the emulator have run it, and no real
pad yet.

KNOWN-ISSUES.md explains each one in full.
What's next
Planned, roughly in this order.

Reports from other machines. Most releases so far were made of what
players reported, and later ones will be too. The issue form is the way
to send one, with snap64.log attached.
Android on more devices, with a pad. The beta has run on one phone
and on Android's emulator. It needs a handheld with its own pad, a phone
with a Bluetooth pad, a phone with a Mali GPU, and hands on the touch
controls.
A physical Mac. The Mac build runs on GitHub's virtual Mac; it needs
someone with a physical one to try it.
A Linux desktop. The native build has run under WSL and on a Deck,
and on no Linux desktop yet. The first report from one would be welcome.
Linux on ARM64 and the Flatpak. Both are built on GitHub's machines,
and no machine has played the game from either yet.
Gyro on a controller. Gyro aim is confirmed on a Steam Deck and on
no other pad. A DualSense, a DualShock 4 or a Switch Pro controller
would settle it.
Smooth 2D, the last cases. A picture that slides past the side of a
menu in a wide window still moves at the game's own rate.
A mod that adds something new to a course. It will show what the
mod kit can do.

The same list, with what to try and a place to reply, is pinned under
Discussions.
Reporting a bug
Open an issue at
github.com/JackandBeans/Snap64Recomp/issues.
The issue form asks for these:

snap64.log from the run that went wrong; it is written next to the
executable
Snap64Recomp.map, if the log has [SNAP-AV] lines
your snapsettings.json
what you were doing, and which system, GPU and driver you have

What Windows or an antivirus may object to, and where the port's files
live, are under Running in the manual.
Contributing
Bug reports, pull requests and mods are all welcome. Most of the releases
since the first were made of what players reported, and the
changelog names who reported each fault beside its fix.
For code, CONTRIBUTING.md says what a pull request
needs. For a mod, MODS.md and the
mod template
are the way in. Questions and requests have a place under
Discussions.
What has been verified
The whole game has been played through on a Windows PC. That is every
course, every course again with Widescreen on, Oak's evaluations, the
Report, the album, the Gallery and a Snap Station print. On a Steam Deck,
the Beach, the menus, the settings and the station have been played. On
GitHub's virtual Mac, the intro, a Beach ride with its photos scored and a
mod's hooks have run, natively and under Rosetta 2. On an Android phone in
Samsung's test lab, the intro, a Beach ride with its photos scored, the
menus and a mod's hooks have run; the touch controls and a pad made in
software have run on Android's emulator.
Every release also passes an automated suite before it ships
(tools/release_check.py). On the 1.1.7 executable it passed 39 of 39
checks, and the station's 5 of 5. VERIFICATION.md says what
each check does, what every release reported, and what has only been read
from the code and not seen.
Building
See BUILDING.md. Short version: the decompilation and IDO
under WSL, N64Recomp for the game and the patches, CMake and MSVC on
Windows, and a list of things git does not carry
(What a clean checkout is missing).

gh-1412425732.title: GitHub - YodaMMM/NightfirePort: Nightfire Rust: a native Windows PC port of 007: Nightfire (PS2), written in Rust
gh-1412425732.content:
Warning
This port is not finished.
Nightfire Rust is a work in progress. Expect bugs, missing features, and levels that don't yet play like the original. The driving missions can't be played yet. If you hit a problem, press F10 in game (or Report crash in the launcher) to send a report.

Nightfire Rust is a native Windows PC port of 007: Nightfire (PS2), written in Rust. This 007 Nightfire port is rebuilt from the game's own data and logic (the PlayStation 2 release, NTSC-U SLUS-20579), runs natively on Windows with no emulator, and treats mouse and keyboard as first-class input. The repository is named NightfirePort.

What this is, and isn't

It is a port. The game's behaviour is re-implemented in Rust, using a Ghidra decompile of the disc's executables as the reference for what the original code does.
It is not an emulator and not a static recompiler. No PS2 code runs.
You need your own disc. The port reads your disc image at run time (picked in the launcher, or NF_ISO / a path on the command line). No game files are in this repository, and nothing the tools extract is committed.
The 2002 PC "Nightfire" is a different game (Gearbox, GoldSrc) and is not involved.

The disc holds two engines: ACTION.ELF (Eurocom's on-foot engine; shipped unstripped with 3,038 functions and 5,603 symbols) and DRIVING.ELF (EA's EAGL-based driving engine, stripped). The on-foot engine is where almost all of the work has gone so far.
Status at a glance

In short:

On foot: all 27 on-foot archives on the disc load and run. Not every level can be finished yet. The walkthrough tests that drive Bond through the same input a player uses still stop on two levels (07000016 in Countdown and 0700001b in Equinox), several others still move Bond past a spot the walk cannot cross yet, and other levels have known problems. Each level's page in docs/levels/ lists them.
Driving: the five driving missions can't be played. Picking one in the mission list shows a notice and unlocks the next mission. Parts of the driving engine exist as model code only: vehicle physics, the road network, AI traffic, input mapping, HUD data and mission scripts.
Front end: it follows the game's own menu flow. With the movies feature, the disc's videos play where the game plays them: the boot logos, the intro, the menu backdrops, and each mission's briefing and outro.
Multiplayer: the game's on-foot match rules and modes run on the 8 arenas, with bots, on one screen. There is no split screen. Online play is new in the port (see below).
Cut-scenes: faces animate from the game's own morph data.

The latest release is v0.1.26 (2026-10-30). The releases since 0.1.19 have been single-player fixes across Double Cross, The Exchange, Night Shift, Chain Reaction, Phoenix Fire and Countdown; among them, Double Cross part 1 can now be finished behind Mayhew (0.1.24). Each release's notes are on the Releases page.
"Cited" in the graphic is deliberately a loose measure. It counts a function whose address or name appears anywhere in the Rust crates or the docs. The port-map documents hold the stricter per-function grade (ported, partial, stub, stand-in, not started). The verification ledger lists three functions proven bit-exact against recorded PCSX2 calls (PS2Sinf, Quat_QuatToMat, Rand_Rand, 40 of 40 each).
What the port adds over the PS2 version
Everything below is on top of the game as it shipped. The game's own controller mapping, auto-aim and secret codes are still there.
High frame rate. The simulation stays at the game's fixed 60 Hz. Rendering interpolates the camera and skin palettes between ticks, so the frame rate is whatever the hardware allows (--fps N caps it). The original ran at 60 Hz with a 30 Hz fallback; in PCSX2 98.8 % of measured updates were at 60 Hz.
Mouse look. Raw mouse deltas go straight into yaw and pitch (0.0025 rad per count), with no dead zone, curve or ramp. There is no manual-aim box with a mouse. Auto-aim is the Auto Aim profile option (on by default, as in the game). The wheel switches weapons (G for gadgets) and zooms while you aim a zoomable weapon.
Online multiplayer. The PS2 game is four-pad couch play with no online mode. The port adds Host Online and Join Online pages over a UDP lockstep session in nf-net, with acks, retransmit, input delay and a per-tick state hash for desync detection. A match takes up to 16 participants, humans and bots together. To join a match you can:

type a 4-character code;
pick it from the public list a small lobby service keeps;
or enter the host's IP:port.

The lobby service only introduces the players; the match itself runs between the players' own machines. UPnP / NAT-PMP port mapping, STUN and hole punching are built in.
Widescreen and window size. Gameplay fills the window's aspect; cut-scenes are pillar-boxed at the game's 4:3. The window can be any size.
Keyboard and mouse menus. Menu rows are hit-tested where they are drawn, and the hint bars name keyboard keys instead of PlayStation buttons.
Dev tools in a separate window. With --dev, a native "Nightfire dev" window opens beside the game and the game keeps running. It offers weapon and gadget lists, grenades, ammo and health, NPC spawning, teleport, level selection, toggles and screenshots. In the game window, F1 is an AI overlay and F2 brings the dev window forward.

Rapid fire. An optional rapid-fire toggle, off by default (--rapid-fire, or in the dev window).

Smaller things.

A "Keep shell casings" option; the default is the game's own lifetime.
Optional gamepad support through gilrs (a build feature, off by default), running the game's own mapping and curves.
A launcher that updates itself from this repository's GitHub releases.

The port's images in this README were rendered by the port at 1280x720. The left half of the comparison clip further down is a PCSX2 capture of the original game.
Performance

Measured on one PC (Ryzen 9 7900X, RTX 4090, Windows 10) on 2026-10-21 at the start of The Exchange (level 07000005).

Frame limiter off: PCSX2 2.8.2 (Vulkan, 4x internal resolution) reaches 110 fps by its own overlay. The port reaches 1,220 fps by its frame log (median of three 10-second runs at a 2543x1400 window, the largest the desktop allows; 1,209 at 1920x1080, 1,210 at 1280x720).
240 Hz monitor with vsync: the port holds 240 fps on 33 % of one core. PCSX2 cannot reach 240 at all, and at the game's own 60 fps it uses 81 % of a core.

The two frame rates do not mean the same thing. PCSX2's is emulation throughput: at its "183 %" readout the whole game, logic included, runs 1.83x fast. The port keeps the game logic at a fixed 60 Hz and renders as many interpolated frames as the hardware allows, so 1,220 fps is rendered frames at normal game speed. PCSX2 is also drawing a 4x upscale of the PS2's ~512x448 frame, where the port renders natively at the window size.
Frame time per level (2026-10-21)
Average frame time at each on-foot story level's start view, release build, a real 1920x1080 window, limiter off (one 10-second run per level after 20 seconds of warm-up). 240 Hz needs 4.17 ms or less.

It is fixed, and the per-frame cost test (frame_cost_live) now also budgets the render encode on every single-player archive.
Roadmap

The on-foot side follows the plan's rule of porting one subsystem whole at a time: core loop, player, weapons, guards (268 functions), objects and levels, then rendering. A subsystem is done when every function in its port-map is ported or justified and the recorded PCSX2 traces match.
Multiplayer has the match core, local and online games, and bots in matches. Split screen is not implemented. The remaining bot behaviours, radar, panes and weapon sets are still open.
The driving engine has its own phased plan (docs/atlas/driving.md) and is the furthest out. A later polish phase lists FOV, a rebinding UI, rumble and accessibility.
Long-term guardrails from the plan:

determinism: a shared bit-exact RNG and a fixed 60 Hz tick;
players kept as a list, so co-op is possible later;
the game's own multiplayer first;
the port's data structures as a future mod format.

Building and running
Windows builds are published on this repository's Releases page: a single NightfirePort.exe (the launcher, which updates itself). You need your own NTSC-U disc image (v1.00).
To build from source you need a Rust toolchain:
cargo run --release --offline -p nf-view --features movies -- "<path to iso>" 07000005

nf-view [<iso>] <level> [--all] [--seq K] [--frame F] [--fire] [--reinforcements] [--shot out.png ...]. Without <iso> the path comes from NF_ISO. Without a level, the game boots to its title screen. --shot renders one 1280x720 frame headless and exits.

Optional cargo features:

gamepad: gilrs, off by default.
movies: the MPEG-2 decoder for the disc's videos. It is off by default to keep plain builds light, but without it no movie plays, so build with --features movies to play the game as shipped.

Tests read the disc only when NF_ISO is set and are silent (NF_SILENT=1):
NF_ISO="<path to iso>" cargo test --offline --release -- --test-threads=1

The workspace has six crates:

nf-formats: on-disc format readers.
nf-game: the fixed-tick simulation ported from ACTION.ELF, plus the driving model code.
nf-view: window, renderer, menus and launcher; the playable app.
nf-audio: SPU voices mixed in software, played through cpal.
nf-net: the UDP lockstep session, join codes and the lobby client.
nf-extract: a CLI for inspecting your disc: info, manifest, elfs, files-extract, tex-export, bigf-extract, weapon-matrix, ... (57 commands).

That is about 370,000 lines of Rust in total.
Legal
This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to the rights holders of 007: Nightfire or James Bond, nor with the original game's developers or publisher. You must own the game and supply your own disc image.
Apart from the screenshots and clips on this page, the repository contains no game data. Golden test snapshots hold numbers, hashes and identifiers only. The research material (decompiles, ELFs, emulator snapshots) lives in a git-ignored directory and is never uploaded.
Code reused from the rerac project (a Rust port of Ratchet & Clank 1, which served as the model for this one) is under its ISC licence; see THIRD_PARTY_RERAC_LICENSE.txt. Code ported from OpenGOAL (the Jak & Daxter decompilation project; its SPU ADPCM decoder variant lives in crates/nf-formats/src/vag.rs) keeps its ISC licence notice in THIRD_PARTY_OPENGOAL_LICENSE.txt.
How the work is verified
Visual work is checked against the real game side by side: the same scene rendered by the port and captured from PCSX2 at the same spot and timing.

Every claim in the docs carries an evidence tag:

[M] from the machine code;
[D] from the disc data;
[L] from a live PCSX2 snapshot;
[S] suggested (not yet backed by evidence).

Behaviour is checked against the original by recording PCSX2 calls and traces and comparing numbers, not images, so no game data ends up in the tests. The verification ledger lists what is proven bit-exact.
The test suite has about 4,100 #[test] functions across 989 integration test files. The last full run on master (2026-10-31) was 3,747 passed, 1 failed (a frame-timing test that passed when re-run on its own), 269 ignored.

Walkthroughs: 26 walk_* and 25 walkreal_* test files drive the story levels headless; the walkreal_* ones drive Bond through the real input path.
Placements and archives: every placement on all 27 story levels is checked to resolve, and all 27 on-foot archives run 600 ticks without a panic.
Performance: per-frame cost budgets are part of the same suite.

Open work is tracked in a gaps list (docs/GAPS.md: 49 items, 23 still open or partly open) and open questions in docs/UNKNOWNS.md (48: 21 open, 7 partly answered).

gh-1445853209.title: GitHub - VibePorter/Lazarus: Mass Effect 2 (Xbox 360, Title Update 2) statically recompiled for the PC & Nintendo Switch, with a native deko3d renderer. Bring your own game files.
gh-1445853209.content:
BioWare's Mass Effect 2 (Xbox 360, Title Update 2), statically recompiled for the Nintendo Switch

What it is · Known issues · Highlights · What we fixed ·
Screenshots · Editions · Install ·
Build · Controls · FAQ ·
Troubleshooting · Roadmap · Story · Docs ·
Credits

ImportantNo game files are included, and none may ever be added. Lazarus is made from your own Xbox 360 copy of
Mass Effect 2 and its Title Update 2. The code generated from the game, the converted shaders and the finished
NRO are all built on your computer from your files.

🧬 What it is
The Lazarus Project brought Shepard back. This one does the same for the Xbox 360 version of Mass Effect 2:

Static recompilation. The game's PowerPC program (default.xex + the TU2 patch) is translated to C++ by the
ReXGlue code generator and compiled for the Switch's ARM CPU. No emulator
runs at play time: the Xbox 360 kernel, file system, audio (XMA) and input are provided by the SDK's runtime.
A Direct3D-level renderer on deko3d. Instead of emulating the Xenos GPU, Renut hooks the game's own Direct3D
calls (draws, shaders, render targets, resolves) and replays them through plume
on deko3d, the Switch's native graphics API. The game's ~38,700 shaders are converted ahead of time
(Xenos microcode → SPIR-V → GLSL → DKSH).
Game-specific work on top: Umbra occlusion answers, size-based culling, native replacements for hot functions,
PGO builds, Switch button glyphs, gyro aiming, a working ME1 character import and more (see below).

It runs on a real Switch and in Ryujinx. It is a work in progress: read known issues before
you start a long playthrough.
🚧 Known issues at a glance
Warning

Heavy hubs and big fights are not a locked 30. Entering the location for the first time, heavy sceanes like Kasumi's party,
action-packed combat (many enemies, powers and effects at once) can drop into the high teens or low 20s fps:
the game's own render thread is the limit there, and long heavy stretches can bring short audio dropouts. For now,
the fix is to overclock the console above the clocks the profiles were tuned for.
You build it yourself, for Title Update 2 only. There is no download; the NRO and shader files are made from
your own discs and TU2 package, and the build chain has not yet been re-run from a fresh clone.
Some picture features are off: the game's 2x MSAA and the lens flares, and size culling can make distant lights
pop in.
No online, no restart: the Cerberus Network and store do not exist, and where the Xbox would restart the game
(signing out, some import failures) the port stays where it is.

The full list: docs/known-issues.md.

⚡ Highlights

Feature
What it does

🎨

The game's Direct3D calls drawn by deko3d: no GPU emulation, no Vulkan driver in the NRO

👁️

✂️

🔥

🎮

🎯

Hold ZL and aim with motion; options rows in Options → Controller

🧬

Pick an ME1 save (PC .MassEffectSave or Xbox save) from the game's own load screen: no restart

📊 Measured
Real Switch, fidelity profile at 540p, CPU 1785 / GPU 998 MHz (logs of 2026-11-03): gameplay median 29.4 fps,
48 % of the 10-second windows at 30. The heaviest hubs (Omega, Kasumi's loyalty party) still drop into the high teens
or low 20s: there the game's own render thread is the limit. The performance profile is tuned for stock clocks
(handheld CPU 1020 / GPU 460.8 MHz). How to measure your own runs: docs/measuring.md.

📦 Install
The full guide, with the SD card layout, Ryujinx and the forwarder, is docs/install.md. In short:

Build the NRO and its shader files from your game (building). There are no
prebuilt downloads: every file that comes from the game has to be made from your own copy.
Copy the game (both discs merged, plus TU2) and the build to sdmc:/switch/me2-deko/.
Pick a settings profile from config/profiles and copy it as me2.toml.
Start me2_opt.nro with full memory (hold R while starting a game), or install the
NSP forwarder, which also unlocks the 4th CPU core and Switch user saves.

sdmc:/switch/me2-deko/
├── me2_opt.nro ← tools/nx/build_switch.sh
├── me2.toml ← config/profiles/<en|ru>/<performance|fidelity>/me2.toml
├── deko3d_glsl.bin ← the game's shaders (from your game)
├── deko3d_shaders.bin (+ .idx) ← precompiled shader variants (from your game)
├── game/ ← your game: both discs merged, TU2's default.xexp and update/*.tlk
├── me2/ ← DLC and user data
└── ME1/ ← (optional) ME1 saves to import

🛠️ Building from source
The step-by-step guide is docs/building.md. The outline:
# 0. Source and the third-party libraries the repository does not carry
git clone https://github.com/VibePorter/Lazarus.git && cd Lazarus
python tools/fetch_thirdparty.py # SDK libraries (ReXGlue v0.10.0 and its submodules)
python tools/fetch_app_thirdparty.py # plume / XenosRecomp submodules (Vulkan headers, DXC, zstd, ...)

# 1. Windows: your game into assets/game_root (+ TU2's default.xexp), the code generator, the C++ of the game
powershell -File tools\codegen.ps1 -Flavor optimised

# 2. Windows: the game's shaders (Xenos -> SPIR-V -> GLSL / DKSH), see docs/building.md "Shaders"

# 3. WSL / Linux: the Switch NRO (devkitA64)
sudo bash tools/nx/setup_wsl.sh
SHADER_CACHE_CPP=... GLSL_DIR=... DKSH_DIR=... bash tools/nx/build_switch.sh

❓ FAQ

Where is the download?
There is none, and there will not be one with game content in it. The NRO contains code translated from the game,
and the shader files are made from the game's shaders, so you build both from your own copy
(docs/building.md).

Does it run on an unmodified Switch?
No. It is homebrew: you need a console running Atmosphère. The NSP forwarder also needs sigpatches.

Can I use the PC, PS3 or Legendary Edition files?
No. Lazarus is the Xbox 360 program, and it needs the Xbox 360 discs and Title Update 2. Other versions have
different program code and data formats.

Can I continue my Xbox 360 or PC save?
Yes. An Xbox 360 save is an STFS package: extract it with python tools/stfs_extract.py <package> <folder>, and the
.xbsav inside works as it is. PC saves (.pcsav) convert with
python tools/me2_save_convert.py <in.pcsav> <out.xbsav>, which needs Gibbed's save editor sources in tools/ext
(git clone https://github.com/gibbed/Gibbed.MassEffect2 tools/ext/Gibbed.MassEffect2). Put the .xbsav in a career
folder under me2/<profile>/454108CE/00000001/ (the game creates it at its first save). With the
forwarder the saves live in the Switch user's save data instead.

Can I bring my Mass Effect 1 Shepard?
Yes, from a PC or Xbox 360 ME1 save: docs/me1-import.md.

Switch Lite / OLED / docked?
Any Switch that runs Atmosphère should work; handheld and docked are both supported, docked at a higher resolution
(see docs/configuration.md).
The profiles are tuned for stock clocks (performance) or an overclocked console (fidelity).

Should I play in Ryujinx?
Ryujinx is for testing and debugging. It runs the port, but the console is the target and the profiles are tuned for
it. Ryujinx needs two extra settings (docs/install.md).

📜 How it came back to life
About two weeks from the first NRO to the version in this repository. The full story:
docs/timeline.md.

Before: ME2's Xbox 360 program recompiled for Windows first; by 24 October it booted, saved and loaded DLC.
24 Oct: the first Switch NRO, on masseffect-nx's Vulkan (NVK) route: main menu on a real Switch, then in game at
13-15 fps, and a hang in Eden. That evening: mgr-nx-deko shows a renderer on deko3d without a Vulkan driver.
25 Oct: the switch to deko3d. First picture from Renut on the PC in the afternoon, the title screen in Ryujinx
in the evening, running on a real Switch that night (12-15 fps).
26-27 Oct: optimised codegen, Cinnamon's ideas and the 4th CPU core: heavy scenes 13-16 → 26-30 fps. Picture
fixes, FXAA + FSR, PGO, Switch glyphs, real occlusion queries.
28-31 Oct: Umbra answered without waiting (Omega 16 → 27 fps), the vanishing particles fixed, the Russian edition.
1-2 Nov: UE3's render thread in the cross-hairs; naruto-nx ports and size culling; the ME1 import worked out.
3 Nov: median 29.4 fps in gameplay (540p, overclocked); the port moves to Title Update 2; gyro aiming.
4 Nov: subtitle size, the import crash fixed, and the port becomes Lazarus.
5-7 Nov: a CPU occlusion rasterizer and a native visibility pass in place of Umbra's traversal, the lighting
blobs on characters fixed, HD button icons, the asset pack split into 3 GB parts.
14 Nov: Legendary Edition ME1 saves for the import, saves overwritten properly, me2_fps_limit, a third batch
of renderer fixes, and the room that vanished in Lair of the Shadow Broker's first shot (the rasterizer's near
plane).

18rhdkp.title: From 2D to 3D and back to 2D again, the original platforming classic Super Meat Boy returns with a slick remaster complete with new levels and too many old saws
18rhdkp.content:
That's a plus, again

Image credit: Team Meat

Earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff."

Watch on YouTube

If the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as big a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.

1vurw6c.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
1vurw6c.content:
Last month, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. More recently, privacy-focused AI assistant Ollie announced its shutdown a few weeks ago.

Aside from Character.ai and Ollie, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence, about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand.

The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry.

OpenAI has taken several stumbles

Image Credits:SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg / Getty Images

Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “super app.” On July 9, OpenAI updated the app to combine several experiences, including separate “Chat,” “Codex,” and “Work” modes, while renaming the traditional, familiar version “ChatGPT Classic.”

The redesign quickly drew criticism from users who found the new interface confusing and cluttered, and OpenAI rolled back the change soon after, bringing the familiar ChatGPT interface back.

That wasn’t OpenAI’s only attempt to pull everything under one roof. The company has also shut down several stand-alone apps and folded their features directly into ChatGPT — a strategy that’s worked out better than the redesign did. ChatGPT Atlas, a stand-alone AI-powered web browser, lasted less than a year before being discontinued on August 9, with its most useful features absorbed into ChatGPT.

The company did the same thing with Operator, an AI agent that could browse the web and complete tasks on a user’s behalf, and OpenAI has increasingly built image generation directly into ChatGPT, shrinking the role of DALL-E as its own separate destination for creating images.

We also can’t forget its video-sharing platform, Sora, which struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026.

Apple’s Siri AI

Image Credits:Artur Widak/NurPhoto / Getty Images

When Apple unveiled Apple Intelligence in 2024, an improved Siri was one of the highlighted features. The pitch promised a Siri that could understand context, know what was happening across apps, and get tasks done effectively.

However, Apple repeatedly pushed back the release of the new Siri, citing various reasons like engineering issues and bugs. This delay eventually contributed to a $250 million settlement over claims regarding how Apple marketed the AI capabilities of the iPhone 16.

Siri AI finally appeared in the iOS 27 beta this past July, with the new AI-powered version rolling out to English-language users first this month; support for other languages is expected to follow.

Character.ai

Image Credits:Character.AI

Founded in 2021 by former Google researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, Character.ai was a consumer AI app that let people chat with customizable bots, many of them modeled on celebrities and fictional characters. It raised $150 million at a $1 billion valuation in 2023. Then, the next year, Google paid a reported $2.7 billion to license its technology and bring its founders back into its orbit, leaving the startup to carry on without them.

Character.ai has run into a lot of trouble over the years. Families have sued, alleging the chatbots contributed to teen suicides and self-harm, and Disney sent a cease-and-desist letter over unauthorized use of its characters. Character.ai barred under-18 users from open-ended chats late last year and agreed to settle several of the suits, along with Google, in early 2026.

But it wasn’t enough. The company filed for bankruptcy in early October, citing legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds. In an ironic twist, Disney is now the opening bidder, offering $20 million for a license to some of its intellectual property. The app is still running during the process, and the sale is expected to wrap up by late November or early December.

Relay

Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August 2026.

The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product.

Ollie

Image Credits:Ollie

Ollie launched in June 2026 as one of the first mainstream apps to achieve SOC 2, a privacy compliance standard.

Similar to the other family-focused agents, the idea behind Ollie was that families already have the information they need, but it lives across school messages, calendars, task lists, and group chats. Ollie aimed to bring those pieces together and keep them in sync. It kept track of calendars, emails, reminders, tasks, and other household details, then delivered relevant information to users through text. 

However, the app faced a very common challenge: keeping up with heavyweights like Muse and Instinct. Co-founder and CEO Bill Lennon revealed the app would shut down on November 6, citing difficulties like being unable to stand out, failing to grow, and not raising enough capital.

Microsoft’s Recall

Announced at its 2024 Build developer conference, Microsoft’s Recall feature was pitched as an AI-powered “photographic memory” for Windows PCs, periodically taking screenshots of what a user was doing so they could later search back through their own digital history.

Predictably, the announcement triggered an immediate backlash over privacy and security. Critics argued that Recall could create a searchable archive of highly sensitive information, including passwords, private messages, financial details, and other activity. Microsoft delayed the feature for nearly a year, giving the company time to rethink its security and privacy protections. 

Even after a redesign, the controversy hasn’t gone away. A cybersecurity researcher recently built a tool that could extract and display data that Recall had captured, reviving questions about whether Microsoft has actually fixed the underlying problem.

Notion Mail

Image Credits:Notion

Notion Mail launched in April 2025 as an AI-focused email product designed to help users organize and automate their inboxes. However, the company noticed its users were using separate AI agents to handle their email inboxes instead. As a result, Notion Mail is scheduled to shut down on September 22.

Humane AI Pin

Image Credits:Brian Heater

The Humane AI Pin is probably one of the most well-known failures in AI hardware. Designed to provide AI features through a wearable device rather than a traditional smartphone, Humane raised $230 million from investors and garnered significant attention. 

But the product struggled mightily with performance, and the situation worsened when Humane warned customers to stop using its charging case because of a potential battery fire risk. Humane then shut down its AI Pin business in February 2025, with most of the company’s assets acquired by HP for $116 million.

Rabbit R1

Image Credits:Rabbit

The Rabbit R1 was another heavily hyped AI device. Unveiled at CES in January 2024, the AI companion was designed to perform tasks on behalf of its owner. Rabbit said it had sold 100,000 units shortly after launch.

However, strong initial sales didn’t mean it was a strong product. Early reviews described the device as unfinished, with unreliable performance and a limited number of useful integrations.

The company hasn’t given up, though. It has continued updating the R1, positioning it as a computer controller capable of performing agentic tasks. It also recently announced a new hardware project, dubbed “Project Cyberdeck,” aimed at creating a portable device built for vibe-coding.

Huxe

Image Credits:Huxe

Huxe was an AI audio app, built by former developers of Google’s NotebookLM, that turned written information into conversational, podcast-style audio.

The company shut down in May 2026, partly as larger platforms began offering similar experiences to large existing audiences. For instance, Spotify has been expanding its own AI-powered audio tools.

Yupp

Image Credits:Yupp

Yupp was an interesting AI product: a free playground that allowed users to compare responses from hundreds of AI models side by side. Users could also vote on responses and earn cryptocurrency through the platform.

At its peak, the platform let users test more than 800 models, including from companies such as OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. But according to its founders, Yupp never achieved strong enough product-market fit to survive. The platform shut down in March 2026. 

Figgs AI

Figgs AI operated from 2023 to 2024, letting users create and interact with customizable AI characters for role-play and storytelling. The platform reportedly drew more than 1 million users, but its developers said keeping the service free became too expensive to sustain, and they shut it down.

1pnoa0x.title: TikTok streamer arrested after allegedly killing wild opossum on livestream
1pnoa0x.content:
A man has been arrested on aggravated animal cruelty charges after an online video allegedly showing him killing a wild opossum circulated on social media.

Brandon Terry Honea, 34, is a taxidermist and TikTok livestreamer from Tennessee. On Wednesday, November 11, he was arrested and charged with aggravated animal cruelty.

The incident leading to his arrest was first reported to authorities on November 9, with the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office confirming it had received multiple calls concerning alleged animal abuse captured on video.

Honea claimed an opossum killed his chickens

According to TMZ, Honea, who was reportedly livestreaming, could be seen on video grabbing an opossum by its tail and repeatedly slamming it against a porch, while a woman could be heard pleading with him to stop.

Both the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office and the Fayetteville Police Department received calls about the killing, before referring it to the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (TWRA). The agency was called in because opossums are classified as Class 2 wildlife in the state.

Honea allegedly claimed that the animal had been killing his chickens, and that the TWRA had told him he had done nothing wrong.

However, the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office ultimately confirmed that its deputies had identified the individual involved and made the arrest following their own investigation.

The opossum could not be recovered, as footage provided to investigators showed that the animal had been killed.

Investigator Cheyenne Gonzalez told TMZ that the Sheriff’s Office couldn’t comment on the TWRA’s alleged comments to Honea, emphasizing that deputies independently investigated and brought the charges themselves.

The TWRA’s communications manager, Jason Harmon, told Voice For Us that the agency was reviewing the case and would coordinate with the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office and the District Attorney General.

The Sheriff’s Office has not released further details about the case, while the TWRA has declined to comment further due to the ongoing investigation.

1vmiemd.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
1vmiemd.content:
Cursor confirmed it suffered a security breach that let hackers distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through its marketplace after stealing credentials from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI.

The breach also let attackers access internal systems and steal customer data, including historical AI coding-agent traces containing unredacted credentials that were later used to compromise additional services.

The breach was disclosed in a new incident report published Friday, which explains how attackers distributed malicious versions of Anthropic's Claude Code extension through Cursor's marketplace on October 29.

The attack exposed up to 5,000 developers to malware that installed persistent SSH backdoors.

Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built on Microsoft's open-source Visual Studio Code (VS Code), allowing developers to write, modify, and debug software using AI assistants.

According to Cursor, the attack began when hackers obtained an access key stored on Fireworks AI, a third-party provider used for AI model training and inference.

The attackers used the exposed key to copy data from a read-only storage bucket Cursor used to share information with Fireworks.

This bucket contained historical AI coding-agent traces, mostly from 2025, collected from users who had not enabled Privacy Mode and whose data could be used for model training. Some of these traces contained unredacted API credentials, allowing the attackers to access additional Cursor systems.

Cursor says fewer than 0.05% of users had coding-agent traces exposed, while fewer than 0.01% of customers had API credentials compromised.

Using the exposed credentials, the hackers stole data from several of Cursor's software-as-a-service (SaaS) tools, including:

Archived, non-production Cursor source code repositories, some containing business contact information.
Limited customer support information and email conversations.
Product usage metrics and customer contact details.
Summaries of some AI coding-agent conversations.
Credentials that customers had previously shared with Cursor's support team.

Cursor says its monitoring systems detected the unauthorized activity, leading the company to revoke the Fireworks access key, rotate exposed credentials, and investigate additional unauthorized access.

As the investigation progressed, Cursor temporarily turned off some internal and product services as a precaution.

However, the attackers had already obtained a credential that allowed them to distribute extensions through Cursor's marketplace.

On October 29, the hackers used that credential to publish malicious copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on Cursor's VS Code extension marketplace.

"On October 29, using a stolen credential from the exposed data from our internal system, the attacker placed malicious, unauthorized copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension directly on the cache used to serve the Cursor VS Code extension marketplace," Cursor explained.

The attack did not compromise Anthropic's legitimate extension or Open VSX, the extension marketplace Cursor uses.

The malicious extensions, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, were available for approximately 11 hours before Cursor removed them.

As BleepingComputer previously reported, the attackers modified the legitimate Claude Code extension to execute malicious JavaScript that attempted to install persistent SSH backdoors on developers' computers.

The malware collected system information, installed an attacker-controlled SSH key, attempted to enable SSH access, and configured persistence mechanisms to maintain remote access.

However, security researchers found coding errors that likely prevented the backdoor from working on many Windows and macOS systems where SSH was not already enabled.

Cursor estimates that up to 5,000 users who requested affected extension versions during the exposure window may have received the malicious builds.

The company says its production infrastructure, official application releases, customer code repositories, and code and prompts belonging to users with Privacy Mode enabled were not affected.

Cursor says it has moved all inference traffic away from Fireworks, revoked and rotated exposed credentials, rebuilt its extension marketplace, and redeployed its production infrastructure as a precaution.

Customers who installed or updated to the affected Claude Code extension during the attack are advised to follow Cursor's remediation guidance.

Black October

The incident comes amid a wave of attacks targeting AI developer platforms that cybersecurity company Wiz has dubbed "Black October".

These attacks targeted development infrastructure to steal authentication credentials, especially those providing access to AI models.

Stolen credentials have been used for unauthorized AI inference, generating substantial charges for affected customers, with some incidents also linked to attempts at AI model distillation.

The attacks have affected numerous companies, including Railway, Northflank, Lightning AI, OpenCode, and Warp.

At Railway, attackers stole customer authentication secrets, which were later used to generate approximately $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges. OpenCode also reported exposed API keys and unauthorized AI usage.

Fireworks AI was also affected, disclosing multiple security breaches in October, including one involving exposed API keys and tokens and another in which attackers accessed development machines through a compromised third-party cloud provider.

The Fireworks incidents also affected other customers, including Notion, which recently disclosed that AI chat transcripts from a small number of workspaces were exposed.

1i0vy8t.title: Новый надежный кроссовер Honda появился в России с ценой дешевых «китайцев»
1i0vy8t.content: Кроссовер Honda Vezel, пожалуй, единственная модель, которую в Россию по параллельным схемам поставляют сразу из двух стран – Японии и Китая. Различить версии несложно: у японской руль справа, у китайской слева. Цены при заказе стартуют ориентировочно с 2,17 млн рублей.Honda VezelСамое доступное предложение обнаружилось во Владивостоке: праворульную машину в максимальной комплектации G с полным приводом готовы привезти за 2 170 000 рублей. В оснащение входят кожаный мульти-руль, обогревы лобового стекла, боковых зеркал и передних сидений, электронный стояночный тормоз, светодиодная оптика и литые диски.Леворульный вариант с передним приводом из Благовещенска оценили в 2 195 000 рублей. В Кемерово такой же заказ обойдется в 2 200 000, во Владивостоке – в 2 300 000, в Иркутске – в 2 500 000, а в Томске – в 2 539 000 рублей.Правда, суммы из объявлений почти никогда не становятся окончательными. Конечная цена складывается из курса валют на день сделки, фактических расходов на оформление документов и логистику, утильсбора, комиссии брокера и еще целого ряда обстоятельств.Honda VezelГотовые машины тоже попадаются. В Уссурийске праворульный полноприводный Vezel продают за 2 320 000 рублей, а леворульный переднеприводный экземпляр в Хабаровске выставлен за 2 330 000.Для ориентира: официально представленный в России Geely Coolray стоит минимум 2 774 990 рублей, Haval Jolion в двухпедальных версиях – от 2 499 000. Выходит, привезенный по альтернативной схеме кроссовер нередко оказывается дешевле машин, которые продаются у дилеров.В Красноярске за китайскую версию просят минимум 2 450 000 рублей, в Иркутске уже привезенный автомобиль с левым рулем обойдется не меньше чем в 2 520 000. Приобрести новый Vezel можно также в Находке, Ангарске, Чите, Екатеринбурге, Абакане, Улан-Удэ, Пензе и Благовещенске – там цены доходят до 2 900 000 рублей.Интерьер Honda VezelЛеворульные кроссоверы с китайского рынка оснащают 1,5-литровым атмосферным двигателем мощностью 118 сил, который работает в паре с вариатором. Привод у них, как правило, полный.У праворульных Vezel обычно передний привод, мотор того же объема выдает 124 силы, а трансмиссия – такой же вариатор.Кстати, ранее модель попала в рейтинг самых надежных автомобилей Китая по версии местного подразделения американского аналитического агентства J.D.
