18qwc8e.title: Large companies can still fall short on their climate commitments. Here's what must change
18qwc8e.byline: Rebekkah Markey-Towler, Bei Cui, Ella Vines
18qwc8e.content:
Credit: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain

International climate conferences like the COP31 climate summit, now in its second week, tend to focus on the role of individual countries.

Yet, more than half of global CO₂ emissions from fossil fuel and cement are produced by just 32 companies. Many have already set net-zero targets in response to mounting international pressure.
However, new research into Australian companies, from the Monash Business School Green Lab, calls the credibility of these targets into question—revealing a major gap between what some companies say and do regarding emissions.
Without stronger regulation, large companies will continue to be vague about how they will achieve their climate commitments.
Australia's corporate emitters
Our new study took a closer look at 16 of Australia's largest listed companies operating across the emissions-intensive metals, mining and energy sectors. This includes energy giants BHP and Woodside, both of which have recently made headlines for rolling back their climate commitments.
For each company, we reviewed publicly available information published between July 1, 2024, and June 30, 2025. Sources included annual reports, sustainability reports, climate reports, transition plans and sustainability data books.
We assessed companies' disclosures against a set of indicators to test the credibility of their net-zero targets and performance metrics, such as reported greenhouse gas emissions. We also examined their implementation measures, including electrification and energy efficiency improvements, and the financial resources allocated to these measures.
We focused on public information because it helps:

investors decide how to distribute their money
regulators evaluate how effective government policies are
community members hold companies to account for their climate action or lack thereof.

The gap between ambition and action
There's evidence that many companies have kept their net-zero targets in place despite political and economic challenges, such as the United States' second withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and the ongoing Middle East conflict.
However, our findings reveal a significant gap between companies' reported net-zero targets and the concrete actions they have publicly committed to take.
All companies in our sample have set public net-zero targets. Some have a transition plan—laying out the targets, actions and resources a company will use to reduce its emissions—and identify a broad set of measures to implement these targets.
Each of the 16 companies cited electrification and fuel switching—replacing fossil fuel-based systems with renewables—as implementation measures. Improving energy efficiency was also common across 15 of the 16 companies studied. For example, BlueScope Steel reported that upgrading industrial paint ovens at its Western Port facility in Victoria cut the company's annual emissions by about 18,000 tons.

All but two companies had supply chain decarbonization—the process of reducing or cutting carbon emissions produced at various stages of a supply chain—as a goal.
However, many companies published limited quantitative data showing whether these measures would actually reduce their emissions. For example, Fortescue's 2025 Climate Transition Plan described efficiency initiatives without offering clear emissions reduction figures. What's more, we found a major gap between companies' stated decarbonization commitments and the information they publicly disclosed about how they would pay for these efforts.
Of the 16 companies studied, 11 claimed to have allocated funds for decarbonization measures. However, only seven companies disclosed how they calculated climate-related costs or considered them in their investment decisions. Rio Tinto, for instance, reports it assessed proposed investments against criteria including their potential to reduce emissions and financial costs. Just five of the 16 companies conducted post-investment reviews or audits.
These discrepancies make it extremely difficult to know if company climate targets are contributing to corporate, national and global net-zero goals.
While all companies had room for improvement, some provided more detailed disclosures than others. Fortescue forecast spending US$700 million to US$900 million (A$1 billion to A$1.3 billion) on emissions reduction in 2025, but subsequently reported spending US$405 million (A$600 million). Disclosing both planned and actual expenditure offers insight into how companies are progressing, but doesn't necessarily show whether their investments are enough to meet their climate targets.

Disclosure is not enough
Australia's new mandatory climate disclosure system requires large Australian companies to provide climate-related financial information each year. They must submit this information alongside their annual reporting obligations, including greenhouse gas emissions and climate targets.
However, disclosure alone will not give companies enough incentive to realize their net-zero commitments.
Governments must also introduce stronger policies that require companies to reduce emissions and invest in cleaner technologies. Australia's Safeguard Mechanism, the main federal tool for cutting emissions from big polluters, is one such example.
Clearer international commitments can also help. Australia and other countries should support the development of a global roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels, proposed by Brazil at last year's COP30 summit. This could provide greater certainty about the direction of the global transition and encourage companies to invest in greener technologies.
Effective scrutiny by regulators, investors and the courts is also key to keeping companies accountable for their commitments.
For too long, large companies have failed to make good on their climate commitments. More specific and robust reporting requirements will go some way to fixing this. And by scrutinizing company claims, investors, researchers and the wider community can also help keep net zero within reach.

Who's behind this story?

gh-1450926019.title: GitHub - SamiEnazi/infamous2-port: inFAMOUS 2 (PS3) as a native PC program for Windows and Linux: Setup recompiles YOUR copy on your PC (static recompilation, Vulkan). No game files included.
gh-1450926019.content:
What this is
Setup translates the game's PS3 code into PC code on your machine, from your own copy, and compiles it. The
game then runs directly on your CPU, with its graphics drawn through Vulkan: native 1080p up to 4K, any
controller or keyboard and mouse, an in-game settings menu, mods, cheats, a save manager and trophies.

No game content is included, and none is downloaded. You need your own copy of the game. Builds of the
game (the .exe) are never shared, because they contain the game's code. Each player builds their own.

Install in 3 steps

Download Setup.exe from the latest release and put it in a folder on a local
drive, for example C:\Games\inFAMOUS2.
Run it and pick your game: its folder, a disc image (.iso) or a PSN package (.pkg). Use the button or
drop it on the window. Setup says which game it is before anything is downloaded.
Press Install, wait, press Play.

That's all. No RPCS3, no Git, no Python, no Visual Studio, no admin rights, and nothing is installed into Windows.
Setup downloads about 85 MB from GitHub (the port and its own tools) and 433 MB from Sony's servers (the game's
1.04 update and the PS3 system software, the same files a PS3 downloads), copies your game into the port's folder
and builds it once. On the test PC the whole install took 12 to 15 minutes.

Linux and the Steam Deck: see below. More detail on copies and keys: FAQ.
What's new in v0.6.2
A stability update.

Windows: no Visual C++ runtime needed. On a PC without it the game did not start ("MSVCP140.dll was not
found"). The game now carries what it needs.
Linux: the game's window opens on Wayland (#54, #44); Setup's folder
question no longer becomes the folder; and Setup stops, and says what to do, when the game would be built
without its shader translator and draw nothing (#61, #69).
Direct mouse: a fast flick turns the camera 1:1 (#59): the whole turn at once, nothing
after the mouse stops. And the Alt keys can be bound (#68).
Low-end PCs: the start notice names the 720p picture it chose (#73).

What's new in v0.6.1

Windows 10: Setup installs again. v0.6.0 stopped on Windows 10 with "unpacking llvm-22.1.8-slim-win-x64.7z
failed: tar.exe: LZMA codec is unsupported" (#62, #70): it used Windows'
own tar.exe, and only Windows 11's can read that file. Setup now unpacks its compiler with its own Python and
needs nothing from Windows for it. If v0.6.0 stopped there for you: get this Setup.exe and run it in the
same folder, or just press Try again.
DLC is picked up (#56, #48): Setup copies your DLC's unlock files
from RPCS3 when it has them, and files you put in the port's dlc folder are used at the next start
(FAQ).

What's new in v0.6.0
Install

One small Setup, one pick. About 85 MB from GitHub instead of 1.3 GB of build tools, and no Microsoft
license to accept.
No RPCS3 needed. The update and firmware come from Sony's servers.
PSN copies and encrypted disc images are supported, new in this version: a PSN copy with your .rap
license, an encrypted disc image with its disc key file.
A progress display that always moves: each long step says in plain words what it is, how far it is and
about how many minutes are left.
Fully portable. Your game is copied into the port's folder (about 9 GB), and settings, saves, mods and the
shader cache live there too. Copy the folder to another drive or PC and it plays.
Any folder name works: &, %, !, ', ( ), [ ], other alphabets, very long paths
(#34, #19, #41).

In the game

A new F2 menu over the live game: see below.
Sharper shadows: the sun's shadows are drawn at twice the PS3's resolution by default, with a 4x option.
MSAA 2x / 4x as an option. Off by default: it costs a lot of GPU time (4x: about 40% of the frame rate at
1080p on the test PC).
Mesh trimming is off by default: whole meshes are drawn, so nothing small goes missing.
Faster, most of all on small CPUs: Performance.

Linux

./setup.sh now works on distributions that keep their libraries in lib64 (Fedora, openSUSE), stops with a
clear message when glslang could not be built, and NixOS has its own environment file
(#64, the first community pull request, thanks to ANewJanuary).

Fixed

The digital (PSN) version's own folder is taken directly (#40).
16:9 on an ultrawide screen keeps its shape with black bars (#35); the wide picture no longer
flickers to 16:9 (#47).
The window can be resized, and F2 → Display → Capture-friendly window helps Lossless Scaling and OBS
(#51).
The game's first-start HDD install finishes properly (it was made again at every start).
AMD Radeon RX 7000 / 9000 with an Adrenalin driver older than 26.6.1: the game says so once.

Known limits of this version

AMD graphics cards keep the earlier, conservative graphics path: the new GPU-side optimisations are off
there until they are tested on AMD hardware. The CPU-side gains apply.
Linux: this version was built and run by us on one Linux PC only (Ubuntu 22.04, Radeon RX 550, RADV). Other
distributions and graphics cards: please report.
Setup.exe is not code-signed, so Windows or an antivirus may warn about it (FAQ).

Every version and its changes: Releases.
The F2 menu

Press F2 (or hold L3+R3) while you play:

The game stays visible behind a panel on the left.
One icon per page: Display, Graphics, Audio, Controls, HUD, Lighting, Effects, Mods, Update, Cheats, About.
Change page with L1 / R1, Q / E, or a click.
Presets on the Graphics page: Standard and Low-end PC. Change anything and it becomes Your mix.
One line of help per setting: what it does, what it costs, and whether it applies at once or after a restart.
A PS3 | YOURS compare line for the picture settings: drag it across the screen to see the PS3's picture
beside yours. Hold F3 for the whole PS3 look.
About: the version, the project page, and the people who support the port.
Two themes: Hero (blue) and Infamous (red).

Performance
Everything here was measured on one test PC on 17 Nov 2026: i5-13600K, RTX 2070 Super, 32 GB, Windows 11. The game
drew at 720p internal (the PS3's own resolution) on both sides, uncapped, with the build Setup makes.
Against RPCS3

Same PC, same save, same spot (the city dock right after loading): RPCS3 0.0.42 ran at 43 fps, this port at
147 fps: 3.4x. In the three lighter views from the same spot it is 3.6x to 4.9x (up to 251 fps against 51).
RPCS3 ran with its default settings (LLVM recompilers, Vulkan, 100% resolution scale), with its frame limit and
VSync off so it is uncapped too; the settings RPCS3's own database recommends for this game were slower (31 fps),
so they were not used. Medians of 3 runs.

On a smaller CPU

The same spot with the test PC held to fewer cores, average fps:

CPU limit
RPCS3 0.0.42

Whole CPU (20 threads)

On 4 cores / 4 threads the port went from 63 to 110 fps. RPCS3 is not playable there on this PC (6 fps).
These rows are the i5-13600K held to its fast cores by process affinity, not a real old 4-core PC. No real
low-end PC was measured: if you play on one, your numbers in an issue are welcome.
"Previous version" is v0.6.0's Setup with the engine of v0.5.7.
A browser and other programs were open during the runs (0.2 to 0.5 cores); the runs repeat within 1-3%.
The average is higher everywhere, but the slowest 1% of frames at the whole CPU is not better than before (84
fps against 95), so this version does not claim to be smoother.

At native 1080p with the default picture settings, where the graphics card does more of the work, v0.6.0 is 9%
and 12% faster than the previous version in the two heaviest city views, and 2.5% to 19% in the opening fight.
Story videos and cutscenes run at 30 fps in both, as on the PS3.
What you get

Native 1080p and up: F2 → Graphics → Internal resolution: 720p / 1080p / 1440p / 4K, with SMAA, FXAA or
MSAA, FSR 1 upscaling and sharpening.
Any controller, plug and play: Xbox, DualShock 4, DualSense, Switch Pro, 8BitDo and every pad in the
community SDL_GameControllerDB. The button pictures follow what
you play with. Every button and key can be remapped in F2 → Controls.
Direct mouse aiming: the mouse turns the camera directly, as in a PC game, with separate sensitivity for
aiming.
Enhanced lighting: soft, sharper sun shadows, full-resolution ambient occlusion, smooth light gradients.
F3 flips to the original PS3 look.
HD fire, smoke and effects: drawn at full resolution instead of the PS3's 512×288, plus texture packs.
Widescreen: 21:9, 32:9 and 16:10. You see more at the sides, nothing is stretched.
Cheats (F2 → Cheats): invincibility, infinite energy, super jump, karma rank, unlock all powers, one-hit
kills, longer glide, black lightning, saved spots (F7) and more.
Mods: see below.
Save manager: every save with its picture, mission, completion and date; New Save Data, overwrite, delete.
Trophies: the game's 52 trophies unlock as on a PS3, and Playnite and RecompLauncher can read them.
Languages: F2 → Audio → Language picks voice and text separately, from what your disc has.
Field of view slider, depth of field switch, a frame rate cap, an fps counter (F1).

Trophies in Playnite and RecompLauncher
The port keeps its trophies in game\gamedata\trophies\NPWR01730.json and also writes them the way RPCS3 does,
in game\gamedata\dev_hdd0\home\00000001\trophy\NPWR01730_00\, so trophy trackers made for RPCS3 can read them.
Playnite (Playnite Achievements or
SuccessStory). Both look for an emulator with RPCS3 in
its name, so the port gets one:

Library → Configure Emulators → Add: name it RPCS3 inFAMOUS 2 port, installation folder
<port folder>\game\gamedata, and one custom profile whose executable is <port folder>\Play inFAMOUS 2.cmd.
Add the game by hand: installation folder <port folder>\game\disc\PS3_GAME, and a play action of the Emulator
type with that emulator and profile.
Playnite Achievements: turn on its RPCS3 source. SuccessStory: Settings → RPCS3 → turn it on and add
<port folder>\game\gamedata\dev_hdd0\home\00000001 as a home user folder.
Start the game once (the folder is made then), then refresh the game's achievements.

Already set up for RPCS3? Add PS3_TROPHY_RPCS3_DIR=<your RPCS3 folder> to settings.ini and the port also
copies its unlocks into RPCS3's own trophy folder for the game. It never locks anything or moves a date later
there, and it keeps a copy of RPCS3's file once (TROPUSR.DAT.port-backup).
RecompLauncher: started from RecompLauncher, the port reports each trophy to
Recomp Achievements. A cheat that changes play makes the
session's later unlocks Casual. Picking or saving a spot and Black lightning don't.

What you need

Your copy of inFAMOUS 2. Confirmed by players: the Europe disc (BCES01143), the Turkey disc (BCES01229) and
the US disc (BCUS98125), and the digital (PSN) version 01.03 (NPUA80638 / NPEA00318). In one of these forms:

the game's folder (the one that holds PS3_GAME, or the PSN version's own folder)
a disc image (.iso)
a PSN package (.pkg)

A PC with: Windows 10/11 64-bit (or Linux), a CPU with AVX2 (Intel 4th gen / AMD
Ryzen or newer), a Vulkan graphics card, 16 GB RAM, about 16 GB free disk space on a local drive (not a network
drive).
Internet for the install: about 85 MB from GitHub and 433 MB from Sony.

Tested PCs: the test PC above at 1080p to 4K; players on Windows 10 and 11 up to an RTX 5070 at 1440p; Linux on
Ubuntu 22.04 with a Radeon RX 550 (RADV), and a player's Steam Deck (#24).
Linux and Steam Deck
The port builds and runs natively on Linux, with no Wine or Proton. There is no Setup.exe on Linux: ./setup.sh
does the same job, and needs no RPCS3 either.
Download inFAMOUS2-port-v…-Linux-x64.zip from the latest release, unpack it and run
./setup.sh. The first time it asks for your game folder, gets the update and firmware from Sony's servers,
copies the game into the port's folder, builds it, then starts it. After that, ./setup.sh just plays. Or from git:
git clone https://github.com/SamiEnazi/infamous2-port
cd infamous2-port
./setup.sh # or: ./setup.sh --disc <your game folder>

tools/setup.sh lists what it needs from your distribution (a C/C++ toolchain, python3 with venv, the Vulkan
loader, SDL2). Unlike Windows, it downloads its build tools (LLVM 22.1.8, CMake / Ninja when the system has none)
and builds the engine itself: there are no prebuilt Linux tools yet.
Fedora, openSUSE and other lib64 distributions work since v0.6.0 (#64).
NixOS: build and play inside the FHS environment in tools/nixos/fhs-env.nix
(the commands are at the top of that file). Tested by its author on NixOS 26.05 with a Radeon 780M.
Steam Deck: a player built it inside an Ubuntu Distrobox container in Desktop Mode and plays it in Game Mode
(#24).
v0.6.0 on Linux was built and run by us on Ubuntu 22.04 with a Radeon RX 550 (RADV): it installs, starts and
plays there (slowly: that card is the limit). No Linux frame rate is claimed. Please report how it runs on
your distribution and GPU.

Updates

When the game starts it asks GitHub whether a new version is out (in the background, at most every 6 hours;
offline it just starts). F2 → Update shows what's new and installs it. Your saves, settings, mods and
controls are kept, and the saves are copied to saves-backup\ first.
An update rebuilds only what changed, so it takes minutes.
From v0.5.x: F2 → Update (or Setup.exe on your folder) moves the install to the new layout. It deletes the
old 2 GB of build tools and copies your game folder into the port's folder (it asks once and shows the size;
your folder is not changed).
F2 → Update → Check for updates automatically turns the check off, and with it the supporters list of the
About page. Nothing about you or your PC is sent.
A copy installed by RecompLauncher is updated by RecompLauncher.

Playing
Start with Play inFAMOUS 2.cmd or the desktop shortcut. For Steam, Playnite and other launchers, add
work\port\build\Infamous2Recomp.exe from the port's folder; Steam Input and the Steam overlay work.

Key
Action

F1
fps counter

F2 (or hold L3+R3)
the settings menu

F3
your picture vs the original PS3 look

F7
go to your saved spot

F9
mark a moment in the session log (a stutter, a glitch)

Alt+Enter
fullscreen

Keyboard and mouse: WASD to move, mouse for the camera, right button to aim, left button to shoot,
Space = ✕, Shift = ○, F = □, Q = △. Remap anything in F2 → Controls → Buttons and keys.
Mods
The community's inFAMOUS 2 mods made for tiffsomniac's inFAMOUS Mod Manager work as they are (whole files,
texture patches, xpps patches, and mods with options).

F2 → Mods → Add a mod from a zip takes the zips in your Downloads folder (only mod files are taken out,
never a program), or unzip a mod into the mods folder yourself (mods\<mod>\mod.json).
No Unlocker and nothing to install: your game files are never changed.
Turn each mod on or off and pick its options in F2 → Mods, then Restart to apply.
When two mods change the same file, Use this one instead picks the winner.

How it works and the mod format: engine/docs/MODS.md.
FAQ
Do I need RPCS3?
No. Since v0.6.0 Setup gets the game's update and the PS3 system software from Sony's servers itself. If RPCS3 is on
your PC and already has them, Setup copies them from there instead, and that is all it is used for.
I have the PSN (digital) version.
Pick its folder (NPUA80638 / NPEA00318) or its .pkg. It is unlocked with your own license, the .rap file:
put <CONTENT_ID>.rap beside the game and it is found by itself, otherwise Setup asks for it. No license is
shipped with the port. PSN support is new in this version and was made without a real PSN copy on the test PC, so
if Setup stops, please report it with Setup's log (Details → Copy log).
My disc image (.iso) is encrypted.
A decrypted image is read directly. An encrypted one (a raw copy of the disc) needs its disc key, a .dkey or
.ird file: put it beside the image with the same name (game.iso + game.dkey), otherwise Setup asks for it. A
3K3Y image carries its key. No key is shipped with the port. New in this version.
Windows or my antivirus warns about Setup.exe.
Setup.exe is not code-signed, because signing a program costs money. So Windows SmartScreen or an antivirus may
warn about it, as they can for any new, unsigned file. On the Windows message, click More info, then Run
anyway. The source is open (tools/setup_exe/ in this repository), and here is the VirusTotal scan of this
release's Setup.exe: https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/756d6f24fa0eba885f12a8d5993db466578f3189bf7674d09b9aae9372f5e233
Does DLC work?
Yes, when its unlock files are in the port's folder. inFAMOUS 2's DLC (the extra skins, amps and powers) is a set
of small unlock files, dev_hdd0\game\<your game's ID>\USRDIR\dlc\ulf\unlock_*.edat; the content itself is
already in the game. A game copy that carries them (a PSN folder with the DLC installed) brings them along. From
v0.6.1 Setup also copies them from RPCS3 when it is on your PC and has the DLC installed, on install and on every
update (added DLC to RPCS3 later? run Setup again). And there is a dlc folder in the port's folder: put the
.edat files there and they are picked up the next time the game starts. The DLC must be for the same version
(region) of the game as your copy. DLC that needs a license (.rap) is not supported yet.
Where are my saves and settings?
All in the port's folder. Saves: game\gamedata\dev_hdd0\home\00000001\savedata, backed up to saves-backup\
before every session. Settings: settings.ini, mods.ini, spots.ini, and your controls in input.toml.
Can I move the folder?
Yes. Move or copy the whole port folder to another drive or PC and start Play inFAMOUS 2.cmd. The desktop
shortcut is made again by itself.
How do I uninstall?
Delete the port's folder and the desktop shortcut (copy your saves out first). Nothing was installed into Windows.
Your original game is never touched. Only if you used a version before v0.6.0: also delete
%APPDATA%\inFAMOUS2-port and %LOCALAPPDATA%\inFAMOUS2-port.
The game looks or runs wrong.
Please open an issue and attach the newest play\<date-time> folder: it holds the frame times,
your F9 marks and every long frame with what the game was doing.
Contributing

Bug reports with the session's play\<date-time> folder are the most useful thing.
Test reports are wanted for: AMD graphics cards, Linux distributions, a real PSN copy, an encrypted disc
image, and old or small CPUs.
Pull requests are welcome and are reviewed by the owner before they are merged. The first one,
#64, is in v0.6.0.
Never post game files, keys, licenses or builds of the game.

Without Setup.exe (git)
git clone https://github.com/SamiEnazi/infamous2-port

Then run Setup.cmd, or from PowerShell:
tools\setup_build.ps1 -Source <your game folder, .iso or .pkg> [-Rpcs3 <your RPCS3 folder>] -Cleanup

Updating later is the same (git pull first). -Cleanup keeps the tools and build files, so only what changed
is built again. -NoBuildCache deletes them too.

Your own decryption tool (advanced)
Setup hands the game's 1.04 EBOOT.BIN and three firmware modules to a decryptor, by default ps3tool
(tools/ps3tool.py), and checks that what comes back is a decrypted program. To use another tool, put a line
like this in config.local.json in the port's folder:
"decryptor": "\"C:\\Tools\\mydecrypt.exe\" \"{in}\" \"{out}\""

{in} is the encrypted file and {out} where the decrypted one must go.

Supporters
The port is free. If you'd like to support the work, you can here: paypal.me/samiEnazi.
Supporters and contributors are listed in the game, in F2 → About.
Contributors: ANewJanuary (Linux setup, #64).
How it works

ps3recomp translates the game's PowerPC (PPU) and SPU code, and
three PS3 firmware modules from your download of the PS3 system software, into C/C++. The small clang + lld
compiler Setup brings then compiles it on your PC.
The engine is prebuilt: it is a release asset with no game code in it.

vol3hf.title: Joseph Zada Spent a Month Watching “Everything Woody Harrelson Has Ever Done” to Prepare for ‘Hunger Games’ Role
vol3hf.content:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took over New York City on Monday, bringing together casts old and new.

Original franchise stars Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, Woody Harrelson and Elizabeth Banks walked the carpet alongside Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes stars Rachel Zegler and Tom Blyth, along with newcomers Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Elle Fanning, Glenn Close, Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin and Maya Hawke.

Sunrise on the Reaping follows the 50th edition of the Games and is centered on a 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy who is portrayed by Harrelson in the central films. Zada takes on the younger version of Haymitch, and explained to The Hollywood Reporter how much Harrelson and his signature mannerisms impacted his own performance.

“It was kind of like a base layer; I spent a month when all that I did was look at everything Woody has ever done,” Zada told The Hollywood Reporter, “and past that, it was just up to me to bring myself to it because that’s what’s going to be interesting and what you want to see on the screen: the true light of yourself and bringing out all those aspects of me that align with the character.”

Ben Wang, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Kieran Culkin, Glenn Close, Ralph Fiennes, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace, Joseph Zada, Whitney Peak, Jesse Plemons and Maya Hawke at the New York premiere.

Mike Coppola/Getty Images

Sunrise on the Reaping, the fifth novel in Suzanne Collins’ bestselling series, is also known to be the darkest and most brutal, with Hawke emphasizing, “This story is devastating. The hope that you feel from this story is what you know the future is going to hold. The story itself is not overly hopeful; it’s gut-wrenching.”

As for how they navigated shaking off that material when leaving set, Zada admitted, “I didn’t even try, and I should have tried harder but I didn’t because I just didn’t want to. I wanted to give this every single inch of myself and push myself to the next level, and I’m so glad I did because it paid off and I’m so proud of the film.” Peak, whose character has a romance with Haymitch before he’s drawn into the Games, added, “Joe and I were definitely trying to keep it a little bit lighter between takes just so you can relieve your nervous system a little bit. It’s kind of tough to stay in that place for too long.”

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters on Friday.

19yk7cm.title: Lava flows studied for their carbon dioxide storage potential
19yk7cm.content:
Credit: Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar

As global warming intensifies, scientists are exploring ways to reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. One emerging approach being explored in environmental research is carbon capture and storage (CCS), which involves capturing CO₂ and storing it deep underground, away from the atmosphere. In this context, researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) have investigated ancient volcanic rocks in Maharashtra to assess their suitability for this purpose.

Basalt, the type of volcanic rock investigated in this study, is attracting interest for carbon capture and storage because it contains minerals that can react with CO₂ dissolved in water and convert it into stable minerals through a process known as mineralization. In Maharashtra, these rocks form part of the Deccan Traps, a vast expanse of volcanic rock in west-central India formed by successive lava flows around 65 million years ago. This landscape therefore offers a significant geological setting for investigating the potential of India's basalt formations for long-term CO₂ storage.
By studying Deccan basalt exposed at the surface, researchers can gain insights into similar formations buried underground, a method known as an outcrop-analog approach. However, these formations are not uniform. Individual lava flows can contain dense rock, fractures, pores and cavities and differ in mineral composition.
"These features influence how fluids move through the rock and interact with it. Understanding variations in internal architecture and the characteristics of individual lava flows is therefore important to identify which formations may be suitable sites for CO₂ to be pumped at a commercial scale," said corresponding author Pankaj Khanna, associate professor at IITGN's Department of Earth Sciences and Maritime Engineering.
Addressing this challenge, the researchers investigated seven basalt lava flows at Kumbharli Ghat in Maharashtra's Western Ghats. The findings are presented in the research paper titled "Characterising the Architecture of Deccan Basalt Flows for Subsurface CO₂ Storage: A 3D Digital Outcrop Analogue Approach," published in Marine Geoscience and Energy Resources.

The study marks the first use of drone-based photogrammetry to map individual lava flows in the Deccan basalt region. This technique combines photographs taken from different positions to reconstruct a three-dimensional model of the landscape.
Discussing its significance, Khanna added, "This is the first time such an outcrop-analog approach has been used to quantitatively assess Deccan basalt. By combining detailed mapping of individual lava flows, including their boundaries, thickness, and shape, with rock analysis, the study provides the first systematic data sets of their kind for the Deccan basalt region, documenting variations in their structure. These insights offer a way to investigate how such variations influence fluid movement underground, where these complex structures are difficult to explore using conventional approaches."
These findings are particularly relevant because basalt's ability to facilitate mineralization depends on several factors, including the availability of reactive minerals, the pathways through which fluids travel, and interactions between CO₂ and the surrounding rock. Given these complexities, individual basalt formations must be assessed on their own merits rather than treated as uniform underground reservoirs. Yet, only a handful of studies have investigated how these processes operate under subsurface conditions in Deccan basalt and what this means for its suitability for CO₂ storage.
Looking ahead, the data sets generated through this study can serve as a starting point for further investigations beyond the area examined.
"For us, an important outcome of this research is that these data sets can help other researchers better understand and model basalt formations underground. We hope this work will contribute to international efforts to explore geological CO₂ storage as part of the wider response to climate change and energy transition. Scientific collaborations across countries can help build the shared knowledge needed to work toward a more sustainable future," said lead author Debasmita Datta, a Ph.D. student in the Department of Earth Sciences.

More information
Debasmita Datta et al., Characterizing the architecture of Deccan basalt flows for subsurface CO2 storage: A 3D digital outcrop analogue approach, Marine Geoscience and Energy Resources (2026). DOI: 10.1016/j.marger.2026.207885

gh-1442537159.content:
TNRP (The Nimbus Recompilation Project, formerly The Nimbus Project) is a free fan project by Animorph Allocations.
Native ports of Dragon Ball Z: Budokai, Budokai 2 and Sagas (NTSC-U GameCube), Supersonic Warriors and Taiketsu (USA Game Boy Advance), Tenkaichi Tag Team, Shin Budokai and Shin Budokai – Another Road (USA PSP), Infinite World (USA PlayStation 2, SLUS-21842), Super Dragon Ball Z (USA PlayStation 2, SLUS-21442), Budokai Tenkaichi 3 (USA PlayStation 2, SLUS-21678), Ridge Racer 2 (Europe PlayStation Portable, UCES-00422), Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja 5 (Europe PlayStation 2, SLES-55605), and Mobile Suit Gundam: Gundam vs. Gundam NEXT PLUS (Japan PlayStation Portable, NPJH-50107) — fourteen games in one launcher on Linux, Windows and Android (four consoles: GameCube, GBA, PSP and PS2), with online play and full 3-platform crossplay across 16 global server instances. Ridge Racer 2 went online in 2.1, with 2–8 player crossplay racing through Wireless Battle.
Official website: nimbusrecomp.org
This repository holds the finished release distros only. Grab them from Releases.

The runtime components for all fourteen games are bundled; no original disc images, ROMs or ISOs are included.
What's new in Alpha 2.2

Naruto Shippuden: Ultimate Ninja 5 (PlayStation 2, Europe, SLES-55605) joins as a native port — the thirteenth game and the first Naruto title — on Linux, Windows and Android. Link your own disc image; nothing from the game ships with Nimbus. HD texture packs are on the website: PC 2x, 3x and 4x, plus Android 2x lite and full. Three optional "Faster picture" settings (Native glow, Fast bright blends, Fast cut-out edges) are off by default, which gives the exact picture.
Mobile Suit Gundam: Gundam vs. Gundam NEXT PLUS (PlayStation Portable, Japan, NPJH-50107) joins as the fourteenth game — the first Gundam title — on Linux, Windows and Android, with the same HD pack tiers and a "Game text" setting: English (the default) or Original.
A new HD texture pack standard, starting with the two new games: BC7 on PC, ASTC on Android, every detail level made offline, and the whole linked pack loaded into graphics memory before play starts — nothing loads or builds while you play, at about four times less video memory than uncompressed textures. The other twelve games keep their existing packs in 2.2.
Shaders are prepared once, for every game. The one-time "Preparing shaders" pass after an install or update now covers every game that has a shader set; Budokai Tenkaichi 3, Ultimate Ninja 5 and Gundam vs. Gundam no longer compile their own shaders at their first start.
Local 2 players in every game — even games that didn't ship with it in their original release. PSP fighters and Ridge Racer 2 open two linked consoles, each with its own picture; PS2 games read the second pad; GBA games show both consoles side by side.
Saves: a new in-game setting for every game — My save or Everything unlocked (the provided save, on its own copy). Ridge Racer 2 boots on your own save, Sagas has a provided save, and Android GameCube games each have their own memory card.
Fast-forward now works in the PS2 games, and from a controller (hold Back + RB, rebindable) and a touch button in every game.
Online fixes: Tenkaichi Tag Team's false "Connection was lost" is fixed (both players update to 2.2), and Ridge Racer 2 rooms work on a fresh install again.
Early in this build (to be finished in 2.3): player save states in PSP and PS2 games (off in multiplayer), and Android pause and resume when you switch apps.
All twelve games from Alpha 2.1 remain fully playable.
Known issue: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 shows a black screen on Pixel-class phones (Mali graphics, for example the Pixel 9a); a fix is planned for 2.3. Gundam vs. Gundam's English text covers the main menu and its help text in 2.2; submenus and notices are still in Japanese.
Next up (2.3): HD movies for the two new games, new-standard packs for the other twelve games, the Budokai Tenkaichi 3 Pixel fix, and finished save states.

Bring your own legally dumped games. No copyrighted game files are included.
How TNRP works
TNRP runs on a hybrid core that sits between recompilation and decompilation. Each game has its own native core, running on a shared Nimbus host and renderer. There's no emulator and no interpreter emulating the hardware. Every game can be played in Original or Remastered mode. Detailed architecture notes will be posted on the website later.
We don't pretend to be the hardware.
Source
The Nimbus Recompilation Project is closed source for now, while server hosting, networking and cross-platform compatibility get sorted out, and to keep development focused. Open source is planned, along with a mature toolset. Everything is free, and we don't take donations. Third-party licenses and notices are included inside each download.
Contact: TheNimbusProject@yahoo.com

1cevgs6.title: Instagram Testing Joke-Stealing Detection to Crack Down on Fake AI Comics
1cevgs6.content:
Stop them if you’ve heard this one before.

Meta is rolling out new features to help crack down on scammers stealing other people’s content.

The changes include a pilot program where eligible creators can enroll in a service where they’re notified if the company’s algorithm finds plagiarized versions of their content.

The move reported in The Hollywood Reporter and other outlets about comedians spotting their jokes being stolen, often word for word, by accounts featuring attractive AI comics. Often, these bogus comedians were linked to OnlyFans accounts.

Instagram chief Adam Mosseri announced the measure on Threads on Tuesday: “This week we’re starting to roll out ‘Content Protection,’ a new way to see and review copies of your videos in your insights on Instagram. You can decide to hide the copy or add a link back to your original. We’re also working quickly on ways to catch copies that are harder to spot, like when someone takes scripts or jokes and uses AI to swap out the visuals. We will not get everything right at first, but we’ll keep improving as fast as we can.”

According to a spokesperson, the service “alerts eligible creators when it finds visual matches of their original videos and lets them decide what happens next, including tracking a copy, adding a credit link or hiding it. Once enrolled, creators’ new original videos are automatically protected, and they can manually select eligible older videos for protection.”

“Separately, we’re testing script detection with a small number of creators to help identify copies that reuse someone’s script or jokes while changing the visuals with AI,” the spokesperson added. “That remains a limited test, distinct from the broader content protection rollout, with plans to expand soon.”

Instagram says eligible creators will receive a notification in their activity feed allowing them to enroll.

In October, two comics posted detailed side-by-side breakdowns showing how their joke was taken by AI. “AI stole my joke and my outfit,” said George Brett Olson. “You might be saying, ‘I’ve heard comedians talk about this already,’ but this is new — very new.”

“So another AI bot just stole my joke,” added Julia Jasunas. “I’ve seen a couple other videos of other comedians posting about the exact same problem, and the thing that’s the most concerning is these AI bots are going viral, and people think that they’re real people. Who does comedy in Daisy Duke shorts?”

The real George Brett Olson is at left.

1xlcjg7.title: Keke Palmer & Lena Dunham Circling Universal Rom-Com From Writers Tracy Oliver & Scott King
1xlcjg7.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Universal Pictures is in early development on an untitled romantic comedy to team Keke Palmer and Lena Dunham, sources tell Deadline.

Reps for Universal declined to comment. Plot details are currently under wraps. The script is by Tracy Oliver, creator and executive producer of the Prime Video comedy series Harlem, and Scott King. Eyeing to star, Palmer is also in talks to produce, as are Lena Dunham and Michael Cohen through Good Thing Going, and The Bachelorette alum Rachel Lindsay.

Oliver’s series Harlem, exploring 30-something New York friendships, ran on Prime Video for three seasons from 2021-2025. Over its run, the show earned six NAACP Image Award nominations and two at the GLAAD Media Awards, among others. She’s otherwise perhaps best known for creating and writing the BET series First Wives Club and co-writing Girls Trip, with which she became the first African-American woman to write a film that grossed over US$100 million. Most recently, Oliver co-wrote the upcoming holiday comedy Deck the Y’Alls, starring The Help’s Octavia Spencer and Jessica Chastain, also contributing to the writing of Netflix’s Women Like Us. She is repped by CAA, Artists First and Myman Greenspan Fox.

A three-time WGA Award nominee for his work on Mad TV, King worked with Oliver on Harlem and has most recently served as showrunner and executive producer of Prime Video’s Overcompensating. Also part of the writing and producing teams for Insatiable, SMILF, Difficult People and The Real O’Neals, he is repped by UTA, Entertainment 360 and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller.

A two-time Emmy winner, Palmer has most recently been seen starring in Peacock’s The ‘Burbs and Boots Riley’s I Love Boosters. Upcoming, she has Spaceballs: The New One and Ride or Die, a Lionsgate romantic buddy comedy where she stars opposite Marlon Wayans, among other projects. She is repped by 3 Arts and Hertz Lichtenstein Yong & Polk.

Dunham just announced a five-episode limited series revival of her lauded HBO series Girls. Prior to that, she released Too Much, her rom-com limited series created with Luis Felber for Netflix, which she and Cohen exec produced. Also upcoming for Dunham’s Good Thing Going banner is her latest directorial feature, the Netflix rom-com Good Sex, starring Natalie Portman and Mark Ruffalo. She is repped by CAA and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller.

Best known as a contestant on ABC’s The Bachelor turned lead on spin-off The Bachelorette — where she became the first Black lead in the history of the franchise — Lindsay has made appearances on a pair of HBO Max series: Hacks, where she played herself, and Made for Love. The Universal rom-com would mark her first feature producing credit. She is repped by Entertainment 360 and Myman Greenspan Fox.

1je4faf.title: Festival In Focus: Qatar Ramps Up International Film & TV Ambitions As Local Talent Shines
1je4faf.content:
Qatar will be re-signaling its ambitions to become a major international film and TV player this week with the second edition of its revamped Doha Film Festival and accompanying Industry Days, with Joe Russo and Omar Sy among the guests at the latter.

The Doha Film Institute, which launched the festival under the Ajyal banner in 2013, and oversees the new version, has been steadily building an ecosystem supporting local filmmakers and indie world cinema talents since its creation in 2010.

The country’s Film Committee, which was created in 2022 under the auspices of Media City Qatar, is now turbo-charging efforts to connect the territory with mainstream film and TV players.

At the inaugural Industry Days in 2025, the committee unveiled a 50% film and TV cash rebate; the shoot of a Barbara Broccoli-produced production of Othello starring David Oyelowo and Cynthia Erivo and partnerships with Neon, Company 3, Miramax, Department M and Sony.

Amid the buzzy atmosphere and networking chat at the event, no-one foresaw the U.S. and Israel’s military campaign against Iran’s Islamic Republic regime coming down the line at the end of February. The latter’s retaliatory bombardment of its Gulf neighbors would temporarily bring the region to a grinding halt.

Some nine months later, hostilities have abated and Qatar is at the heart of negotiations to bring about a truce, while life has almost returned to normal amid an uneasy calm across the Gulf states.

Film Committee Hassan Al-Thawadi, who previously oversaw the organization of the Qatar World Cup, remains resolute in his drive to make the territory a key film and TV player.

“The feedback around Industry Days was very encouraging. The first edition gave us an opportunity to introduce our vision for Qatar’s film industry, engage the region and hear directly from filmmakers, studios, producers and financiers,” he says.

“More importantly, after the event, we understood that our vision resonated with support for the ecosystem around financing, production, talent, infrastructure and access to the region we are trying to build,” he adds.

He acknowledges that the U.S.-Israel-Iran war has thrown up challenges but says the overall plan remains in place.

“We can’t escape the difficult period our region has experienced,” he says. “However, the fundamentals of what we are trying to build has not changed. We have a long-term strategy to attract international production, develop Arab talent and capability and to create a stronger platform for stories from our region to reach global audiences.”

Proof of this, is the second edition of three-day Industry Days which kicks off on Thursday, with a guest list bursting with heavy-hitters and the promise of as many announcements as the inaugural event.

“Last year was about introducing the Film Committee, our ambition to transform Qatar into a global hub for the film industry, and a new proposition for the region to create greater opportunities and international visibility for Arab cinemas. This year the emphasis is on progress and moving from ambition into activity,” says Al-Thawadi.

“The clearest evidence of progress this year is a portfolio of supported films with Paper Tiger, Artou and Furies reaching international festivals, and projects moving through creative development and production planning,” he continues.

“You will hear more about the Qatar Screen Production Incentive and how we are extending its regional reach, about projects and talent moving into their next stages, and about partnerships becoming more practical and production focused.

Among those due to attend are Squid Games creator Hwang Dong-hyuk, who will join a conversation on how the show conquered the world and Joe Russo, who is no stranger to the Gulf region.

Omar Sy will join a discussion on why actors are increasingly creating their own studios. Alongside his acting career, the Lupin star is a producer under the Carrousel Studios banner, his joint company with Thomas Benski who will also be town.

Regional talents joining the conversation include Ukraine-born, Germany-based Syrian Lebanese filmmaker Ameer Fakher Eldin (Yunan) who will join a conversation with Syrian star Taim Hasan and Kuwaiti journalist and media host Ammar Taqi on the challenge of bringing real lives onto the big screen.

In other panels, there will be a focus on Indonesia as Asia’s Next Screen Powerhouse, while the event venue is also hosting an exhibition going behind the scenes of the making of films including Jurassic Park and Forest Gump.

Grassroots growth

The Doha Film Festival program in the meantime bears testimony to the grassroots filmmaking culture which is slowly but steadily taking shape.

In a watershed moment for the local filmmaking scene, four locally produced features – spanning Jodari Meno by Jamal Al Khanji, A Very Ordinary Life by Muhammed Deniz, First to Fly by Rodrigo Vazquez Salessi and When the News Breaks You by Hamad Al Hajri – will world premiere in the Made in Qatar section.

In documentary Jodari Meno, Qatari director Al Khanji, a trained heart surgeon and avid spearfisherman, reflects on his life and family ties while documenting his worldwide quest to catch a world record dogtooth tuna.

Turkish director Deniz’s Qatari–Moroccan–Turkish feature film A Very Ordinary Life follows a retired Qatari pilot and a young Moroccan art teacher whose lives become intertwined through dreams and letters, unaware of a buried family secret.

Argentinian London-based journalist and director Vazquez Salessi’s documentary First to Fly follows two young gymnasts on a quest to become the first ever athletes to represent Qatar in the Rhythmic Gymnastics World Championships.

The debut feature documentary of Qatari filmmaker Al Hajri, When the News Breaks You explores the challenges facing journalists working in the Middle East.

Both Jodari Meno and When The News Breaks were made with the support of the Doha Film Institute over many years, with the directors also attending its workshops as well as its annual project and talent incubator Qumra.

“Attending events like Qumra and exposing the work to critics definitely shaped this work,” says Jodari Meno director Al Khanji.

“The film started as an adventure documentary with my goal to show all this footage I had shot around the world with these strange fish and crazy encounters with sharks,” he explains.

It slowly dawned him that there was also a more personal side to the story, but it took feedback from mentors at Qumra and the DFI to push him in that direction

“Someone said the underwater footage is beautiful, but you need to talk more about you,” he recalls. “It’s not something I would necessarily have done on my own.”

Al Khanji hopes films like his will bring a fresh perspective on the region.

“The more we have people telling human stories, the better the area will be understood,” he says.

1yvgc1h.title: Michiel Huisman, Samuel Armfield & Erik Alens Join Apple TV’s Wyatt Russell-Led Monsterverse Series
1yvgc1h.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Michiel Huisman (Echo 3, The Flight Attendant), Samuel Armfield (Big Boys, Edge of Extinction) and Erik Alens (Dune: Prophecy, The Agency 2) have joined the recurring cast of Apple’s upcoming series from Legendary’s Monsterverse, centering on Young Lee Shaw. They join series lead and executive producer Wyatt Russell, reprising his titular role from the series Monarch: Legacy of Monsters.

Character details for Huisman, Armfield and Alens are under wraps.

From showrunner Joby Harold, the series will follow the story of Col. Lee Shaw (Russell), an American operative who, in 1984, went on a secret mission behind enemy lines in an attempt to stop the Soviets from unleashing a horrific new Titan big enough to destroy the U.S. and turn the tide of the Cold War.

The previously announced cast also includes Millie Brady, Pilou Asbaek, Corey Stoll, Ralph Ineson, Nyasha Hatendi, Connie Nielsen and Stana Katic.

Legendary’s Monsterverse is an expansive cross-platform story universe centered on humanity’s battle to survive in a world facing a catastrophic new reality: the monsters of myths and legends are real. The franchise began with the Godzilla film in 2014 and continued through 2017’s Kong: Skull Island, 2019’s Godzilla: King of the Monsters, 2021’s Godzilla vs. Kong and most recently Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire. Next up is the sequel Godzilla x Kong: Supernova, which is set to release in 2027.

The new series is executive produced by Harold and Tory Tunnell for Safehouse Pictures alongside Russell, Chris Black, Kyle Bradstreet, Alex Boden, Dillard, Andy Goddard and James Skotchdopole. Hiro Matsuoka and Takemasa Arita executive produce on behalf of Toho Co., Ltd., the owner of the Godzilla character.

Huisman is repped by UTA, Authentic Talent & Lit, and Conway Van Gelder Grant. Armfield is repped by The BWH Agency. Alens is repped by Independent Talent Group, Mosaic, and Ziffren Law.

4soycr.title: Records from 2,000 lakes reveal ecological changes moving increasingly in sync
4soycr.content:
Credit: Tom Macret from Pexels

Although lakes cover less than 2% of Earth's surface, they play a key role in regulating global carbon, nutrient and biodiversity dynamics.

A recent study led by professor Zhang Ke from the Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (NIGLAS) has found that global lakes are undergoing a structural shift: They are losing their historical spatial heterogeneity and becoming increasingly synchronized across the planet.
The study, titled "Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling," was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences on Nov. 16. It highlights how this ecological synchronization has emerged as a new hallmark of the Anthropocene, fundamentally changing how inland waters respond to large-scale environmental changes and potentially threatening Earth-system stability.
Lakes are losing their natural buffering capacity
Historically, lake ecosystems fluctuated independently, with local watershed characteristics helping buffer them against broader environmental changes. This "spatial asynchrony" acted as a natural planetary shock absorber, distributing ecological disturbances across time and space. However, by integrating century-scale sedimentary archives with continuous satellite observations from approximately 2,000 lakes, the research team identified a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000, accompanied by a significant decline in network modularity.

Increasing ecological synchrony among lakes revealed by satellite observations and long-term sedimentary records. Credit: NIGLAS

Driven by environmental telecoupling, including climatic extremes (such as heat waves) and socioeconomic pressures, this widespread synchronization is aligning lake dynamics on a planetary scale. The researchers said that phytoplankton biomass and water clarity act as integrated proxies for lake metabolic activity. The increasing synchrony of these indicators suggests that the underlying carbon, nutrient and biodiversity dynamics they reflect may also be becoming more synchronized over time.
"This loss of buffering capacity transforms lakes from passive, regionally distinct systems into active amplifiers of global environmental risks. Synchronized lakes can concentrate biophysical fluxes, potentially triggering high-amplitude global pulses, such as simultaneous greenhouse gas emissions or widespread aquatic hypoxia, thereby exacerbating the triple planetary crisis," Zhang said.

Managing interconnected lakes as a planetary commons
Addressing this challenge, the study highlights a "scale mismatch" in current environmental governance, which traditionally manages water bodies as isolated local resources. Zhang and his co-authors propose a paradigm shift: treating interconnected lake networks as a dynamically coupled "planetary commons."
To operationalize this concept, the team introduced the framework of Strategic Planetary Lake Areas (SPLAs). By tracking macroscale synchrony and modularity metrics, policymakers can identify prime candidate regions—such as rapidly converging regional subnetworks—for targeted polycentric governance. The ultimate objective is not to eliminate synchrony but to safeguard the localized ecological processes that maintain landscape heterogeneity.
"This research not only redefines the critical importance of inland waters in global change studies but also introduces a macroscale dimension to international sustainable development agendas," Zhang said. "The work emphasizes that preserving the diversity of ecological responses is essential for maintaining long-term Earth-system stability in an increasingly interconnected world."

Publication details
Ke Zhang et al., Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (2026). DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2611874123

1pijyq1.title: Paramount Pictures представила новый постер "Angry Birds 3 в кино", выполненный в стиле Grand Theft Auto 6
1pijyq1.content:
Создатели картины "Angry Birds 3 в кино" продолжают пародийную рекламную кампанию, обыгрывающую главные хиты поп-культуры. Свежий постер использует узнаваемую коллажную сетку, которая стала визитной карточкой обложек игр от студии Rockstar Games.
Визуально арт отсылает к эстетике Ваис-Сити и предстоящей GTA 6: на фоне неоновых закатов и пальм размещены кадры с главными героями. Ред, Чак и Бомб позируют в солнцезащитных очках, устраивают гонки на картах и управляют воздушным транспортом.
Ранее авторы мультфильма уже выпускали похожие промо-материалы, пародирующие постеры к фильмам "Дюна: Часть третья" и "Обитель зла".
Мировая премьера "Angry Birds 3 в кино" состоится 23 декабря 2026 года. К озвучке своих персонажей вернулись Джейсон Судейкис, Джош Гад, Рэйчел Блум и Дэнни Макбрайд, а среди новичков каста значатся Кеке Палмер, Лили Джеймс и Эмма Майерс.

j9nb9p.title: New research shows why human–AI collaboration requires more than task allocation
j9nb9p.content:
Process model of representational integration. Credit: Strategic Management Journal (2026). DOI: 10.1002/smj.70089

A 2026 Strategic Management Journal study finds that successful generative AI collaboration in expert work depends on how organizations integrate fundamentally different forms of human and AI knowledge.

Tomoko Yokoi, Daniella Laureiro-Martinez, Federico Magni and Stefano Brusoni conducted a qualitative study of GenAI use in professional perfume creation—a setting heavily dependent on tacit, sensory and embodied expertise.
The researchers identify a "cognitive asymmetry" between humans, who draw on tacit and contextual knowledge, and GenAI, which works through codified representations. This creates a representational gap that must be actively bridged.
To bridge the gap created by cognitive asymmetry, the authors identify a process consisting of three practices. First, allocate work according to cognitive advantage: humans frame problems and evaluate solutions while GenAI generates alternatives. Second, translate knowledge between tacit and codified forms through disembodiment and re-embodiment. Third, iteratively steer GenAI as human understanding of the problem evolves.
The paper contributes an organizing framework for human-AI collaboration in creative problem-solving. For managers, the message is that organizations need workflows and skills that translate AI outputs into human context while preserving human sensemaking and expertise.

Publication details
Tomoko Yokoi et al., Organizing across cognitive asymmetry in human–AI collaboration: A study of perfume creation, Strategic Management Journal (2026). DOI: 10.1002/smj.70089

80tksy.title: Paul Bettany and Ruaridh Mollica Can Finally Talk About Those ‘VisionQuest’ Spoilers
80tksy.content:
Logo text

[This story contains MAJOR spoilers from the finale of VisionQuest, “Forever.”]

For all its existential theatrics, Marvel’s VisionQuest was always going to tell a profoundly human love story between a synthezoid father, Vision (Paul Bettany), and the long-lost son he finally claims as his own, Tommy Maximoff (Ruaridh Mollica).

Created by Terry Matalas, the new Disney+ series picks up the threads left dangling after WandaVision and Agatha All Along, where White Vision vanished into the sky with his restored memories and Tommy’s soul was reincarnated into the body of teenager Thomas Shepherd. Over the course of eight episodes, VisionQuest finds both characters wrestling with their fractured sense of identity. Vision works to piece together his humanity while keeping his paternal instincts at arm’s length — fearing that acknowledging Tommy means accepting the loss of Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) — even as Tommy struggles to reconcile his new life with his latent super-speed and a deep longing for the family he barely remembers.

Vision and Tommy’s parallel journeys collide in the finale, when grief pushes a newly unleashed Ultron (James Spader) — Vision’s own mercurial A.I. father figure — to launch a deadly nanobot swarm on London after Jocasta (T’Nia Miller), the companion he unwittingly falls for, is killed. Rather than defeating his creator through brute force, Vision pulls Ultron into a shared sitcom mindscape — a poignant callback to WandaVision — to talk him through his pain and convince him to stand down. The gambit saves the city at the cost of Vision’s own power core, leaving Tommy and his newly arrived twin brother Billy (Joe Locke) to combine their powers and revive their father, cementing the family bond Vision spent all season running from.

Having finally reclaimed his humanity (and transformed back to his original red self), Vision decides to finally release the various A.I.s from his mindscape, dismantling the internal sanctuary he once used to shut out the world so he can build a real life with his now-grown sons.

By the end of VisionQuest, Vision is “fully ready to engage with planet Earth [and] the people in it, rather than this space that he has created where he can just hide and ruminate in his own mind,” Bettany tells The Hollywood Reporter. Still, the English actor — who first played the synthezoid in 2015 — insists that he doesn’t know what the future holds for his character: “As long as there are interesting and fun stories for Vision, I’ll be putting on my tights.”

Similarly, Mollica claims that he does not know when he will play Tommy again, but he knows how his character fits into the MCU canon. “I loved the Young Avengers comics,” says the Scottish-Italian actor. “I really started reading them all as I was going through the audition process for character research. Those stories are so cool, and it’d be cool to explore that one day.”

In separate conversations last week, which have been edited into the extended Q&A below, Bettany and Mollica spoke to THR about playing out Vision and Tommy’s parallel trajectories, sharing the screen with Locke’s Billy for the first time, and their hopes for a full Maximoff family reunion.

***

Jac Schaeffer initially conceived WandaVision as the first show of an MCU trilogy, but she reportedly stepped away from this Vision sequel to focus on Agatha All Along, and Terry Matalas quickly stepped in to redevelop the show. Paul, what exactly was your collective vision — no pun intended — for this final installment, and how involved were you in crafting the story as an executive producer?

PAUL BETTANY It was actually a great thing that we had five years to figure this out. We were able to sit with ideas about what the show could be. It’s easy to think of Marvel as a kind of infernal machine churning out endless product, and actually, it’s very boutique in that you can count the people on one hand that you’re actually speaking to about a project. When Terry came on, he and I went and had a delicious lunch, and he was very collaborative, which is in keeping with how all of my experiences with Marvel have been. He was asking what I wanted to do, and I knew that we were going to have Tommy in it and eventually Billy — it feels so weird to say because I’ve been keeping that so secretive for so long! (Laughs.)

To that end, I wanted to make it really about fathers and sons. I thought it would be a really cool counterprogramming to WandaVision, which was a lot of female energy, to end it with something that was a lot of positive male energy and see how different characters deal with their grief. So when Terry said, “I have an idea. What about we get the band back together and we get James Spader?” I was like, “That’s it! Because now we can do pain and trauma being passed down from father to son, but do it with robots and lasers and fighting and all of that great Marvel stuff.”

Ruaridh, you didn’t even know what you were auditioning for until you met Paul and Terry for a screen test in Los Angeles. How did those early conversations inform your approach to playing Tommy, given that he is also grappling with dual identities like Vision?

RUARIDH MOLLICA The hardest part was figuring out the inner conflict within Tommy right at the start in the first few episodes, where he is denying his existence as Tommy Maximoff, and he’s very much holding onto his life as Thomas Shepherd. He grew up an orphaned kid, he’s not had a lot of support and love in his life, and all he really wants to be is seen. So when you throw something else into the mix that he others himself with, it makes that harder to accept. He’s really struggling with the impossibility of these nightmares that he’s having.

Through those conversations, we really wanted to lean into his utter fear. In that first scene where Tommy meets Vision, I’m strapped in the chair in St. Mayben’s [the psychiatric facility where Thomas Shepherd was held after Tommy’s consciousness was moved into his body], and White Vision goes underneath the red light, and it makes up the red face of all of these nightmares that my character had been having. I put a picture of Paul’s face as Red Vision on my wall and wrote “Devil! Nightmare!” around it, because it was so important to be afraid of him at the start.

And then it meant a really natural progression into slowly trusting and that back and forth of slowly accepting the truth. I guess we’re both doing that simultaneously. To see them on such a parallel journey is really funny sometimes because they’re both wanting the same thing and both unable to accept it. But that’s what’s so beautiful about that relationship, because they need each other to do that.

VisionQuest.

Disney

For most of the season, Vision acts like a father to Tommy while refusing to claim the title, fearing that acknowledging his son means accepting the loss of Wanda and the destruction of their family. It isn’t until he confronts that grief and embraces his humanity that he can finally step wholeheartedly back into fatherhood.

BETTANY You’ve identified what the whole show really is about, which is an acceptance of who you are and being cool with your identity. There is a moment where I’m with Tommy at the pool in episode three, and I tell him, “This isn’t you. I just haven’t been listening well enough, and you are who you think you are.” I think that’s a really powerful thing to say to young people.

I’ve had the fortune — because I’ve been playing this character so long — of meeting the people who are fans of that character. If you listen and you are open, you will hear what feels important about Vision to them — and I really did listen. There was a lot of similarity in the people who were fans of Vision, and I realized, “Oh, that was me when I was young. I was the bullied kid. I was the kid who didn’t feel like he fit in anywhere, who was so concerned that there wasn’t going to be a place for him in the adult world.” And then you understand what that contract is between the audience and Vision.

So that moment foreshadows the moment where Vision finally accepts who he is and what has happened to him, which Terry and I wanted to be the moment that Vision becomes his most powerful. It’s true of humans: [The moment] you really accept who you are and what has happened to you and are okay with that is when you become the most powerful version of yourself. So because we’re in a superhero show with robots, that’s where he gets his powers back. The initial remit from Kevin Feige was: How do we get cool White Vision back to warm Red Vision? We thought it’d be so great and a nice bit of clockwork storytelling if that is the reason that he becomes whole again.

Vision’s personal breakthrough comes in episode seven, when he finally confronts the grief of losing his family — allowing him to transform back into his red self. He only reaches that point after an encounter in his mindscape with two figures whose own complicated father-son dynamic forces him to reflect on his role as a parent: Dr. Phineas Horton, the WWII-era scientist who built the first synthetic man, and J.I.M., his emotionally conflicted creation. Considering you had to play all three characters in that scene, what was the biggest challenge of acting opposite yourself multiple times?

BETTANY I’m always up for a challenge, and it was the most challenging three days mentally, but not really for the reasons one might think. I had a brilliant stunt man called John who was up for learning all of the lines, and he would play the scenes with me. But the problem is when you’re working on your script, you know the story and the lines, but you don’t know how the other actor is going to say those lines. It made me really relish working with actual other actors who are not me, because, for instance, [when] you’re working with James Spader, there’s never a scene where he doesn’t do something to surprise you, and that’s gold dust as an actor working opposite them. Whilst I am working opposite John, I basically know what I’m going to do when I’m the other person.

So it was a tricky three days, but it was such a laugh to know what we were trying to accomplish. There was some pressure on that scene, because it’s really where you are landing the plane in terms of Vision coming to terms with who he is. The last thing we shot was White Vision’s coverage.

Terry, who was directing episodes seven and eight, did a fantastic job with me. He’s an actor’s director, and he pushed me. It’s a silly thing, right? You think of sad things and make yourself upset, and unless you’re an insane person, it’s hard to want to stay in that place. You get in there and you want out; you want to get the shot. I said, “I don’t know, Terry. I think we’ve got it.” He walked me around the corner and we sat down together, and he went, “I think we got it, but I was wondering: We do still have a little bit of time left, and if you have one [more]…” He was, in that very gentle way, pushing me to dig deeper — and that’s the take [of Vision’s breakdown] he used.

As Vision rediscovers his own powers, Tommy — whose superhero name is Speed — is also just beginning to realize that he has powers he can’t control yet. Ruaridh, how did you figure out what those powers would actually look like in live action?

MOLLICA One of my favorite parts about superhero films and shows is when they’re figuring out their powers and don’t quite know how they work yet. At the start, it had to manifest as smaller things. So exploring how that would exist in the transference of energy from the electrical cattle prod in episode two felt like a good way to let that out first, where even Tommy’s not sure what happened. It planted seeds of the truth in his psyche, but it wasn’t a big enough event for him to be like, “Oh wow, I have superpowers,” because it could still be played off as a freak accident.

But it was really cool doing the one in the swimming pool with Paul when I bring him back to life, exploring how speed manifests in being able to change the molecular structure and put that atomic speed into the water to create enough electrical charge to bring him back. We did things multiple times so they’d be stacked over each other in post and used a lot of flickering light and the camera at a certain frame rate [to create that effect].

The running was great, though. When I say, “I’m Tommy Maximoff,” [in the finale], that was the first time I actually sprinted. It was my favorite moment to shoot the whole show because it felt so badass, and Terry was just like, “Just fucking leg it.” And I just ran! I was like, “This is my big sprint moment. I’ve got to sprint.” And only Terry could take the epic superhero moment and make it hilarious by having a father-son argument while running around the table.

Did you have any particular conversations about Tommy’s green Adidas jacket, given that it is the closest he gets to wearing a super suit this season?

MOLLICA At the start of the show, we actually did plan to fit a superhero suit, and it was only later on as we got into the show that [we realized] Billy could create his suit because of his powers, but there was actually no way for Tommy to find a speed suit. I guess we leaned more into how Spider-Man made his first suit. We wanted to do a really strong nod to the suit and have that essence of the comic book green. Obviously, we did get our speed goggles, which are such a signature part of Speed. I think the direction of the track suit and that kind of vibe goes hand in hand with his superpower and the nod to running. It’s kind of funny — of course, Tommy was like, “Wow, I’m super Speed. What would I wear? Oh yeah, running gear.”

Paul, you mentioned that the plan was always to have Billy reunite with Vision and Tommy by the end of VisionQuest. Ruaridh, at what point did Terry clue you in that the twins would be reuniting and using their combined powers to save their father?

MOLLICA I didn’t know before we’d started shooting or anything because I don’t think those scripts had been written yet. I’m sure the ideas were already there, but it must have been almost halfway through when I found out Joe was coming back. I actually think I knew Joe was coming back before he did! (Laughs.)

It was absolutely epic to read that in the script, but doing those scenes in real life and bringing that off of the page was just so magical — pardon the pun — because it’s really a different visual language that gets brought in with Joe’s character that is his signature blues and purples and witchy hexes. It was like stepping into a whole different world, which was really quite exciting. There was that really tough day where we meet each other in the hex for the first time [at the start of the finale]. It was lit by all real candles, so that was the hottest room in the world, so much so that I think me and Joe spent a lot of time laughing.

Tommy initially believes that Billy is too far away to help him, but Tommy could not save Vision alone. Can you give voice to what is going through Tommy’s mind when he sees Billy come through that portal?

MOLLICA I think he just feels held and united in a way that I don’t think he ever has felt before. Tommy really goes into that moment believing that he can bring Vision back. And when he can’t, I think he starts to doubt his strength: “How could I possibly lose the father that I only just found?” Terry and I really agreed that Tommy should be crying in this moment. For him, he has just lost the most important person in his life that he only just found. And having Billy come in that moment to help save the day really solidifies this theme of what WandaVision was, which is that strength of family to tackle things. Obviously, for Wanda, it was to tackle her grief; in this situation, it’s to resurrect. There’s such beauty in that theme.

VisionQuest.

Disney

What else do you each remember from shooting that emotional father-sons reunion?

BETTANY It was really uncomfortable. (Laughs.) I was wildly overacting, and my eye had been blown out from the day before or something from overacting again. [Vision’s] being sort of electric shocked, I guess, to try and bring him back to life, and I was on top of that goddamn nest. (Laughs.) But, actually, it was a lot of fun and it felt like a moment of, the sun is shining, and [imitates a warm hug] God is in His heaven. I wanted it to be, as I did a lot of moments, redolent of things that people know. I think that every parent knows what it is when you’ve been away from your children to just be able to pull your children into you and hold onto them. So, yeah, it was a lovely moment for me.

MOLLICA That finale scene was actually my last day on the whole job. So to have Joe there for that as well was actually really beautiful, and it was quite a momentous way to end everything — and it was really powerful.

Making the show was the single most incredible and biggest moment of my whole life so far. So to have had Paul in there with me at the screen test, where I was learning about everything for the first time and finding out I got the job, and then to be with him at the end — it’s just that funny thing of art imitating life. Our relationship on the show, I feel like, really reflects our relationship in real life. I am always asking Paul for advice, and I feel very supported by him as a titan of the MCU.

Paul, you recently joked that you blew a bunch of blood vessels in your eye while shooting the show, but I didn’t realize that it happened toward the end of filming the finale. Were you really overacting?

BETTANY Well, you can imagine the pressure of thinking, “Okay, so I’ve got a device on my head that’s sucking out my brain somehow. What’s that going to look like?” So you do it and that’s all fine, and then you realize, “Fuck! I’ve got to do this for six hours, or whatever.” (Laughs.) And you’re kind of going [imitates grimacing] for six hours. At some point, [I began] making a self-deprecating joke about wildly overacting and blowing out my eye and it being a lesson in “less is more,” because I don’t know how many thousands and thousands of dollars it must have cost to paint my [bloodied] eye out.

In their final scene together, Vision and Tommy talk about having dinner with Billy in Eastview. What do you imagine their lives together will look like now? How does Vision feel about having to parent his boys now as young men?

MOLLICA I think they’ll just make up for so much lost time; they’ll just want to be together and do regular father-son things. I imagine all the memories they had of their time in WandaVision — I think their first Halloween again together will be funny. I imagine it will still sometimes be awkward and clunky, like that scene in episode six when we’re both alive [after the shootout] and I get out the back of Paladin’s van, and Vision’s like, “Well… I’m glad you’re alright.” And I’m like, “I’m glad you’re alright.” There’s those silly, awkward moments that will always exist in that relationship because that is what family is.

BETTANY I think right now [Vision’s] thrilled and high on it all, and I’m sure the reality of all of that will cause complications. I have a similar thing that happened in my actual life when I married Jennifer [Connelly]. She already had a son. I become a sort of instant father, and that is incredibly exciting. And then the reality of it is there is a lot of work really to build that connection.

I don’t know how to play a robot. I never have. I’ve never tried to. I always try to find human paradigms because I don’t know what else to do.
