tsxgca.title: Jason Blum and James on ‘Obsession’ Success and Horror's Big Year
tsxgca.content:
Blumhouse Atomic bosses Jason Blum and James Wan took a victory lap Wednesday at their Business of Fear panel, during which they discussed horror’s banner year at the box office and why “Obsession” became the breakout hit of the summer.

But before the horror talk began, they had to address the name change. Blum’s Blumhouse and Wan’s Atomic Monster merged in 2024, and the combined labels were therefore known as Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Recently, in early November, Blumhouse Atomic Monster rebranded to just Blumhouse Atomic. Blum explained they rebranded to give a more definitive identity to the overarching banner of the two companies, while also clearing the way for both distinct labels to take credit for their work.

Wan added that Blumhouse Atomic Monster was also “a bit of a mouthful.”

“As Jason pointed out, it really still is Blumhouse movies and Atomic Monster movies,” Wan added. “We’re still making the movies as one company, but still under two labels. We put out a bunch of movies, and so we have to sort of divide it. Some movies play better at Atomic Monster, some movies play better at Blumhouse. At the start of movies, even though it’s going to say Blumhouse Atomic Presents, our logos will still stand individually.”

It was then on to horror’s stellar year. Moderator Ray Subers, head of film at NRG, presented Blum and Wan with a stat that theater attendance for horror films in 2026 went up 7% from pre-pandemic levels, while attendance for all other genre films (action, sci-fi, rom-coms) decreased. Blum theorized this was because watching horror on the big screen is “participatory,” and that audiences craved a “collective experience” after emerging from COVID lockdown.

“I think that after COVID, audiences ran back to sporting events and ran back to concerts, but they had been fed movies,” Blum said. “Kids had been fed movies so much at home that it took longer to discover and remember the movies [in the theater]. And I think horror specifically, if there’s any genre that’s close to a concert or a sporting event, I think horror is more than anything else because it’s so participatory. I think movies generally, but horror specifically, are kind of joining sports and concerts as a great way to get out of your house and have a collective, fun, exciting thing to do that doesn’t involve your phone.”

The conversation then shifted to “Obsession.” Blum joined as an executive producer shortly after Focus Features acquired the film, which, from a budget of less than $1 million, grossed over $500 million worldwide. Blum said he thinks “Obsession” took off for two reasons. The first is because young people can relate to the “universal feeling” of being “obsessed or having someone obsessed with them.” The second reason was that director Curry Barker sharpened his filmmaking skills on YouTube and social media before coming to Hollywood.

“I think that he has a dialogue with his audience, which he has honed over years and years and years of putting little pieces of content on YouTube and watching his audience react and adjusting to it,” Blum said. “The best way I can describe it is it almost feels like when you’re watching the movie, Curry is like whispering in your ear little funny things or like you’re talking to this invisible hand that’s directing the movie in a way that’s very unique.”

Wan added that the success of “Obsession” has inspired a whole new generation of filmmakers wanting to make scary movies, which reminds him of when he was trying to break into the industry with “Saw.”

“That stigma is gone. Horror has crossed over from the black sheep of the household, right?” Wan said. “I really do credit the younger generation with accepting the genre in a big way and not turning your nose down on it in a snooty way. When I was doing ‘Saw’ people looked down on it, right? And it was only a certain demographic that would come out and support the films that we made. But today, like today, it is cool and hip to be making horror films.”

gh-1459523936.title: GitHub - Dimi42FR/OcaDim: Récompilation native d'Ocarina of Time sur PC, depuis ta propre copie du jeu. Fork de Longshot : frame generation AMD (FSR) dans le jeu, correctifs au-delà de 60 fps, leviers CPU mesurés, Setup qui compile chez le joueur. Windows x64 · GPL-3.0 · aucune donnée de jeu.
gh-1459523936.content:
La récompilation native d'Ocarina of Time sur PC, depuis ta propre copie du jeu — par Dimi42FR
Nouveautés de la 0.0.3 — la mise à jour des petits PC
Tout ce qui suit a été conçu et codé côté OcaDim — pas seulement repris de l'amont. Cette version est
pensée d'abord pour les petites cartes et les portables : moins de VRAM, moins d'à-coups, des réglages
qui s'adaptent au lieu de vous demander de deviner.
On fait de notre mieux : une seule machine de test (RX 9070 XT), aucun budget, et beaucoup de cas
difficiles. Ce qui est annoncé ici a été mesuré et testé ; ce qui ne l'a pas été est écrit noir sur blanc
plus bas. Vos retours font le reste.

Menu F1 entièrement en français, avec une section OcaDim séparée des réglages du jeu.
Ça rame ? — un diagnostic qui lit une seconde de mesures (temps par image, 1 % low, VRAM, plafond,
frame generation), nomme la cause probable et propose un réglage. Entrée analyse, applique, puis annule.
Mode Petit PC — moitié de résolution interne, Lanczos, ombres du jeu, sans frame generation ;
le même geste remet les réglages d'avant.
Résolution dynamique (60 / 120 / 144 images/s) sur les paliers de l'upscaler, jamais au-dessus du choix du joueur.
Garde-fou mémoire — au-delà du seuil, la 3D baisse d'un cran, avec message et annulation.
Budget VRAM (Auto / 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 / 8 Go) : c'est le seuil du garde-fou.
Ombrage à taux variable (VRS) 2x / 4x — le HUD et le texte restent nets.
Ordonnanceur de vcores : Auto / Standard / Réactif (200 ms) / Ultra réactif (préemption 1 ms).
Précompilation au chargement — plus rien n'est compilé en jeu (program census (play): created 0).
Mips à la demande, compilation des shaders selon les cœurs, profil conseillé d'après la machine détectée.
FSR 4 (4.0.2) et FSR 3.1 (3.1.6) au choix, applicables à chaud ; HDR corrigé (frames générées en PQ).
Fichiers renommés en ocadim_* ; les anciens longshot_* sont repris automatiquement.

Mise à jour depuis la 0.0.2
Tes réglages, tes sauvegardes et tes caches sont conservés. Le nouveau Setup permet de cocher
NVIDIA (DLSS, DLAA, DLSS-G) lors d'une mise à jour : un joueur en 0.0.2 peut l'activer en passant en 0.0.3.
Sur AMD, la case ne change rien.
Mesures (RX 9070 XT, pilote 26.10.2)

Place du marché : 48 images/s, 21,3 ms, 1 % low 47,8 ms (limité par le CPU).
Plaine d'Hyrule : 67 images/s, 15,1 ms, 1 % low 21,7 ms, GPU 8,5 ms (56 %), VRAM 7,4 / 15,1 Go.
Pas encore vérifié : DLSS/DLAA sur une RTX, et le build joueur PGO du Setup.

Fork de Longshot ·
Windows x64 (Linux hérité de l'amont) ·
Crédits et licences ·
La carte technique ·
GPL-3.0

OcaDim est un fork personnel de Longshot — lui-même un fork de
Hookshot. Il repart du meilleur état de l'amont et y ajoute ce qui est décrit
ci-dessous : la génération d'images d'AMD dans le jeu, des réparations pour jouer au-delà de 60 fps, des leviers CPU
mesurés, et un Setup qui compile le jeu chez le joueur.
Le jeu n'est pas dans ce dépôt et n'y sera jamais. Rien n'est distribué : tout se compile sur ta machine, à partir de
ton .nup.
27 heures. C'est le temps qu'il a fallu pour sortir cette première version : du premier commit (14 novembre, 23:53)
à la version livrée (16 novembre, 03:19). La frame generation d'AMD y est entrée dans la dernière nuit.
Télécharger : OcaDim 0.0.2 — le Setup Windows x64. Il compile le
jeu chez toi, à partir de ton .nup.
Tu viens tester ? Il y a trois choses à essayer ce soir et quatre façons d'aider sans coder, plus bas, dans
À tester chez toi. Un retour qui dit où ça casse vaut dix « c'est bien ».
ImportantLa règle, sans exception : le .nup et le jeu compilé ne se partagent pas. Chacun compile depuis SA copie.
Ce qui se partage : ces sources, ce compilateur.

Ce qu'OcaDim ajoute, et d'où ça vient
Chaque ligne dit d'où ça vient. Quatre de ces ajouts sont écrits ici — la base poussée à fond, la frame generation
d'AMD, le prefetch des descripteurs, les leviers CPU. Deux viennent d'ailleurs, et c'est dit : NX2navi pour les réparations
au-dessus de 60 fps (et huit optimisations portées), Longshot pour le profil PGO. Le reste est de l'assemblage.

Ajout
D'où ça vient
Où le voir

La frame generation d'AMD (FSR) : branchée dans le jeu, en FSR 4 sur RDNA 4
écrit ici — gpu/vk/vk_fg_amd.cpp n'existe pas chez l'amont ; la FG est une fonction du SDK d'AMD, pas une invention de notre part
Graphics → Frame generation by

Le prefetch des descripteurs (seqlock, cache négatif, asks apprises)
écrit ici — zéro occurrence de prefetch dans le replay de l'amont
Graphics → Descriptor prefetch

Batched submits, Draw order barriers, CPU affinity (CCX), et l'auto-échelle petite config
écrits ici — absents de son menu, et gpu/vk/par_scale.h n'existe pas chez lui
Graphics

Deux réparations au-dessus de 60 fps (sols porteurs, eau à pas fixes)
portées de NX2navi (domaine public / MIT)
Graphics → Above-60 fixes

Le Setup, l'identité, le confort
assemblés ici
OcaDimSetup.exe, le menu

1. La base elle-même, poussée à fond — avant d'ajouter
On n'a pas seulement posé des choses sur le dessus : on a repris ce qui était déjà là et on l'a poussé. Ce qui suit
n'ajoute aucune fonction — ça enlève des millisecondes.

Ce qui a été poussé
Le chiffre
D'où ça vient

Les vues de textures (texture_view_of)
4-5 ms → ~1 ms par frame : le stampede d'évictions est mort, une génération de vue par texture
écrit ici

Le cache frontal des programmes (ViewFast, trois générations) fusionné avec le FlatMap de l'amont au lieu de choisir l'un ou l'autre
moins de recompilations ; un test vérifie que le cache répond comme la carte seule
écrit ici

Le chunk chaud à -O2, piloté par assets/profiles/hot_funcs.txt et hot_order.txt
le code chaud compilé au maximum, le reste à -O1 : on ne paie pas le prix d'un -O2 global
écrit ici

Huit optimisations minées chez NX2navi et portées : descripteurs gardés entre les draws, updates d'uniforms par buckets de 1 Ko, index buffer par pool, storage buffer non re-noté, pick du programme par slots, layouts partagés, write-backs là où le CPU relit, images détruites sur leur thread
la somme se voit dans le frame time, pas dans une ligne de menu
portées (NX2navi)

La fenêtre d'éviction fermée à la source, le recyclage borné des tombstones, le budget d'upload revalidé en jeu
le scintillement noir/bonne image/noir, qui revenait toutes les 24 h, est mort
écrit ici

La règle des 90 % de mémoire (la pression mémoire de l'amont, combinée à la nôtre)
le jeu ne se met plus à doser la mémoire au mauvais moment
écrit ici

Le profil PGO du renderer, committé dans le dépôt
-3 à -5 % de frame time, mesuré sur trois sessions
de l'amont (Longshot)

Et la fusion elle-même : les 91 commits de l'amont ont été combinés aux nôtres au lieu d'être choisis — les deux
côtés survivent au lieu d'en perdre un.
2. La génération d'images d'AMD — le branchement est écrit ici
La frame generation du SDK FidelityFX d'AMD est une fonction d'AMD, pas une invention : ce qu'on a écrit ici, c'est
son branchement dans le jeu — alimentée par les vraies données de la scène, et choisissable au menu. L'amont a sa
propre interpolation et la FG de NVIDIA ; celle d'AMD, non.
Où on en est, sans enjoliver : FSR 4 (RDNA 4) est livré et mesuré, c'est ce que les chiffres ci-dessous
mesurent. Le chemin FSR 3.1 n'est pas encore validé, donc pas encore livré : sur les autres cartes AMD, Auto laisse
la frame generation maison faire le travail.
Rien n'a été copié d'une autre build — ni de NX2navi, ni de Triforce, ni d'un build tiers. L'upscaler FSR 4 est celui
du socle Longshot ; la sonde des versions (dans vk_fsr4.cpp) et tout le branchement de la frame generation
(vk_fg_amd.cpp) sont écrits ici, au-dessus des en-têtes MIT d'AMD. Ce qui vient d'AMD, ce sont ses en-têtes et ses DLL,
pas notre code.
Comment c'est branché, en quatre morceaux :

Morceau
Ce qu'il fait

La swapchain du SDK
ffxCreateContextDescFrameGenerationSwapChainVK prend la place de celle de la fenêtre : vkGetSwapchainImagesKHR, vkAcquireNextImageKHR et vkQueuePresentKHR passent par les pointeurs que le SDK rend. Le SDK exige trois queues distinctes de la famille graphique (jeu, présentation, acquisition) : le device les crée.

Les frames générées
À chaque frame, ffxConfigureDescFrameGeneration + ffxDispatchDescFrameGenerationPrepareV2 reçoivent la profondeur (R32F), les vecteurs de mouvement (RG16F), le jitter et la caméra que la chaîne temporelle du renderer calcule déjà pour ses upscalers. La frame generation maison est coupée pendant ce temps, pour ne pas empiler deux interpolations.

Le choix dans le menu
La ligne Frame generation by propose Auto / Built-in FG / AMD FSR FG, s'applique immédiatement, et le compteur de FPS dit qui fabrique les frames. Traduite dans les 12 langues du menu.

Les changements de résolution
La taille maximale du contexte suit l'image du jeu (maxRenderSize) et le contexte est refait s'il grandit ; une bascule vers AMD retire d'abord la swapchain simple, donc une seule par surface.

C'est opt-in : sans la ligne du menu (ou sans RX_VK_FG_AMD=1), les pointeurs Vulkan réels restent en place et le
présent est exactement celui d'avant. Si la bibliothèque d'AMD manque, si le device refuse, ou si le SDK ne donne pas son
accord, le log dit pourquoi et le chemin simple reste.
Mesuré en jeu (RX 9070 XT, pilote 26.10.2, sauvegarde dans la Place du Château) :

Ce qui a été mesuré
Résultat

Une zone chargée (la Place du Château, 2765 draws), FSR 4 en 2134x1200 → 2560x1440
44,1 fps réels — c'est le cas difficile — 36 000 présents, 42 130 affichées, 6 148 générées, aucun device lost

Les zones normales, hors des plus chargées
60 à 76 fps réels selon l'endroit — autour de 60 le plus souvent, 69-76 dans les plus légères

Activé par le menu seul (aucune variable)
contexte 4.0.2 en 118 ms, 10 800 présents, 15 729 affichées, 4 931 générées, swapchain refaite en place à 2560x1373 et contexte refait en 86 ms, aucun refus, aucun écran noir

Limite connue : le HUD et les éléments 2D bougent avec les frames générées — c'est la limite de la FG sur un HUD
dessiné en 2D. Une capture « sans HUD » a été tentée (copie compute, parce qu'amdvlk plantait sur vkCmdCopyImage et
vkCmdBlitImage de cette cible) : elle tournait sans planter et le SDK générait bien, mais le rendu composé n'a pas été
jugé bon et a été retiré. Le code n'est pas dans ce dépôt ; la voie reste ouverte.
3. Le prefetch des descripteurs — écrit ici
C'est le poste qui coûte le plus cher au replay : pour chaque descripteur (uniform buffer, texture), et sur chaque
worker, le replay relit la mémoire du jeu au travers de la capture — le mutex des pools, la recherche de page, le scan
des updates. Des milliers de fois par frame.
L'idée : un thread helper, en priorité BELOW_NORMAL, re-marche chaque tronçon du dry pass et publie dans une
table seqlock les octets de chaque overlay que le record demandera. Le record fait alors un memcpy au lieu de refaire
le travail.
Trois pièces :

Les octets : les pages de la capture et les updates du lieu par-dessus, clé (addr, take, lim, view, rec).
Les asks apprises (pf_learned) : le record note ce qu'il demande ; le helper publie la plus grande demande vue
par borne, donc la table apprend au lieu d'être devinée.
Le négatif : « pas d'update sur cette borne à ce lieu » — ub_overlay et ub_read sautent leurs scans
(~2600 par buffer, deux fois).

La justesse : la clé est auto-vérifiante (une demande non couverte = un miss = le chemin d'avant, mot pour mot), le
seqlock fait qu'une réécriture sous une copie est vue, et les stamps view/rec couvrent le helper en retard. Un
miss ne coûte jamais plus que ce que le code coûtait avant.
En jeu : 357-682 overlays servis par fenêtre, ~215 000 scans sautés, zéro artefact. La ligne est en Auto (on
là où le processeur a des threads à donner) et RX_VK_DESC_PREFETCH force pour un run.
4. Trois leviers CPU et l'auto-échelle — écrits ici

Ligne du menu
Ce qu'elle fait
Le chiffre

Batched submits
Garde les soumissions d'une frame et les envoie en une seule au prochain wait, readback ou present
sur RADV, Kokiri Forest passe de 33-41 à 46-61 fps

Draw order barriers
Une passe de draw après une autre n'attend que dans ses étages de fragment ; un compute après un compute ne prend pas de barrière, comme les barrières du jeu l'ordonnent déjà
Auto sur NVIDIA, où c'est mesuré ; On essaie sur ta carte

CPU affinity (CCX)
Garde les workers du replay sur la moitié haute des CPU logiques (le second CCD d'un Ryzen), pour que le thread du jeu garde son cache
Auto à partir de 12 processeurs logiques

Et l'auto-échelle petite config (gpu/vk/par_scale.h, écrit ici) : les workers du replay sont un pour quatre CPU
logiques, bornés à quatre, et aucun sous six ; les segments valent 32 ; le prefetch s'allume dès six CPU logiques.
C'est ce qui fait que ces lignes ne punissent pas un petit PC : elles restent en Auto, et l'Auto regarde ton processeur.
Pour être exact : les deux lignes Replay workers et Replay segments exposent des mécanismes qui existaient déjà
dans l'amont, mais seulement par variables d'environnement (RX_VK_PARALLEL, RX_VK_PARALLEL_SEG). Les lignes, les
valeurs et l'Auto sont de nous.
5. Deux réparations du jeu au-dessus de 60 fps — portées de NX2navi
Le jeu suppose 60 fps. L'amont en répare déjà deux endroits — le gestionnaire de son ramené à 60 Hz, et le nombre de
pas du solveur physique — et prévient que le reste peut dérailler (« certaines cinématiques et certains boss comptent les
frames »). OcaDim ajoute deux mécanismes de plus :

Ce qui cassait
Ce qu'on voyait
Ce qu'on fait

Les sols qui portent un personnage : les trois mises à jour de suivi de surface du contrôleur (f_8015d490, f_80159dc0, f_838baa40)
au-dessus de 100 fps, le dixième de la vitesse du sol conservé s'applique à chaque frame : Link glisse de la plateforme qui le porte
le seuil de comparaison 100.0 devient 100 / (la frame en frames de 60 fps) : la coupure retombe exactement là où elle était à 60

Les surfaces d'eau à pas fixe : les deux gestionnaires (f_83895f20, f_838a2660)
chaque update plus courte que 1/60 s exécutait zéro pas : au-dessus de 60 fps, ces surfaces ne bougeaient plus
le quotient garde sa fraction par objet : 60 pas par seconde, quel que soit le débit

Ces deux correctifs ne sont pas de nous : ce sont ceux de NX2navi (recomp/patches-v111.txt, les jeux ofollow
et owater : domaine public / MIT, repris dans Triforce). Nous les avons portés ici, comme hooks dans le C lifté
(nx2/oot_patches.py, host/oot_high_fps.*), et exposés par la ligne Above-60 fixes du menu, qui les coupe pour
retrouver exactement le comportement d'avant. Le troisième de leurs correctifs (orecord, l'horloge de l'ocarina) est
déjà couvert dans cet arbre par patch_whole_frames.
6. Le Setup, l'identité, le confort — assemblés
OcaDimSetup.exe (WinForms, .NET 8 self-contained) prend ton .nup, récupère les outils, compile le jeu, et
lance. Le paquet ne contient aucune donnée de jeu : le programme du Setup (164 Mo) et 19,4 Mo de sources. Le
reste — les outils, ~250 Mo — se télécharge au premier lancement, chaque fichier vérifié par son SHA-256 (tools.lock).

Le .nup est vérifié avant tout : programme 0400486024DEC000, build e0f3ccfa. Une autre version est refusée
avec un message clair, et rien n'est créé.
Un seul build à la fois (un .lock), comme côté jeu, sinon les dossiers de travail se marchent dessus.
Annuler laisse le dossier reprenable ; « Mettre à jour » recompile dans le même dossier en réutilisant les
outils ; « Désinstaller » retire le jeu et les raccourcis.
La préparation des shaders n'est jamais tuée : son cache vaut une demi-heure.
Rien ne sort de la machine : aucune télémétrie, aucun serveur, aucune mise à jour en ligne.
Il faut : ta copie du jeu, ~60 Go libres, Windows 10/11 x64. Compte ~40 minutes la première fois.

Et l'identité : le jeu s'appelle OcaDim 0.0.1 partout (fenêtre, titre, sauvegardes dans %LOCALAPPDATA%\OcaDim,
statut Discord « Playing OcaDim » avec son artwork et le temps joué), un backdrop et un blason dessinés pour le
projet, et le menu traduit en 12 langues.

Petits PC : on a besoin de tes chiffres
Rien n'est décidé pour les machines modestes, et on ne veut pas coder au hasard. Ce qui aide déjà est en place et en
Auto (preset Minimum/Low, batched submits, prefetch des descripteurs, affinité CCX, workers du replay, correctifs
au-delà de 60 fps), et le détail est dans docs/PETITS-PC.md avec les pistes et l'ordre dans
lequel on les essaiera.
Si tu joues sur un petit PC, ouvre un retour petit PC :
il demande 4 chiffres (fps, frame time, 1 % low, ce que le Breakdown attribue au GPU et au CPU), 3 noms (la scène,
le preset, l'upscaler et les résolutions) et le dossier bug-reports. C'est tout — et jamais ton .nup ni tes sauvegardes.

À tester chez toi, et comment aider
Pas de palmarès : la liste de ce qu'il y a en plus dans cette version, avec son état réel — ce qui est mesuré ici, et
ce qui a besoin de ton PC pour être confirmé. Le but n'est pas qu'on te croie : c'est que tu vérifies.

Ce qu'il y a en plus
D'où ça vient
Où le voir
L'état

La frame generation d'AMD (FSR) : une image entre deux des tiennes, nourrie par la vraie profondeur, les vrais vecteurs de mouvement, le jitter et la caméra de la scène, et choisie au menu
écrit ici — FSR 4 sur RDNA 4
Graphics → Frame generation by → AMD FSR FG
mesuré ici sur RX 9070 XT : 44,1 fps en zone chargée, autour de 60 à 76 en zone normale. Pas encore sur RDNA 2 et 3 : le chemin FSR 3.1 reste à faire

Le prefetch des descripteurs : un helper pré-résout les descripteurs, cache négatif et asks apprises
écrit ici
Graphics → Descriptor prefetch
~215 000 scans sautés, zéro artefact. À confirmer sur un petit CPU

Batched submits, Draw order barriers, CPU affinity (CCX) et l'auto-échelle petite config
écrits ici
Graphics, les lignes signées « Added by Dimi42FR »
batched submits : 33-41 → 46-61 fps sur RADV. À confirmer sur NVIDIA et Intel

Deux réparations du jeu au-dessus de 60 fps : les sols qui portent un personnage, et les surfaces d'eau en pas fixes
portées de NX2navi
Graphics → Above-60 fixes
mesuré ici (voir le test de la plateforme, plus bas). À confirmer chez toi

Un Setup qui compile chez le joueur : ton .nup vérifié avant tout, les outils vérifiés par SHA-256, un seul build à la fois, reprise après un abandon, rien qui sorte de la machine
assemblé ici
OcaDimSetup.exe
utilisé ici. À confirmer : une installation complète sur un PC vierge

Rien de tout ça n'est une première mondiale, et on ne le prétend pas : c'est ce qu'on a ajouté, avec ses chiffres et ses
limites. Deux des correctifs viennent de NX2navi (domaine public / MIT) et sont portés ici. Le détail complet, avec
chaque licence, est dans CREDITS.md.
Trois choses à essayer ce soir

La frame generation, en deux minutes. Graphics → Frame generation by → AMD FSR FG, puis va dans une zone
chargée. Le compteur doit afficher Base xx, AMD FSR FG. Si ça refuse sur ta carte AMD, le log dit pourquoi : envoie-le,
c'est exactement ce qu'on veut savoir.
Le test qui se voit à l'œil nu : une plateforme qui te porte. Mets le Game frame rate cap à 144, tiens-toi sur une
plateforme mobile (un ascenseur, un radeau), puis compare Above-60 fixes Off et On. Off : le personnage
glisse. On : il reste dessus. C'est le symptôme de l'issue 1798 ; il faut dépasser 100 fps pour le voir, ce que le
jeu d'origine n'avait jamais prévu.
Un petit PC ? Preset Minimum (4GB), et donne-nous tes 4 chiffres : fps, frame time, 1 % low, et ce que le
Breakdown met sur le GPU et le CPU. Le formulaire :
Retour sur un petit PC.

Comment aider, sans coder

Le temps que ça prend
Ce que ça change

1 minute
Une issue « ça marche / ça ne marche pas », avec ta carte et ton pilote. Deux lignes suffisent

5 minutes
Le formulaire petit PC : c'est lui qui décidera des prochains chantiers

15 minutes
La FG sur ta carte, avec le log : c'est ce qui dira si elle tient ailleurs que sur RDNA 4

1 heure
Un avant/après sur ta scène habituelle : le meilleur retour qu'on puisse recevoir

Ce qui nous aide le plus, ce n'est pas « c'est bien » : c'est où ça c

gh-1449755182.title: GitHub - ObeseCatLord/Galaxy-Ange-II-PC: Galaxy Angel 2 PC: a native PC port of the Galaxy Angel II PS2 trilogy, built with PS2Recomp static recompilation
gh-1449755182.content:
English | 日本語

Eigou Kaiki no Toki in English at 4x internal resolution with Anime4K and debanding: a battle in 16:9 widescreen, and a story scene.

In VR: story scenes play on a big screen in the game's own space skybox; battles surround you in stereo (left and right eye) and are played with motion controls.
A native PC port of the Galaxy Angel II trilogy for the PlayStation 2:
Zettai Ryouiki no Tobira, Mugen Kairou no Kagi and Eigou Kaiki no Toki.
It is built with PS2Recomp static
recompilation and runs on Windows and Linux (x86-64 and ARM64).
You need your own disc images of the Japanese releases (five discs). No
game data is included.
Playing

Download the installer for your system and run it:
Windows ·
Linux x86-64 ·
Linux ARM64 / Steam Frame.
It installs the newest release, adds the game to the Start menu or the
application menu, and later updates it (run it again, or the
Galaxy Angel II PC Updater shortcut). On Linux, make the download
executable first (chmod +x galaxy-angel-2-pc-installer-*, or in the
file's properties). Prefer no installer? Download the archive for your
system from Releases and extract it; it holds the same
updater (ga2-installer).
Run ga2 (ga2.exe on Windows), or Galaxy Angel II PC from the menu.
Drag your .iso files onto the window (or put them in the isos folder
of the data folder), then pick a game.

You need a GPU with Vulkan 1.3. From 0.11.0 the install is portable: saves, settings and
caches stay in the data folder next to ga2, so deleting the folder removes
everything. Every option is also a command-line flag (ga2 --help, 0.11.0), and
ga2 game.iso goes straight into a game. Details, all options and the VR
guide are in docs/PLAYING.md.
Features

One launcher for all three games. Discs change automatically, and saves
carry over between the games as on the PS2.
2x and 4x internal resolution, widescreen up to 21:9 (the 3D scenes show
more to the sides), and frame rates up to 240 fps at the original game
speed.
Keyboard, gamepad and full mouse play, including battles. Button prompts
match the device you're using.
Hold Ctrl to skip messages, Esc skips movies.
English translation included: choose English in Options > Language.
Story, names, menus, battles and the translated pictures all switch.
Other translations install as language packs
(docs/LANGUAGE_PACKS.md).
Mods: replacement files and HD textures (docs/MODDING.md).
Filters for the 2D art (Smooth, Anime4K, sharp pixels), debanding, and the
PS2 dither turned off.
Cheats menu (F1) and an in-game settings menu (F2).
VR through OpenXR (SteamVR, Monado). The game is shown on a big screen,
and the 3D scenes are drawn in stereo around you. Battles use motion
controls: point a controller at a unit and pull the trigger to select it,
then at empty space to move it there or at an enemy to attack; elsewhere the
laser pointer clicks on the screen.
Native ARM64 build for the Steam Frame, flat or in VR
(docs/STEAM_FRAME.md).

Controls

PS2
Keyboard

gh-1460749223.title: GitHub - tyle-beep/Haiku: Fire Emblem Fates, statically recompiled to a native Windows program. Contains no game files: you build it from your own dump.
gh-1460749223.content:
Fire Emblem Fates, recompiled for PC.
Haiku is a native Windows port of Fire Emblem Fates Special Edition: the US release, the European release in five languages, and the Japanese release, Fire Emblem if. The game's own ARM code is statically recompiled to x86-64, and everything around it, from graphics and audio to files, saves, input and the system services, is native PC code. Nothing is emulated. On top of that it adds what a PC version should have: an options menu, controllers, widescreen and ultrawide, high frame rates, the bottom screen on one display, mods, a randomizer and online battles.
ImportantThis repository and its downloads contain no game files. There is no part of Fire Emblem Fates here: no code, art, audio, text or keys. To play, you need your own legally obtained copy of the game, dumped by you. Haiku builds itself on your PC from that dump. See No game files included.

Screenshots
The Haiku Setup launcher, which checks your dump and builds the game:

Your dump, checked
Building
Ready to play

Features
A native port

Static recompilation, no emulation. The game's code is recompiled ahead of time to native x86-64 code. There is no CPU interpreter, emulated GPU, sound chip, kernel or system service in Haiku.exe: each run ends by checking that nothing emulated ran.
Native Vulkan renderer. The game's draw lists are rendered directly on your GPU, including 3D models, lighting, terrain, shadows, effects, particles and movies.
Native audio: the game's own sound driver feeds a native mixer. Native files and saves: the game is installed as a plain folder, and saves are plain files.

Three versions of the game

US (CTR-P-BFZE), European (CTR-P-BFZP) and Japanese (Fire Emblem if, CTR-P-BFZJ) Special Editions. Haiku Setup recognises which one your dump is and builds that version; each has its own DLC and its own saves.
The European release plays in English, French, German, Spanish or Italian (Options > Interface > Game Language). Haiku's own menus and added text come in every language, made from your dump.
The Japanese release runs with its own script and voices, and Haiku's menus in Japanese (or English: Options > Interface > Menu Language). It keeps what the Western releases don't have: My Room's petting minigame (drag with the mouse), the Festival of Bonds and Cipher DLC, and Corrin's three speaking styles per gender.
Japanese voices for the US and European releases: on Haiku Setup's Play screen, Add Japanese voices… takes the voice files from a dump that has them, the Japanese release or an undub, and the DLC's from the Japanese DLC. Switch between English and Japanese on the Play screen or in Options > Audio.

Graphics

Render scale from 1x to 8x the 3DS resolution.
High frame rates. In-between frames are drawn at your display's refresh rate (for example 175 FPS on a 175 Hz monitor) while the game itself runs at exactly its normal speed. VSync and an FPS cap are options.
Anti-aliasing (MSAA 2x, 4x or 8x).
Full Draw Distance: grass and objects no longer pop in as the camera moves.
Windowed, borderless or exclusive fullscreen, with a choice of monitor and resolution, ultrawide included.
Map pixel art stays crisp at every map zoom level.

Widescreen and ultrawide

16:9, 21:9 and 32:9, as well as the original 5:3 and an automatic mode that follows the window.
The game's 3D view is truly widened: you see more of the map and battles, with nothing stretched.
Menus and dialogue stay centred at their original proportions, with side panels made from the game's own ornamental art filling the wide sides (or, if you prefer, the backdrop carried on softly, or black). Full-screen pictures such as banners, wallpapers, title cards and the Dragon Vein screen cover the sides too, and the game's artwork is never stretched.

The bottom screen on one display

Auto (the default): the top screen fills the window, and the bottom screen slides in only when the game shows something worth seeing on it (the unit under the cursor, the battle forecast, combat through the EXP bar, tutorials, touch screens), then slides away again. It works during combat too.
Always Shown, Manual (show it with a key or button: tap to toggle, hold to peek), Panel (docked beside the top screen) and Classic (the console layouts).
The floating bottom screen can be moved by dragging its frame and resized from a corner. It snaps to the window's edges, and its opacity and timing can be set.
Touch it with the mouse, or with a cursor on the controller's right stick.

Controls

Controllers through SDL3: Xbox, PlayStation (DualShock 4, DualSense), Switch Pro and Joy-Con, and more, with hotplug.
Button icons in the game's style for Xbox, PlayStation or keyboard, switching automatically or set by hand.
Full rebinding for keyboard and controller, including the key that opens the options.
Rumble when the battle screen shakes.
Keyboard and mouse play: the mouse touches the bottom screen and works the options menu.

An options menu in the game's own style

Opens with Esc or the controller's Guide/Home/PS button, and from Options on the game's Main Menu. The game pauses while it's open.
Tabs: Display, Bottom Screen, Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Interface, Mods, Cheats, all drawn with the game's own art and font, and usable with keyboard, mouse or controller.

Gameplay and quality of life

Game Speed from 1x up to 8x and Max, with a key to switch to fast speed and back.
Skip Story: skipped story scenes aren't shown at all, while battles, boss quotes and enemy phases stay untouched.
Enemy Targeting Lines: on the map, a line from each enemy to the unit its own AI will attack next enemy phase.
Growth Rates button on the bottom screen's unit status.
Divine Pulse, off by default: turn back time on a battle map, as in Three Houses and Engage. A timeline of the battle's moments (your actions and the enemy's) shows the map at each one as you scroll, and you confirm the one to return to. Charges grow with the story as in Three Houses (up to 13, 10 on Lunatic), or set a fixed number or unlimited; they refill every map. It's in the map menu, on a rebindable key, and it offers itself before a defeat.
Boon/bane stats shown when you choose Corrin's boon and bane.
S-supports with anyone: Corrin can S-support any partner, of either gender, using the game's own scenes with Corrin's lines regendered.
Choose Kana's gender: ask when Kana appears, keep the game's own, male, female or random.
Free camera in battles, and a free camera in My Castle (fly or orbit), with a smoother third-person camera when walking around My Castle.
Sunglasses: a new facial detail for Corrin in the avatar creator, on every portrait and the 3D model.
Exit to Desktop from the Main Menu, the map menu and the options, and Return to Title from the map menu and the options.
No SpotPass questions after creating your avatar, no "Loading extra data" message at every start, and no eShop entries in the Dragon's Gate (only what you have installed).
Saves and settings are kept next to Haiku.exe, in userdata\haiku.

DLC and amiibo

DLC: point Haiku Setup at your own DLC and its maps are in the Dragon's Gate, as on the console.
amiibo Hero Battles: the battles of Marth, Ike, Lucina and Robin are in the Dragon's Gate's list, and winning one recruits that hero through the game's own script. No amiibo needed.

Randomizer

Start a New Game as Randomizer, Characters or Classes, chosen on the game's own screens.
Characters trade places through the story, with their own portraits, names, voices, models, growths and skills. The pool has 99 characters, including story characters, Lilith, the amiibo heroes and Kana (of a random gender).
Classes are shuffled within each character's gender and tier, with weapons to match. Corrin's own class is randomized too, and Swap Corrin puts your Corrin in someone else's place.
Seeds: the seed is shown so a run can be shared, and a fixed seed can be set in settings.toml.
Stored per save, with a rules version, so a randomized save always loads the same run and an ordinary save plays as normal.

Cheats
A Cheats tab, off by default:

Units: change a unit's class, stats, level, EXP and weapon ranks, give any skill, or add any character to your army.
Battle: 100% critical or hit, enemies always miss, no damage, one-hit kills, move again, unlimited movement, Dragon Veins for anyone, a frozen turn count, an EXP multiplier, perfect level-ups, any class using any weapon.
Items & Resources: gold, a full convoy, unlimited seals, My Castle's resources.
Story & Supports: every support conversation, support ranks, and Chapter Select.
Save States: eight slots with a thumbnail, the date and where you were (the chapter and turn, or My Castle), plus quick save and quick load keys. They're kept beside Haiku.exe and never touch the game's own saves.

Mods

A Mods screen, from the Main Menu or the options: turn mods on and off, set their load order, see file conflicts and missing dependencies, and Apply and Restart.
Mods go in the mods folder next to Haiku.exe, as folders or zips. Luma3DS-style (LayeredFS) and plain romfs/ mods work as they are, including replacement music and sounds, text, models and maps. File patches (.ips, .bps) are supported.
Texture packs, including Citra-format HD texture packs. Large downloads (zips within zips, or packs split into several parts) are recognised and unpacked once, in the background.
Code mods: code.ips, IPS32, code.bps, code.bin and exheader.bin patches are recompiled to native code, not interpreted. Haiku needs a C compiler for that and asks before downloading one.
Native plugins in C (or anything that makes a DLL), with hooks before and after the game's functions, per-frame callbacks, memory access and options: see sdk/haiku_mod.h.
No mods come with Haiku. Mods made by others, HD texture packs for example, belong to their authors; get them from them.
Haiku's own text is kept under text mods. When a mod replaces a message file, Haiku adds its own lines to it (Kana's chosen gender, same-gender S-supports, End Turn, the Sunglasses) and fills in any line the mod's file lacks from the game's, so nothing shows up blank.
A code patch made for another release (US, European or Japanese) is never applied to the build of a different one: the Mods screen says it's left out, and the mod's files are still used. A mod can name its game in mod.toml (title = "0004000000179800").

Fan translations of the Japanese game
Haiku can use the fan translations made for the Japanese release, Fire Emblem if: Team If's translation (the Fire Emblem if fan translation project) and cris1010's "Fire Emblem Fates Uncensored Patch" (Team If's work continued, released on the Varis Hangout forum). Neither comes with Haiku; get them from their own pages.

Team If: put the release's zip in the mods folder as it is, then turn it on in the Mods screen.
Uncensored Patch: it comes as a RAR, which Haiku can't open. Extract it with 7-Zip (the password is on the patch's own page), and put the extracted folder (or just its rom folder) in mods.
The patcher (IfPatcher.exe) is never run.
On the Japanese release (the best fit, since the translations were made for it): the files go in as they are, and the patch's dlc folders are laid over your own Japanese DLC, so its patched DLC file isn't needed. You get the whole translated game with the Japan-only content: the petting minigame, the Festival of Bonds, the original script and Corrin's speaking styles. Haiku's menus and its added lines (Kana's question, same-gender S-supports) switch to English, made from the translation's own lines.
On the US or European release: Haiku lays the files out as Team If's patcher does (m/X becomes m/@E/X) and trims them to what that game reads. The patch's Japanese fonts are left out: the game's own fonts draw the translation, and the few signs they can't show (such as ō, or the ≪ ≫ around dragon speech) are written as the nearest ones they can. To use the patch's fonts anyway, add options = { fonts = 1 } to the mod's entry in userdata/haiku/mods.toml. What stays as that game has it: the petting minigame is cut from its code, the Japan-only DLC can't run, DLC maps keep their English text, and a line the translation doesn't have is the game's own. Speaking Style (Options > Gameplay, or the avatar creator's voice) gives Corrin the Japanese script's three speaking styles. The translations work with Voices: Japanese; on the European release the translation shows when the Game Language is English.
The patch's title logo is used.
A save state remembers the mods it was made with, and won't load once a translation has been turned on or off since; the game's own saves are fine either way.

Online battles

Online Battle in the game's own Wireless Battle menu: one player picks Host and gets a code, the other picks Join and types it in. It is peer to peer, and each player brings their own team to the game's own multiplayer maps.
The host chooses whether characters changed with cheats are allowed. When they aren't, such characters are greyed out when picking a team.
Gameplay mods must match on both PCs, while visual mods (textures, text, sounds) can be used freely. A mismatch says which mods differ.

Getting started

Dump your game. You need your own Fire Emblem Fates Special Edition cartridge (US, European or Japanese), dumped and decrypted with GodMode9 on your own 3DS: a .3ds/.cci, .cia or .cxi, or the sdmc folder of Citra or Azahar with the game installed. Optionally dump your DLC the same way (a decrypted .cia). Haiku never needs or asks for console keys.
Download Haiku.zip from the Releases page and extract it somewhere you can write to, for example C:\Games\Haiku. No administrator rights are needed.
Run Haiku Setup.exe, select your dump, then your DLC (or continue without it).
Build. Haiku Setup checks your dump against its own hashes, installs the game's files, makes Haiku's own files from them, recompiles the game's code and compiles it with the bundled compiler. It takes about 10 to 30 minutes, once, and runs at low priority. If it stops, start it again and it carries on.
Play. Next time, start Haiku.exe directly. Press Esc for the options.

Your dump is only ever read. Everything Haiku makes stays in its folder.
System requirements

Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
A GPU with Vulkan support.
About 3 GB of disk space: a finished install is about 2.6 GB, most of it the game's files installed from your dump.
The one-time build needs a fair amount of memory. Haiku Setup only starts as many compilers as your free memory allows, so a PC with less memory builds more slowly rather than failing.

Building from source
Most players should use the release. To build Haiku yourself you need Windows x64 with Git Bash, Rust (stable), w64devkit 2.11.0, Python 3 and your own dump.

Haiku Setup: cargo build --release --manifest-path builder/Cargo.toml
The engine: cargo build --release --manifest-path source/Cargo.toml with FATES_RECOMP_DIR pointing at a folder with librecomp.a, the game's recompiled code, which dev/recomp.sh makes from your dump.
A release folder like the one on the Releases page: put the official SDL3 x64 SDL3.dll in dist-dll/, then dev/builder/package.sh <out dir>. It writes <out dir>/Haiku and Haiku.zip. The compiler's source zip comes from dev/builder/toolchain-source.sh.
The files Haiku makes from the game (decoded UI and fonts, button icons, message files and so on) are not in this repository. dev/builder/derived.pack holds recipes for them, and "Haiku Setup.exe" --apply-derived dev/builder/derived.pack <romfs> . makes them in your checkout from a RomFS installed from your dump (the data\romfs folder of a Haiku Setup build).

The dev scripts take their paths from the environment (dev/env.sh: HAIKU_WORK, HAIKU_TOOLCHAIN, HAIKU_DUMP, and so on). The C files in overrides/ replace individual game functions; vendor/3dsrecomp/docs/overrides.md explains how. Never commit anything made from the game: .gitignore keeps the usual places out.
FAQ
Where do I get the game?
From your own cartridge. Haiku only works with a dump you made yourself of a copy you own. This project does not provide ROMs, keys or game files, and won't help you find them. Issues asking for them are closed.
Which version of the game works?
Fire Emblem Fates Special Edition: the US release (CTR-P-BFZE), the European release (CTR-P-BFZP) and the Japanese release, Fire Emblem if (CTR-P-BFZJ). The DLC must be the one for the same release (the region-free DLC also works with the European game, in English). Haiku Setup tells you if a dump is a different version or edition, still encrypted, or incomplete, and if a DLC doesn't fit your game.
Is it emulation?
No. The game's code is recompiled into a native program ahead of time, and the 3DS's graphics, sound and system are replaced by native PC code.
Do I need the DLC?
No. Without it, the DLC maps aren't available. You can add it later from Haiku Setup without rebuilding the game.
Does Haiku go online?
Only when you play online (online battles talk directly to the other player, with a public STUN server to find a way through routers), or when you agree to download a compiler for a code mod. Haiku Setup never uses the network.
Where are my settings and saves?
In userdata\haiku, next to Haiku.exe. Haiku Setup writes a log, Haiku Setup.log, next to itself.
No game files included

This repository and the release downloads contain no part of Fire Emblem Fates: no code, art, audio, text, video or keys, original or modified.
You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, which you dump yourself. Haiku reads your decrypted dump and never changes it.
The game's code is recompiled, and Haiku's game-derived files are made, on your own PC from your own dump. What is published here is only Haiku's own code, the recipes for those files, and third-party open-source components.
We do not provide ROMs or keys and will not help anyone obtain them. Issues or requests about getting the game are closed.
Don't share the files Haiku builds from your dump (its data and assets folders, or a built Haiku.exe): they contain the game.

Legal

Haiku is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Nintendo or Intelligent Systems.
Fire Emblem and Fire Emblem Fates are trademarks of Nintendo / Intelligent Systems. All other trademarks belong to their owners.
Haiku is provided as is, without warranty of any kind, under the MIT License (see LICENSE).
The release bundles a C compiler (GCC and GNU Binutils from w64devkit), which is under the GNU GPL version 3. Its complete source code is offered on the same release page as Haiku-toolchain-source-w64devkit-2.11.0.zip, next to Haiku.zip (Releases). The GCC Runtime Library Exception means the Haiku.exe it builds is not bound by the GPL.
Third-party mods, such as HD texture packs, belong to their authors. None are included with Haiku; get them from their authors.

Licences and credits

Haiku: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Haiku contributors (LICENSE).
Zakuro by fearkov (github.com/fearkov/zakuro): the 3DS runtime Haiku grew from, MIT License, vendor/zakuro/LICENSE. Haiku carries a modified copy in vendor/zakuro.

gh-1436759286.title: GitHub - nayo186/AloneInTheDarkClassicReborn: A source port of the Alone in the Dark trilogy and Jack in the Dark for modern PCs (Windows and Linux): fixes, HD options and its own launcher. Built on FITD by yaz0r, with parts of Re-Haunted
gh-1436759286.content:
Alone in the Dark: Classic Reborn
Play the original Alone in the Dark (1992), Jack in the Dark, Alone in the Dark 2 and Alone in the Dark 3 on modern PCs and Android phones, with their original graphics and a set of careful fixes and options.
⬇ Download the latest version for Windows, Linux, macOS (experimental) or Android (experimental): unpack it, run Launcher.exe (Launcher on Linux and macOS) and choose your GOG or Steam copy of the game. Nothing else to install. On Android, install the .apk and import your copy of the game (see On Android).
Alone in the Dark, Jack in the Dark, Alone in the Dark 2 and Alone in the Dark 3 are playable from start to end. If something behaves differently from the original, please report it.
Classic Reborn is a C++17 source port of the Infogrames engine, built on a decompilation of the original DOS game. It is a fork of Alone in the Dark: Re-Haunted, itself based on FITD (Free in the Dark) by yaz0r. Its goal is the 1992 game as it was meant to be seen, without its defects: the remaster's HD mode was removed and every addition is optional.

The game data is not included. You need your own copy of Alone in the Dark, Alone in the Dark 2 and/or Alone in the Dark 3 (the GOG or Steam editions). Nothing of the original games is in this repository.

Trailer

Screenshots

The launcher

More screenshots (Alone in the Dark, Alone in the Dark 2 and 3)
Alone in the Dark

Alone in the Dark 2

Alone in the Dark 3

How it was made
Classic Reborn started from a decompilation: FITD's C++ translation of the original DOS engine. On that base it became a source port, the same engine rebuilt for modern systems.
It is not a static recompilation: a static recompilation translates the machine code mechanically into code that runs on another system, without making it readable; here the engine is readable C++ that can be changed and fixed.

The engine comes from FITD, which reverse engineered the DOS executable into readable C++ (renderer, animation, collisions, cameras, inventory, saves...). It is non-matching: it behaves like the original, but it does not rebuild the original executable byte for byte. The engine's French function names (AffObjet, LoadEtage...) come from that work.
The game's logic (doors, monsters, items, events) is not in the executable: it lives in the "Life" scripts of the game's own LISTLIFE.PAK, which the engine interprets as the original did. For study, the engine can translate those scripts into readable C++ (TatouSource/FitdLib/scripts/native/); the game always runs the original scripts.
Everything else (graphics through bgfx, audio, controls, menus, fixes) is new code. Jack in the Dark's music is written for the AdLib sound chip, which modern PCs no longer have, so it plays through an emulation of that chip.

Requirements
To play

Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, and a graphics card with DirectX 11.
Or Linux, 64-bit (x86-64): Ubuntu 22.04, Linux Mint 21, Debian 12, Fedora 37 or newer, or any other distribution of the same age, with a graphics card that supports Vulkan or OpenGL.
Or macOS 11 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel (experimental, see On macOS).
Or an Android phone or tablet with Android 7 or newer, 64-bit (almost every phone since 2017), with Vulkan or OpenGL ES 3.0 (experimental, see On Android).
Your own copy of Alone in the Dark (Jack in the Dark comes with it), Alone in the Dark 2 and/or Alone in the Dark 3: the GOG or Steam editions, or your original CD as an image (see Your original CD).
Nothing else to install: no .NET, no Visual C++ Redistributable, no DirectX setup, no Linux packages. Unpack and run the launcher.

To build the project

On Windows: Visual Studio 2022 (the free Community edition works) with the Desktop development with C++ workload. It includes CMake.
On Linux: GCC 11 or newer, CMake, Ninja and the development packages of X11, Wayland, OpenGL and the sound systems (the list is in Building).
On macOS: Xcode (or its Command Line Tools), CMake and Ninja; tools/makeRelease-macos.sh builds the players' package.
For Android: JDK 17 and the Android SDK with its NDK (the versions are in TatouSource/android/app/build.gradle), on Windows, Linux or macOS.
Git to download the repository.
Optional: Python 3 for the scripts in tools/ (dictionary of methods, layer check).
Every library is included in the repository.

Supported games

Game
State

Alone in the Dark (1992, CD version)
Playable from start to end

Jack in the Dark (1993)
Playable from start to end

Alone in the Dark 2 (1993, CD version)
Playable from start to end

Alone in the Dark 3 (1994, CD version)
Playable from start to end

What it adds

Fixes to the original: objects drawn in the wrong order, monsters stuck at windows, gaps in 3D models, lines at the edges of masks, game speed tied to the frame rate, and many more (see docs/baseline/BUGS.md).
Launcher to choose the game, its language (the five of the GOG and Steam editions: English, French, German, Italian, Spanish) and the data folder, with the same options as the in-game F1 window. The menus are translated into the same five languages.
Screen options: resolution, aspect ratio (4:3, 16:10, stretched), integer scaling, fullscreen, frame limit, VSync.
Optional effects: edge smoothing (FXAA) on the 3D models, bloom from the painted backgrounds, film grain, CRT scanlines, ambient occlusion (SSAO), smoother animations, sharper text.
Custom backgrounds: export every background and mask of the game, enlarge or repaint them, and the game uses yours. Ready-made HD packs are available for Alone in the Dark, Jack in the Dark, Alone in the Dark 2 and Alone in the Dark 3 (see Custom backgrounds). Backgrounds, masks, animated sequences, music and narrators can all be changed: see the modding guide.
Controls: keyboard and game controller (Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch Pro and most other USB or Bluetooth controllers), every action can be changed, several inputs per action.
Modern left stick: the character walks where you push the stick, seen from the camera, like the Resident Evil HD remasters; the D-pad and the keys stay tank controls (see Controls).
Controller vibration: a little when you are hit or shoot, more when you die; it can be turned off in Controls.
Cheats (F1): infinite life (in all four games), behind an "Enable cheats" switch.
Your original CD: play from an image of it (.cue and .bin, or .iso), read as it is (see Your original CD).
Game file check: the launcher checks the files of your game folder against the editions we know and warns if one is missing or different (see Checking the game files).
Separate volumes for music and for voices and effects.
CD or AdLib music in Alone in the Dark and Alone in the Dark 2, which come with both.
Narrators: the French CD's narrator (from your own CD) or a fans' dubbing, with any text language; in Alone in the Dark 2 and 3 the narrator reads the books from the CD, and fans can dub it too (see Narrators).
Alone in the Dark 3 in any of its languages over your GOG or Steam installation, with the files of that language (English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish from the original Spanish CD): texts, voices and narrator (see Other languages in Alone in the Dark 3).
Saves in the format of the GOG edition: saves made in the GOG game load here (the three Alone in the Dark games).
Menus that adapt to any window size and work with mouse, keyboard, controller and touch.
Android: the four games on a phone, with on-screen controls as a controller (see On Android).

Getting started

Build the project (see Building) or get a release.
Run Launcher.exe (next to Tatou.exe). On Linux: Launcher (next to Tatou), see On Linux.
Choose the game in the library on the left (Alone in the Dark, Alone in the Dark 2 or Alone in the Dark 3), press Browse and choose your game folder:

a GOG or Steam installation: the folder with GAME.GOG (or its INDARK subfolder; INDARK2 for Alone in the Dark 2, INDARK3 for Alone in the Dark 3). Music and voices are read straight from the CD image (for Alone in the Dark 3, from its MUSIC folder); nothing is extracted or written there;
or a copy of the game files (a folder with the .PAK files; Jack in the Dark in its JACK subfolder);
or a folder with your original CD as an image (.cue and .bin, or .iso; see Your original CD).

Choose the language of the game and press Play (see Languages). Jack in the Dark has its own button, next to Play on the Alone in the Dark page, when its files are found.

Everything in one folder (portable). Each game can also live inside UserData, in its own GAME folder (the launcher creates them empty): UserData\AITD1\GAME (with Jack in the Dark), UserData\AITD2\GAME and UserData\AITD3\GAME. Copy your GOG or Steam installation there; only these files are needed (the rest, like DOSBox, GOG's saves or the installers, can be left out):

Game
Files

Alone in the Dark
GAME.GOG, GAME.INS (Steam: GAME.INST), the .PAK and .ITD files of INDARK, and those of JACK for Jack in the Dark

Alone in the Dark 2
GAME.GOG, GAME.INS (Steam: GAME.INST), the .PAK and .ITD files of INDARK2

Alone in the Dark 3
the .PAK and .ITD files of INDARK3 and its INDARK3.CFG, and the MUSIC folder

When the launcher opens, a game with no folder chosen takes its GAME folder, and so does one whose chosen folder is gone (uninstalled or moved). If neither is there, its folder stays empty for you to choose. With UserData and the programs in one folder, everything can be moved or copied to another computer or drive.
Updates. When it opens, the launcher asks GitHub for the latest release of this project and, if there is a newer one, offers to install it; the Update button next to the version (bottom right) looks again. Installing downloads the package for your system and replaces only the programs and the documents next to them: UserData (options, saves, backgrounds) and launcher.cfg are never touched. Then close the launcher and open it again. The launcher connects to the internet only for this, and the game never does.
Starting a game without the launcher (for example from a frontend that lists your games, each one as its own entry). The simple way is enough for almost everyone: open the launcher once, choose the game folder and the language there, and set the rest with its Options, Controls and Audio cards (or in the game, with F1). From then on, each game only needs its name:
Tatou.exe --game aitd1
Tatou.exe --game jack
Tatou.exe --game aitd2
Tatou.exe --game aitd3

(./Tatou --game aitd1 on Linux; in PowerShell, with the full path in quotes, put & before it: & "C:\Games\ClassicReborn\Tatou.exe" --game aitd2.) The game finds the folder, the language and the options you chose by itself.
Only if you want something else for one entry, add it to the line:

--data "<folder>": another game folder, the same kind you would choose with Browse (for example --data "C:\GOG Games\Alone in the Dark" or --data "C:\GOG Games\Alone in the Dark 2");
--lang <language>: another language of the game for that session (ENGLISH, FRANCAIS, DEUTSCH, ESPAGNOL or ITALIANO).

Your original CD
If you own the original CD of a game, you can play from an image of it instead of the GOG or Steam edition. Put the image in a folder of its own and choose that folder with Browse (or copy it into the game's GAME folder of UserData):

a .cue with its .bin: the whole CD, with the music. A .bin per track, as many programs make them, works too: keep them all next to the .cue;
or an .iso (or a .bin without .cue): the game files only, so the game plays without music.

Everything is read straight from the image: the game files (from its INDARK, INDARK2 or INDARK3 folder, and Jack in the Dark from JACK), the voices and the music tracks. Nothing is extracted, and nothing is written next to the image: options, saves and the log go to UserData, as with GOG. The languages on the CD are offered in the launcher.
Editions. The game knows the files of the GOG and Steam editions, which are the English CDs, and of the Spanish CD of Alone in the Dark 3. Other CDs (other countries, other years) should work too, but some may have small differences: the launcher checks the files of your CD as those of any game folder and warns you if one is in no edition we know (see Checking the game files). If something goes wrong, please open an issue saying which edition you have (language, year) and attach launcher.log and tatou.log: they list the files that differ, which is what we need to make it work. If everything works, please tell us too, so your edition can be added to the known ones.
Checking the game files
When you choose a game folder (and when the launcher opens), the launcher checks its game files against the editions we know: every .PAK and .ITD (not the saves) and the game's .EXE, by size and checksum. It works the same with a copy, a GOG or Steam installation or your CD image. If it takes more than a moment (a slow drive, a pen drive, a phone), a window shows how far it got. The next time only the files that changed are read again, so it is instant.

Files missing: a file the game needs is not there (a copy that was cut short, for example). The launcher says so in red at the bottom and, before playing, warns that the game will close or freeze when it needs that file, listing the first ones. Copy the game folder again from your installation or your CD.
Files in no edition we know: from another edition, changed or damaged. The launcher says so in red and, before playing, warns that the game may not work well, freeze or close. You can play anyway, and if you changed those files on purpose (a mod), tick Do not warn again for these files: the warning comes back only if the files change again.

Both lists, with each file's name, size and checksum, are in launcher.log and in tatou.log (the game checks too, without waiting, also when it is started without the launcher). Please attach them when you report a problem.
Languages
GOG and Steam sell the same edition of each game, with the same languages:

Game
Text
Narrator

Alone in the Dark
English, French, German, Italian, Spanish
English

Jack in the Dark
English, French, German, Italian, Spanish
none (it never had voices)

Alone in the Dark 2
English, French, German, Italian, Spanish
English

Alone in the Dark 3
The one chosen when installing it (English, French, German or Italian); Spanish from the original CD
The one of your installation; Spanish from the original CD

The narrator reads with any text language. A French narrator only came on the old French CD of Alone in the Dark (1993), not in GOG or Steam; if you own it, see Narrators.
Changing them takes a click:

Game language: the Game language list on each game's page of the launcher. It is kept for next time.
Menu language (launcher and F1): Interface, at the top right of the launcher.
Narrator, if you added extra voices: the Narrator list of the Audio window, in the launcher (its Audio card) or in the game with F1.

Other languages in Alone in the Dark 3
GOG and Steam sell Alone in the Dark 3 one language at a time (English, French, German or Italian), and each language has its own texts, voices, narrator and some data files. Spanish was only on the original Spanish CD. The launcher offers the language of your installation; any other one you own can be added as a folder, and the game reads it over your installation without changing it:

Open UserData\AITD3\Languages (next to Launcher.exe; the launcher creates it the first time it opens) and make a folder in it named English, French, German, Italian or Spanish.

Put that language's files in it, from the INDARK3 folder of an installation in that language (or the whole folder):

Language
Files

English
ENGLISH.PAK, LISTSAMP.PAK, LISTLIFE.PAK, ITD_RESS.PAK, LISTMAT.PAK, LISTTRAK.PAK, PRIORITY.ITD

French
FRANCAIS.PAK, LISTSAMP.PAK, LISTLIFE.PAK, OBJETS.ITD, ITD_RESS.PAK, LISTMAT.PAK, LISTTRAK.PAK, PRIORITY.ITD

German
DEUTSCH.PAK, LISTSAMP.PAK, LISTLIFE.PAK, ITD_RESS.PAK, LISTMAT.PAK, LISTTRAK.PAK, PRIORITY.ITD

Italian
ITALIANO.PAK, LISTSAMP.PAK, LISTLIFE.PAK, LISTANIM.PAK, ITD_RESS.PAK, LISTMAT.PAK, LISTTRAK.PAK, PRIORITY.ITD

Spanish (CD)
ESPAGNOL.PAK, LISTSAMP.PAK, LISTLIFE.PAK, PRIORITY.ITD, ITD_RESS.PAK

With a French installation, the other languages also need its OBJETS.ITD, and French over any other one needs its own: the French version numbers its scripts differently. A folder that lacks a file it needs is not offered (the launcher writes which one in launcher.log).

For the voiced intro and the narrator, add that language's audio tracks: the files of its MUSIC folder (Track02.ogg...) as they are, or named after the track minus 1 (01.ogg...), as .ogg, .wav or .mp3. Without them, the texts and the voices of the scenes are in that language and the intro and the books are read by the narrator of your installation. The narrator's timing of each language is built into the game.

The Spanish CD also works as an image: its .bin (or .img) with its .cue of the same name in the Spanish folder. Everything is read straight from the image; nothing is extracted.

In the launcher, choose the language in the Game language list of the Alone in the Dark 3 page (it appears once the folder is found) and press Play.

Your installation is not changed, and choosing its language goes back to it. No game files are included with this project: you need your own copies.
Saves and French. A save keeps the number of the script each object is running, and the French version numbers its scripts differently from the others. So a save made in French can only be loaded in French, and one made in English, German, Italian or Spanish only in one of those (as with the original versions). The load screen shows the others as Other language. Saves made before this version, and GOG's, carry no language and load as before.
On Linux

Unpack the .tar.gz anywhere in your home folder (most file managers open it with a double click, or tar -xzf ClassicReborn-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz).

Run Launcher from that folder (double click, or ./Launcher in a terminal).

Browse to the game installed for Windows (the same for every game):

GOG with Heroic, Lutris or Wine: the game's folder inside the Wine prefix, the one with GAME.GOG (for example ~/Games/Heroic/Alone in the Dark or ~/Games/Heroic/Alone in the Dark 2);
Steam with Proton: steamapps/common in your Steam library (by default ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common);
or a copy of the game files, as on Windows.

Folders whose name starts with a dot (.steam) are hidden: press Ctrl+H in the folder picker to show them, or type the path.

The game runs natively, without Wine or Proton: those are only needed to install the game files. Everything works as on Windows, including music and voices from the CD image and UserData next to the programs. Updates from the launcher need curl (installed on almost every distribution; otherwise sudo apt install curl or your system's equivalent).
The Linux version is ready to play: built and tested on Ubuntu, with the GOG installation and a copy of the game files, in Alone in the Dark and Jack in the Dark. Alone in the Dark 2 uses the same code and is built for Linux too. Reports from Linux players are very welcome, to keep improving it. Controllers are supported too, with the same code as on Windows (SDL3). If anything does not work on your system (a controller, the sound, the picture...), please open an issue (see Reporting a problem) and we will fix it.
From Windows (WSL). The Linux version also runs in WSL2 with Ubuntu. WSL is not a full Linux PC, so for a smooth game it helps to:

use the graphics card through Mesa's Dozen driver (Vulkan over Direct3D 12): Ubuntu's own Vulkan in WSL draws on the processor;
send the sound to a PulseAudio server on Windows: WSLg's own sound tends to stop after a while;
keep the game files inside Linux's disk, not on a Windows drive (/mnt/c, /mnt/d), so camera changes stay smooth;
try controllers on a real Linux PC: WSL does not pass them to Linux.

1co4mni.title: Пригнать машину из-за границы станет труднее: что ждет импорт авто к 2027 году
1co4mni.content:
С 2027 года ввозить автомобили в Россию станет труднее. Причин несколько: очередная индексация утилизационного сбора, ограничения на экспорт машин из Китая – включая требование к автопроизводителям подтверждать наличие сертифицированной сервисной сети на внешних рынках – и возможная корректировка оформления автомобилей, которые приходят через ЕАЭС.Эксперты считают, что для локального автопрома это скорее плюс, а вот покупателю, который хочет пригнать машину из-за границы, станет сложнее.Часть компаний, которые занимаются доставкой иномарок, уже перестала принимать заказы. Об этом рассказал Кирилл Митин, основатель международного сообщества собственников автобизнеса Kir Avto. По его словам, дело не только в сжатых сроках логистики – влияют и грядущие изменения правил экспорта и оформления.Что меняется в правилах ввоза Минпромторг подготовил проект новых правил расчета и уплаты утилизационного сбора. Для машин, которые ввозят через страны ЕАЭС, предусмотрены нововведения. Если автомобиль не проходил таможенное оформление в России, сбор будут считать с учетом разницы между таможенными платежами, которые должны были быть уплачены, и фактически внесенными суммами в другой стране союза.Для расчета планируют использовать специальный перечень средней стоимости автомобилей. Обновлять его Минпромторг намерен не реже одного раза в квартал.По сути, схема должна уравнять условия для тех, кто ввозит машины напрямую, и тех, кто пользовался более дешевым оформлением в соседних странах ЕАЭС. На деле именно это и вызывает тревогу у импортеров: каналы, которые раньше позволяли экономить, могут закрыться.Прогнозы продавцов и импортеров«Новые машины точно подорожают, причем ощутимо. Самое заметное изменение будет в цене доступных машин», – уверен Кирилл Чернов, владелец группы AvtoRevizorro.Компания занимается реализацией и обслуживанием иномарок из-за рубежа, преимущественно из Европы.Елена Лисовская, эксперт по подбору и доставке автомобилей из-за границы, в том числе из Китая и Кореи, тоже не ждет мягкого сценария. По ее словам, «цены на импорт вырастут, а каналы через ЕАЭС планомерно закроются».«С 1 января будет провал продаж и неминуемое подорожание», – заключила она.Чернов полагает: автопродажи просядут, а выбор интересных предложений из параллельного импорта заметно сузится. Зато есть и другая сторона – рынок будет белеть, продавцы окажутся в равных условиях. Сейчас, по его словам, «кто ввозит честно, не может конкурировать с теми, кто пользуется занижением таможенных платежей, а покупатели больше не будут бояться доначислений: все машины будут растаможены, как положено».Ярослав Полозов, основатель LFA Group, которая специализируется на продаже и ремонте иномарок из-за границы и преимущественно из США, придерживается схожей точки зрения.«Подобные инструменты идут на благо экономики, а также положительно сказываются на развитии местного производства и поддержании продаж локальных брендов», – говорит он.Правда, есть нюанс. Из-за новых правил, по словам Полозова, «умирает сегмент определенных автомобилей, включая массовые поставки восстановленных после ДТП машин с североамериканского рынка, позволявшие недорого покупать премиальные модели». А вот аудиторию, которая покупала дорогие иномарки в люксовом сегменте, подорожание с 1 января 2027 года сильно не потревожит.«Что они стоили условно 30 млн руб., что они стоят 35 млн – владельцам таких машин по боку», – уверен эксперт.Дмитрий Иваницкий, основатель компании «Мосподбор», занимающейся импортом иномарок из Кореи и Германии, с коллегами солидарен. По его словам, «из-за предложения Минпромторга фактически приравнять все таможни для тех, кто таможит машины из разных стран в Киргизии или Белоруссии, ценники на автомобили очень сильно вырастут».Прогноз по конкретным моделям у него тоже жесткий.«Скорее всего, перестанут ввозиться распространенные модели вроде BMW X5, X6, X7, а также Zeekr 8X и 9X. Мы посчитали, они подорожают на несколько миллионов», – отметил Иваницкий.Дополнительным фактором для роста цен, уверен он, станут экспортные ограничения, инициированные в Китае.Китай усиливает контроль экспортаС 1 января 2027 года Китай ужесточит требования к экспорту автомобилей. Автопроизводителей обяжут подтверждать возможность технического обслуживания и ремонта на сторонних рынках, а также гарантировать поставки запасных частей и расходных материалов.Для покупателя это означает еще меньше выбора и более высокие цены – причем не только на сами машины, но и на запчасти. Полозов считает, что потребители все чаще будут сдавать старые автомобили в трейд-ин и переходить на новые модели локальной сборки с официальной гарантией завода-изготовителя.В общем-то, картина складывается неоднозначная. Локальный автопром и рынок в целом могут выиграть от обеления и равных условий, но у тех, кто привык искать машину за рубежом, пространство для маневра сузится. И чем ближе 1 января 2027 года, тем заметнее это будет по ценникам и предложению.О том, как сейчас ввозят машины из-за границы, «За рулем» рассказывал на примере Toyota Fortuner из ОАЭ.Обзор выгодных предложений по ОСАГО в 2026 Согласие – ОСАГО. 100% онлайн за 5–10 минут. Дополнительно можно оформить Белую карту (расширение к ОСАГО для поездок в Беларусь) или Мини-каско — покрывает ущерб, даже если у виновника нет полиса. АльфаСтрахование – ОСАГО. Е-ОСАГО. Страховая сумма до 500 000 ₽. Минимальный срок от 20 дней. Сравни – ОСАГО. Сервис подбора и покупки полиса ОСАГО в 3 шага: рассчитать стоимость - выбрать лучшее предложение - купить. Mafin – ОСАГО. Сервис автоматически заполняет данные автомобиля и сохраняет расчёты. Бонус от «За рулем»: промокод AFFILEAD10 - кэшбэк 10% от стоимости полиса. Примените промокод на сайте страхователя, введя его в специальное поле «Промокод».Рекомендуем также: Как реально сэкономить на каско до 50%? Обзор самых доступных допстраховок на автомобиль.

7p6c4g.title: Vintage Modern’s New Fastback Turns the Mustang into a Carbon-Fiber Movie Star
7p6c4g.content: Vintage Modern has built a successful business turning the Bronco into a retro-look attention grabber. Now it's taking on the Mustang.The Vintage Fastback has the look of the “Eleanor” 1967 GT500 Fastback, with just enough tweaks to be its own thing.Choose between the standard V-8 or up to 840 horsepower from a supercharged version.While there are seemingly unending restomod companies flooding into the scene every day now, Atlanta-based Vintage Modern is among the most established of them. Starting out seven years ago building a truck that looked like a vintage Bronco yet offered proper modern mechanicals underneath, the company has by now produced some 500 cars and delivered them to celebrities from Mark Wahlberg to LeBron James. Now, it’s expanding its range.Vintage ModernSpeaking of celebrities, Vintage Modern’s new Mustang-based Fastback is clearly based on a certain 2000s movie star. The hero car from the Nicolas Cage movie Gone in 60 Seconds, a Chip Foose–customized 1967 Mustang GT500, is well known in the enthusiast community as “Eleanor,” the car Cage couldn’t keep his hands off.To be clear, Vintage Modern isn’t saying its carbon-fiber-bodied creation is a take on the Eleanor Mustang, but there are plenty of similarities up to and including those massive front lower driving lights. However, underneath things aren’t 1967 but 2026 and newer, with the platform of a modern S650-chassis Mustang providing the basis for the build.Vintage ModernPower starts from a standard 5.0-liter V-8 with 486 horsepower, paired with either a six-speed manual or a 10-speed automatic transmission. If you need more punch, perhaps for improbably enormous bridge jumps (professional driver, closed course), then a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger ramps things up to a healthy 840 horsepower.Overall, though, what you’re paying for with the Vintage Fastback is the build quality that comes with doing this kind of work for some time. Vintage Modern says that each car represents 900 hours of assembly time, with hand-laid carbon-fiber panels and handcrafted assembly.Vintage ModernVintage ModernNo cost is mentioned at this point, though a quick look at what the Modern Classic truck costs indicates that those builds start at around the $250,000 mark. Since everything’s handmade apart from the mechanical bits, there’s an enormous amount of customization available, so you’re free to keep tacking on line items to that price.Spending that kind of money on a Mustang is a certain kind of flex, but the Fastback’s blend of movie star looks and dependable modern underpinnings should be tempting for those with deep pockets and large Instagram followings. Just maybe lock the keys in a safe if you’re having Nic Cage over for lunch.➡️ Skip the lot. Let Car and Driver help you find your next car.Brendan McAleer is a freelance writer and photographer based in North Vancouver, B.C., Canada. He grew up splitting his knuckles on British automobiles, came of age in the golden era of Japanese sport-compact performance, and began writing about cars and people in 2008.
