1obls0r.title: Rob Lowe Asked Ben Shapiro to Cast Him in ‘Confession’: “I’ve Worked With Left-Wing Writers. Why Wouldn’t I Work With Right-Wing Writers?”
1obls0r.content:
Rob Lowe was ready to sign on to star in Ben Shapiro‘s Confession after he read the “fantastic” script written by the Daily Wire founder.

The Emmy nominee went on the Second Thought podcast Tuesday, where he recounted how he got involved with the film. He started, “I read the script; it was written by Ben Shapiro. I called Ben and said, ‘This is fantastic.’ And he was like, ‘Well, do you think you know anybody 50-ish, leading man who would not be scared just because I wrote it?’ And I go, ‘Yeah, me.’”

“And he goes, ‘You’re good with this?’ I said, ‘I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world. Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’” Lowe added.

During a recent appearance on the Conversations With Coleman podcast on Saturday, Shapiro said that the actor called him and said he was “deeply affected by the script.” When he asked if he could play the lead part, Shapiro said he replied by saying, “You’re Rob Lowe. If you ask to play a part, the answer is yes, but I’m just telling you you’re way too handsome for this. Like, you’re way too good-looking for this part.”

Of Confession, Lowe said the movie was “turned down by every single film festival.” He added, “Summarily frog-marched out of any conversation. Now, this is a movie with me, Nick Nolte, James Franco, Emile Hirsch. I see what they’re picking up, and it’s all political.”

“The thought would be we’d play in a film festival, we would get some buzz, never happened. And then you know Netflix would pick it up or this one would pick — crickets. Absolute crickets,” Lowe said. “So then it defaults to the Daily Wire to be the distributor, and I’m like, hell yeah. I want people to see this movie. And good for them for putting it out. But that wasn’t originally going to be the life of the movie.”

Confession was directed by Václav Marhoul and centers on the interrogation of a prisoner in a Stalin-era Russian jail.

8wx7ga.title: Російські штурмовики в острівній зоні на Херсонщині охоче здаються в полон - пресофіцер
8wx7ga.content:
Чимало російських військових, яких відправляють штурмувати острівну зону в дельті Дніпра біля Херсона, охоче здаються у полон.

Про це в інтерв’ю Укрінформу розповів пресофіцер 34-ї окремої бригади морської піхоти «Борисфен» Євген Воронецький.

«Вони (загарбники - ред.) намагаються працювати в острівній зоні, ми цього робити їм не даємо. На островах загалом без їжі та води питної скільки можна просидіти? Ну, 3-4 дні без питної води, тиждень без їжі. Далі він із глузду з'їжджає. Ми пропонуємо здаватися у полон, коли виявляємо. Скидаємо записку з дрона, з гучномовця пояснюємо, що є можливість здатися, виведемо, інакше – смерть. Просимо кивати – погоджується чи ні. Про полонених: більшість із радістю йдуть у полон», - сказав Воронецький.

За його словами, серед росіян є ті, що в український полон потрапляють удруге, а то й утретє.

Читайте також: Ситуація для цивільних в Олешках погіршиться через збільшення кількості військових РФ - пресофіцер

Воронецький додав, що російські штурмовики справді не розуміють, куди їх посилає командування. Їм пояснюють, що то мало не курорт: «пливіть, а потім чекайте два дні, далі ще два дні». А далі – полон, і вони вже тоді кажуть: «Зрозуміло, що більше ніхто не припливе і що так, мабуть, зникають група за групою».

Як повідомляв Укрінформ, в острівній зоні Херсонщини поле бою завдяки технологіям наразі «прозоре» - спроби ворога просунутися і закріпитися закінчуються знищенням.

gh-1463456970.title: GitHub - Lazaer-YZY/ds2-sotfs-recomp: Static recompilation of Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin (Xbox 360) for Android arm64
gh-1463456970.content:
An unofficial native Android (arm64) port of the Xbox 360 release, made by static recompilation.
Bring your own copy of the game. No game files are included.

Walking through Majula; the very first scene (Things Betwixt by moonlight) and Majula; the opening
cutscene in the witches' hut, rendered in real time. All captured on an AYN Thor at the 60 fps setting.
What it is
The game's PowerPC code (Default.xex v0.0.0.22, title 465307E4) is translated ahead of time to C++ with the
ReXGlue SDK, compiled for arm64 and linked with the SDK's runtime (Xbox 360
kernel, XAM, audio) and a Xenia-derived Vulkan renderer. It runs natively; it is not an emulator of the CPU.
Developed and measured on an AYN Thor (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, Adreno 740) with the Mesa Turnip Vulkan driver,
which the app ships and loads by itself.
Status

Playable from the start of the game through Majula, with saves, cutscenes, audio and the Scholar DLC data.
Performance (AYN Thor, 60 fps setting, a walk through Majula): 60 fps average, 1% low 48-56 fps, no frame over
26 ms; GPU ~13.6 ms per frame at ~640 MHz; about 7.7 W for the whole device, CPU ~79 C and GPU ~68 C.
Frame-rate options: 30, 40 and 60 fps, and "Smoother 60" on 120 Hz panels.
Eco mode (off by default): the 3D scene is shaded at reduced detail for less power and heat; HUD and text stay
sharp. The picture is softer.
Touch controls (or any game controller), a GPU driver manager, a performance overlay.
Known issues: short frame-time dips while new areas stream in; see the issue list.

Gallery

What you need

Your own Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin for Xbox 360: disc 1 and disc 2 (disc 2 carries
Compatibility Pack 4 with the three Crown DLC areas; the game does not start without it).
An arm64 Android device with Vulkan, Android 8 or newer (9 or newer for the bundled Turnip driver). Snapdragon
(Adreno 6xx / 7xx) is the tested path; Mali and other GPUs use the system driver and are untested. About 8 GB free
for the game, plus room for one disc image (7.8 GB) while importing it.

Install
Releases are numbered 0.x while they are test builds; 1.0 comes once they have been played through on more devices.

On the device, download
ds2-sotfs-android-arm64.apk
from the latest release and open it to install
(allow your browser or file manager to install apps when Android asks).

Start it. With no game yet it opens its game-folder page, which lists both discs.

Import the discs from your own disc images (.iso) on the device (internal storage or SD card): tap
Import disc 1… and pick the disc 1 ISO (the game, about 5.5 GB, is extracted), then Import disc 2… and pick
the disc 2 ISO (only its DLC package, 1.2 GB, is copied). The page tells the discs apart by their contents and asks
for the other one when a disc is done; each ISO can be deleted once it is imported.
Or copy from a PC into the device's internal storage, in Android/data/com.ds2recomp.android/files/:

From your discs
To the device (.../files/)

everything on disc 1 (Default.xex, GameData..., sound, movie, ...)
game/ (directly, no subfolder)

the one file in disc 2's content/0000000000000000/FFED2000/FFFFFFFF/ (the DLC package, 1.2 GB)
dlc/

To unpack a disc image on a PC: python tools/android/xdvdfs.py <disc.iso> extract <folder> (Python 3, no other
dependencies). Windows Explorer can browse Android/data on most phones over USB; if it can't, use
adb push <folder>/. /sdcard/Android/data/com.ds2recomp.android/files/game/ (and the same for dlc/).

Start the game. The first start installs the DLC package and loads the bundled shader cache at the title screen
(a minute or two); later starts are quick. The game asks for its "offline" confirmations at boot; that is normal.

Snapdragon (Adreno) devices use the Turnip driver the app ships. Other GPUs (Mali, Xclipse, PowerVR) use the device's
own Vulkan driver: untested, and the game may not start. The CTRL button (top centre) has the frame rate (30 / 40 /
60), Eco mode, depth of field, the performance overlay and the touch layout. If the game crashes, the newest
ds2*.log in Android/data/com.ds2recomp.android/files/logs/ helps in an issue.
You can also build the APK yourself (below).
Building from source
Windows, Git Bash, from a path without spaces. The SDK's third-party sources are not in this repository: take them
from the ReXGlue SDK release this port is built on (v0.10.0), keeping this repository's own files in sdk/thirdparty:
git clone https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk.git ../rexglue-sdk-src
git -C ../rexglue-sdk-src checkout c94f5ebdcb3c9d1a460ca48e04f9758448f8d518 # Release v0.10.0
git -C ../rexglue-sdk-src submodule update --init --recursive
cp -rn ../rexglue-sdk-src/thirdparty/. sdk/thirdparty/
git submodule update --init thirdparty/libadrenotools
Then:
tools/android/extract_game.sh "<disc 1 .7z or .iso>" "<disc 2 .7z or .iso>"
tools/android/build_codegen_host.sh
tools/android/codegen.sh
tools/android/build_android.sh configure build stage apk
Toolchain: LLVM, CMake, Ninja, JDK 17, Android SDK and NDK r28.
Credits

XDASCATX/DS2_switch (GPL-3.0), a Nintendo Switch port of the same
release: the game analysis, codegen configuration, the DLC installer and many game fixes, ported here by hand.
ReXGlue SDK and Xenia: the recompiler, runtime
and renderer this builds on.
Lost Odyssey Recomp: the Android app shell this one grew from.
Mesa Turnip and the
AdrenoTools driver loader.
Notes from MajulaRecomp and
ds2scholar-nx.

License and legal
GPL-3.0 (LICENSE), like DS2_switch; third-party code keeps its own licenses (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
This is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by FromSoftware, Bandai Namco or Microsoft.
Dark Souls is a trademark of FromSoftware, Inc. / Bandai Namco; Xbox 360 is a trademark of Microsoft. You must own the
game; this repository contains no game files, keys or generated code.

ibd240.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
ibd240.content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.

Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.

The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit.

“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.

For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”

He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”

He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”

But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”

When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”

He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”

In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

1fpwcxg.title: SkyShowtime to Shut Down, CEO Exiting
1fpwcxg.content:
Two months after signaling that a major pull-the-plug move was going to be made, Comcast and Skydance are formally shuttering their European streaming joint venture that had been first unveiled five years ago in a far different landscape.

SkyShowtime, the service that serves more than 20 countries, will wind down at the end of 2027, the board of directors for the company informed staff on Wednesday. As part of the decision, CEO Monty Sarhan will exit the streamer.

The company was unveiled in 2021 by Comcast and the then-named ViacomCBS, which had just been merged by Shari Redstone before the company rebranded as Paramount Global. It had been envisioned as a broad general entertainment streaming vehicle with 10,000-plus hours of programming housing Showtime, Nickelodeon, Paramount Pictures, Paramount+ Originals, Sky Studios, Universal Pictures and Peacock content overseas.

At the time of its launch, the race for subscription streaming subscribers was still in its heyday, not to mention that both Comcast and what has become Skydance have made a series of strategic moves that have changed the calculation for a JV. While bundling is still the name of the game, the partners may be changing.

In June, Comcast co-CEOs Brian Roberts and Mike Cavanagh revealed a plan to split into two independent companies, cleaving off its NBCUniversal and Sky content division from its connectivity business. That spin is set to close next year and will reverberate across the entertainment landscape as NBCUniversal goes it alone (“Will it be a buyer or a seller?” questions will only grow louder).

Meanwhile, ViacomCBS morphed into Paramount Global and then was married to Warner Bros. Discovery under the banner of David Ellison’s Skydance. Showtime, which had once been a blue-chip rival to HBO, now is a name that isn’t even on the list of Skydance’s dozens of brands in its giant portfolio of cable channels, studios and streaming services.

Between HBO Max and Paramount+, Skydance now counts 203 million global subscribers, so it’s now already playing in a different tier of the scale game along with Netflix, Amazon and Disney+ among global platforms.

In September, the board of directors at SkyShowtime showed its hand when it informed staff of a “review of strategic options.” At the time, Sarhan noted to staff that the service had “several million subscribers” and could “stand in scale alongside the most established players in the market.” Now the brand will have a one-year transition before fading out.

The full memo from the board of SkyShowtime is below:

Dear SkyShowtime Employees, In September, we shared that SkyShowtime’s shareholders had initiated a review of strategic options, followed by the start of employee consultations in October. That review has now concluded, and the shareholders have made the decision to wind down SkyShowtime’s operations in late 2027. Since SkyShowtime’s launch, the streaming landscape has evolved significantly. Major global platforms have continued to expand their scale and invest heavily in content, technology, and sport. These competitive dynamics have made it increasingly challenging for regional players like SkyShowtime to achieve the scale needed for long-term success. Despite the excellent work and dedication of this team, the shareholders have determined that winding down the business is the most appropriate path forward. After over four years leading the SkyShowtime business, Monty Sarhan has agreed with the Board that it is an appropriate time to exit the company. We thank Monty for his commitment and contributions to SkyShowtime’s journey. We are also grateful to Mark Neil, who has agreed to serve as Interim General Manager, overseeing the wind-down operating period. We are committed to supporting everyone at SkyShowtime throughout this process and sharing information as decisions are implemented. In the meantime, SkyShowtime continues to operate as normal for our members. Employee consultations remain ongoing in accordance with local requirements, and timing and process may vary by country. We want to thank each of you for your hard work, professionalism, and commitment to SkyShowtime and its members. We are grateful for your contributions and will keep you informed as we move forward. The SkyShowtime Board

r84hl7.title: В Евросоюзе хотят наказать Россию за применение химоружия в Украине
r84hl7.content:
ЕС призывает Россию немедленно прекратить любое применение химического оружия (ХО). Об этом в среду, 18 ноября, заявили в Европейской службе внешних связей (EEAS) со ссылкой на выводы отчета Национального следственного управления Украины. В этом документе 17 ноября указали, что имело место широкомасштабное и систематическое применение "средств разгона массовых беспорядков" в форме ХО на линии фронта в Украине.

Выводы однозначны: "они указывают на Вооруженные силы России как на виновника", отметили в EEAS. "ЕС призывает РФ немедленно прекратить любое применение химического оружия и вернуться к полному соблюдению Конвенции о ХО", - подчеркнули в Брюсселе.

Задействование химоружия кем бы то ни было - будь то государство или негосударственный субъект - где бы то ни было и при любых обстоятельствах абсолютно неприемлемо и представляет собой нарушение международного права, указывается далее в документе.

"Виновные должны быть привлечены к ответственности"

Любой случай такого применения должен быть тщательно расследован, а виновные должны быть привлечены к ответственности, заявили в EEAS. ЕС готов ввести в связи с этим дополнительные санкции против РФ.

Организация по запрещению химического оружия (ОЗХО) должна без промедления воспользоваться своим мандатом и установить виновных в выявленных нарушениях Конвенции, указали в Брюсселе.

"Без реальной ответственности Конвенция о химическом оружии и глобальная норма, запрещающая применение ХО, рискуют утратить доверие", - предупредили в Европейской службе внешних связей.

В июле 2025 года в Берлине уже говорили, что Россия все чаще использует в войне с Украиной химическое оружие, включая слезоточивый газ и хлорпикрин.

oam9k9.content: Wondering how to completely fix Jason’s house in GTA 6?This guide explains all the different odd jobs you need to complete in order to totally fix Jason’s house. You’ll get this objective as soon as you return to his house after the game’s second mission, but you won’t have forever to complete it.Jason’s friend Cal mentions that if Lucia’s going to live at Jason’s house, he better fix the place up. In this guide, we’ll explain all the things you have to fix around the house, and what happens if you don’t do it.For dozens of GTA 6 guides,  check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.GTA 6 Jason’s House: All projectsThere are four projects to complete around Jason’s house. You can repair these as soon as you get complete control of Jason following the Gone Fishing mission. You won’t be able to complete the projects at Jason’s House after Lucia is free from prison.You’ll be warned to complete these jobs before she returns, but if you miss that, you’re out of luck.Fix StepsYou’ll have to fix the steps outside Jason’s house to progress the game, so you can’t miss this. There’s a stack of wood to the side of the stairs. Stand next to them and you’ll be able to repair the steps and enter Jason’s house.Fix Leaky RoofTo fix the leaky roof in GTA 6, head outside Jason’s house and find the set of ladders that are stacked next to the door. This is a quick way to make sure that Jason and Lucia get off on a strong foot, and it takes very little time to do.That’s our complete guide to fixing Jason’s house in GTA 6.

tpcbqu.title: GTA 6 Movie? Why Grand Theft Auto Games Haven't Been Adapted
tpcbqu.content:
With this week’s debut of “Grand Theft Auto 6” widely considered to be the entertainment event of the decade, the Rockstar Games-created franchise seems like an obvious target for a Hollywood adaptation. But those producers hoping to land the rights could be waiting indefinitely, as Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has said for years that the company is not interested.

“We’re very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth. Entertainment we’re always proud of,” Zelnick said in an interview on The David Rubenstein Show Nov. 12. “We would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it. If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It’s a high bar to do that. And of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective.”

Zelnick isn’t being coy here, as he’s provided the same answer for years now when asked about the possibility of adapting “GTA” for film or TV. In August 2024, the Take-Two Interactive told Variety the Rockstar Games owner has “selectively licensed intellectual properties” and “the value of those licenses is typically not all that significant, even in great success.”

Beginning with its first title released in 1997, Rockstar Games’ “Grand Theft Auto” franchise is comprised of six mainline titles, as of the release of “GTA 6” on Friday. The games are known for their M rating, extreme violence and criminal activity, largely in the form of committing grand theft auto. For “GTA 6,” the franchise is pushing the boundaries of the open-world genre with the immersive story of Jason and Lucia, a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style criminal duo running on the streets of the fictional Vice City.

In November 2024, Zelnick used the box-office bomb that was the “Borderlands” movie (which was developed and filmed prior to Take-Two’s acquisition of “Borderlands” game studio Gearbox) as an example of what could go wrong if the company’s IP, including “GTA,” was adapted for another medium.

“While the ‘Borderlands’ movie was indeed disappointing, it was good for our catalog sales of the ‘Borderlands’ titles,” Zelnick told Variety. “So we would prefer to have a huge hit and, as you know, we didn’t have a financial exposure to the negative [on the ‘Borderlands’ movie]. So we are selective for exactly the reason that you just cannot control these outcomes and we prefer to control our own destiny. However, we still will license selectively.”

Zelnick hasn’t ruled it out, but sources tell Variety that the team at Rockstar Games, which has also produced the hit “Red Dead Redemption” franchise, is more focused on continuing to build on the “GTA” world within gaming rather than adapting it for Hollywood. The plan has worked out so far: “GTA 6″ currently has a 99 score on Metacritic ahead of its Thursday release, tying it for the highest-rated video game of all time.

Chris Pratt is taking a trip to Paramount. He will star in The Traveler for the studio, where he has also signed a first-look deal. The three-year producing pact could involve starring in projects as well for his Indivisible production banner.

The Traveler is based on Joseph Eckert’s novel, which was published over the summer. It’s a father-son story, about a man who is flung through time every morning at 7:52 a.m. The first jump pushes him 24 hours into the future, but every day, the jump doubles in time, meaning soon he’s hurtling years in a single day. His son, meanwhile, grows up to study quantum physics as he attempts to save his father, who has long been missing through time.

Final Destination Bloodlines filmmakers Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein are directing The Traveler from Justin Rhodes’ screenplay. The feature, one of the more original projects on the runway of any major studio, is gearing up to shoot next year.

Pratt’s first-look deal, meanwhile, also includes Miami Heat, which has a script from Brad Copeland and has Pratt starring and producing with Hutch Parker.

Pratt became an A-list star more than a decade ago with Guardians of the Galaxy, and went on to appear in multiple Avengers movies for Marvel. He also led the Jurassic World franchise from 2015-2022, grossing billions in the process. Earlier this year, he led the animated Super Mario Bros. Galaxy movie, which grossed $1 billion globally, and had a new season of The Terminal List out last month on Amazon.

1cpdr0x.title: Chris Pratt to Star in 'The Traveler,' Inks Paramount Deal
1cpdr0x.content:
Chris Pratt is setting up his next sci-fi adventure: starring in Paramount Pictures‘ big-screen adaptation of “The Traveler,” based on the novel by Joseph Eckert.

The film is part of the new first-look, three-year producing deal Pratt inked at the studio through his Indivisible Productions banner. Pratt will potentially star in select projects.

Eckert’s “The Traveler” tells the story of a reluctant time traveler and his son, and “the bond between them that even millennia cannot break.” A synopsis describes the story as “an adventure full of heartbreak, hope and futures beyond imagination.” Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein will direct “The Traveler,” based on a screenplay by Justin Rhodes. The film will be produced by Adam Rosenberg and Jules Daly.

Additional projects under Pratt’s deal include “Miami Heat,” written by Brad Copeland (“Jerry & Marge Go Large”), with Pratt set to star and produce alongside Hutch Parker (“Venom: The Last Dance”).

Notably, Pratt was among the superstars featured in Paramount’s CinemaCon reel this spring, as David Ellison unveiled his vision for the movie studio under the Skydance umbrella. (Pratt appears in a scene in the executive dining room with director Jon M. Chu, Molly Ringwald, Miles Teller, Damson Idris, Isabel May, Will Smith and James Wan.)

It’s no surprise that Paramount wanted to get in the Pratt business, since it stands to be quite profitable for all parties. The actor has earned more than $15 billion at the worldwide box office, including starring roles in Marvel’s “Guardians of the Galaxy” trilogy and “Avengers” movies, as well as Universal’s “Jurassic World” series and as the voice of Mario in the blockbuster “Super Mario Bros.” movies. (The most recent film, “The Super Mario Bros. Galaxy” movie debuted in April and has grossed over $1 billion globally.) Up next, Pratt produced and stars in “Way of the Warrior Kid” for Apple TV. The film, which adapts Jocko Willink’s bestselling children’s novel, launches on Nov. 25.

After starting his career on TV with shows like “Parks and Recreation” and “Everwood,” Pratt returned in 2022 with the hit series “The Terminal List,” which streams on Amazon’s Prime Video. Pratt produces and stars in the show; the second season, subtitled “True Believer,” debuted on the streamer last month.

6hwvjm.title: Pierce Brosnan Endorses Robert Pattinson as James Bond
6hwvjm.content:
Pierce Brosnan, a former James Bond himself, has taken to social media to enthusiastically endorse the newly anointed Robert Pattinson, who was announced as the new 007 on Monday.

“Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond,” Brosnan, who played the character in four films from 1995 to 2002, wrote on Instagram Wednesday. “You are going to be magnificent. I have fond memories of our time together making ‘Remember Me.’ It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength. Enjoy the ride. Grá mor, Pierce.”

As the “Parent Trap” actor noted in his caption, the two stars first worked together on 2010’s “Remember Me,” a romantic drama also starring Emilie de Ravin and Meghan Markle. With his statement, Brosnan joins stars including Pattinson’s “Tenet” co-star Elizabeth Debicki and former Bond villain Rami Malek in congratulating the “Twilight” actor on securing the role.

Pattinson’s announcement as the next Bond put an end to long-swirling rumors surrounding which actor would step into the role. Other stars in the mix included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult, Josh O’Connor, Tom Francis, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Harris Dickinson and even Harry Styles. Denis Villeneuve will direct the forthcoming film from Amazon MGM.

Before the casting news broke, Brosnan told The Times in September that he thought the new James Bond would be “someone that none of us know about.” He had also noted that “there are lots of good hats in the ring” and “lots of great actors” being considered. When it came to names, Brosnan remained neutral: “I wouldn’t pick anyone,” he continued. “My wife told me not to say anything, and I’ve said too much. Because once I say something it goes [everywhere] and I get hanged.”

12o1mss.title: Bryan Freedman Sued Over Hush-Money Deals Shielding Michael Jackson Estate
12o1mss.content:
Logo text

Five siblings at the forefront of sexual assault allegations against Michael Jackson have sued Bryan Freedman, Hollywood’s favorite lawyer who was allegedly enlisted by the pop star’s estate to deceive them into signing hush-money deals.

In a lawsuit filed on Wednesday in California state court, Frank Cascio and his siblings Edward, Dominic, Aldo and Marie-Nicole accuse Freedman of legal malpractice, breach of fiduciary duty and fraud. They allege that he duped them into signing agreements barring them from publicly discussing Jackson’s alleged abuse that have emerged as obstacles in ongoing litigation against the estate, which Freedman allegedly worked for while representing the siblings when the deals were signed in 2019.

The siblings’ relationship with Freedman started five years earlier when a lawsuit was filed against Edward, who at the time was defending the singer from sexual abuse allegations, and the estate in connection to his work on a posthumous Jackson album. At the recommendation of the estate, which paid for legal fees, he retained Freedman, according to the complaint.

The lawsuit says Jackson’s estate again turned to Freedman to broker deals with the Cascio siblings in the wake of Leaving Neverland, which featured sexual abuse allegations against the singer. Freedman told the siblings that they didn’t need to hire their own lawyer and that the settlement was fair and nonnegotiable, according to the complaint.

“None of this was true,” writes Howard King, a lawyer for the siblings, in the filing. “At the time, Freedman represented the estate, including in connection with litigation against HBO, which had broadcast Leaving Neverland.”

The document the estate presented framed the settlement as an “acquisition and consulting agreement,” identifying the deal as a purchase of the family’s life story rights, the lawsuit says. Under the terms of the contract, the estate made five annual payments of $690,000 to each sibling. In exchange, they are barred from publicly discussing Jackson’s alleged sexual abuse and subject to mandatory arbitration provisions, among other things that include releasing the estate and its representatives from potential liability. It requires the entire family to return all payments if one member is violates the terms of the deal, according to the complaint.

The siblings say they learned of Freedman’s alleged conflict of interest when the lawyer in 2024 told them that the estate hadn’t paid enough money five years earlier. He allegedly called the deal “toilet paper” and that he “had enough on the estate” that would convince its representatives to “do right” by them, the lawsuit says. After Freedman instructed the siblings to hire him, they retained another lawyer, who told the estate that the 2019 deals would be challenged. The estate later filed an arbitration demand against the siblings for breaching the nondisparagement and confidentiality provisions of their deal.

“If Freedman had not fraudulently induced Plaintiffs into signing the agreement, they never would have been dragged into litigation for publicly discussing Jackson’s abuse,” states the complaint, which notes that a child sex trafficking lawsuit they had filed against the estate was forced into arbitration under the terms of the 2019 agreement.

The lawsuit was filed as Freedman, who didn’t respond to a request for comment, fields accusations of helping orchestrate online smear campaigns in public relations battles against his clients’ adversaries. A trial is scheduled to start next year involving Rebel Wilson and producer Amanda Ghost, who accuses the actress and her public relations team of creating a site that accused Ghost of sex trafficking.

1beb3ug.title: Paramount+ Orders ‘Clandestine’ Drama Series Starring Brit Marling & Tilda Swinton From ‘The OA’ Creators
1beb3ug.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Clandestine, a new series from The OA and A Murder At the End of the World creators Brit Marling and Zal Batmanglij, is a go at Paramount+ with Marling and Tilda Swinton starring, Deadline has learned. A high-stakes family drama set in the world of D.C.’s political elite, Clandestine is produced by independent studio Sister Pictures, part of Sister Group.

The series had been developed and greenlighted by the previous Paramount+ regime under former Paramount Chair of Direct-to-Consumer Cindy Holland, I hear. The process of Swinton’s casting was well underway when the October close of the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger brought along a leadership change, with Paramount+ added to the purview of HBO and HBO Max content chief Casey Bloys who became Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Direct-To-Consumer, for the combined Skydance company. Holland exited on the eve of the deal close, with her close associate, Paramount+ Head of Originals Jane Wiseman, who had steered the development on Clandestine, departing a couple of weeks later.

Clandestine is now being overseen by Francesca Orsi, President, HBO Drama Series and Films, I hear.

In the new structure, Wiseman’s team reports to former HBO Max Head of Originals Aubrey, who became Head of Paramount+, Max Originals and International Programming, adding oversight of all Paramount+ programming.

As Deadline reported last month, Aubrey and HBO veteran Orsi have been reviewing Paramount+’s drama slate, with Orsi taking on projects that have a prestige drama feel similar to HBO’s brand. In addition to Clandestine, I hear Orsi also is overseeing Paramount+’s legal thriller Discretion, starring Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning, and 9/11 first responders limited series The Best of Us, headlined by Succession‘s Jeremy Strong.

There has been talk about some Paramount+ drama series potentially moving to HBO but, at least as of now, all of the streamer’s shows are staying put.

According to sources, Marling and Batmanglij started developing the project at Sister while Holland was Global CEO there. Holland left the indie studio in October 2024 to become a senior adviser to then-Skydance CEO David Ellison before becoming DTC Chair for Paramount Skydance post-merger in August 2025.

Marling and Batmanglij took out their script this past spring with Marling attached to star. Paramount+ landed Clandestine in a bidding war with FX, and HBO, I hear. Paramount+ and FX vying for Clandestine made sense as their top executives had commissioned Marling and Batmanglij’s two previous series: Paramount+’s Holland had developed and ordered The OA while running English-language scripted originals at Netflix (in addition to being involved in Clandestine early on), and FX chief John Landgraf and his team developed and picked up A Murder At the End of the World.

This also marks a full-circle moment for Orsi who is now overseeing the series she once bid on.

Clandestine is believed to have received an informal green light as part of Paramount+’s winning bid. While I hear the pickup was not cast-contingent, casting key roles was considered crucial, which explains why the streamer did not announce the series order but instead proceeded with securing the other leads opposite Marling. The process, which started over the summer, is ongoing.

A rep for Paramount+ declined comment.

Clandestine is written and executive produced by Marling, Batmanglij, Rory Haines and Sohrab Noshirvani (Informer, The Mauritanian). Jane Featherstone (Chernobyl, Black Doves) executive produces for Sister Pictures. Blake Holland (The OA, A Murder at the End of the World) and Alice Tyler (Coldwater, The Following Events are Based on a Pack of Lies) are co-executive producers; Callum Devrell-Cameron (Lord of the Flies, Black Doves S2) a producer.

This marks the biggest TV series commitment to date for Oscar winner Swinton who starred in two British miniseries at the start of her career. Her recent feature credits include Pedro Almodóvar’s The Room Next Door, Edward Berger’s Ballad of a Small Player and Joshua Oppenheimer’s The End. She is repped by CAA, UK’s Hamilton Hodell and Peikoff Mahan Law.

Marling and Batmanglij broke out with their 2011 indie movie Sound of My Voice, which the two wrote, Batmanglij directed and Marling co-starred in. Premiering at Sundance, it earned Indie Spirit Award nominations for Best First Feature and Best Supporting Actress (Marling). They are repped by CAA and Hansen Jacobson Teller.

kv2kp4.title: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’
kv2kp4.content:
During his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella lamented the fact that a lot of America’s software systems — including those governing everyday hardware and transportation systems — suffer from unfixable software vulnerabilities that, in the age of AI-aided cyberattacks, are just waiting to be exploited.

“Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable,” Nadella said. “I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet.”

In other words: The smartification of the economy, in which much of the world’s “dumb” devices were hooked up to the internet, is now causing tremendous headaches.

The conversation took place against the backdrop of a wave of recent large-scale outages — including one involving Microsoft Outlook. Others have involved the NSA, the FFA, and Apple. Concerns have swirled that these outages are the result of cyberattacks, although officials have denied those claims. Still, the reality of AI-aided cyberattacks is spurring companies to find new strategies for vulnerability discovery and remediation.

Nadella touched briefly on the recent Outlook situation, noting that the global inconvenience was the result of a “latent bug” that led to a “perfect storm.”

“We put out an incident response, and we’re going to obviously take all of the learnings, both upstream architectural, as well as operational, and fix that,” he added.

“Somebody was telling me about sort of even the transportation systems and the amount of stuff that’s discoverable but with unpatchable firmware,” Nadella also added on the topic of vulnerable systems. “So we’ll have to really modernize for sure … and then we will have to assess what the threat vector looks like, what our own ability to both detect and then defend in real time looks like.”

Nadella made a broader point as well, which is that the process of patching software vulnerabilities has escalated to match the speed of potential exploitation, but that this has caused more problems.

“We now have a very powerful tool that finds vulnerabilities,” he said. However, companies used to have more time to test those patches, understand a situation, and deploy them, he said. At the same time, AI has made sophisticated cyberattacks much easier to enact.

“The patch [now] needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild, right? So that’s going to create instability.”

1czgow2.title: Can you replay missions in GTA 6?
1czgow2.content: Wondering if you can replay missions in GTA 6?Past GTA games have allowed you to replay missions, so now that GTA 6 is out,  players are wondering if there’s any way to replay what they’ve already played through.In this guide, we’ll explain if you can replay missions in GTA 6, and we’ll let you know exactly what parts of the game you can replay forever.If you’re looking for more comprehensive GTA 6 guides, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub, which includes walkthroughs, beginner’s tips and much more.Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.Can you replay missions in GTA 6?Currently there is no way to replay missions in GTA 6.We don’t know if Rockstar will eventually add this feature, but we believe that due to GTA 6’s main missions featuring a lot of different choices that can impact the wider world, including which characters live and die, they’ve decided to not allow players to replay the missions so that the decisions are more impactful.There are some activities in GTA 6 that you can repeat, such as the racing, stunts, pool, and other minigame style missions, but the actual story missions can’t be repeated.Another reason that replaying story missions was removed is likely tied to the medal system from GTA 5 being removed. There are no side objectives on a mission that players need to complete in order to earn a gold medal.  How you play out the missions is totally up to you.Can robberies be repeated  in GTA 6?Yes, you can rob banks and shops multiple times.One element of GTA 6’s gameplay that can be repeated is the in-game robberies. These include shops, which will yield a small amount of cashs. The larger bank robberies, which you’ll get access to over the course of the story, can also be repeated.If you’ve recently robbed somewhere, you’ll see on the map that it’s been greyed out. That means that time needs to pass before it is reset, and you can rob it again.

1fvn26o.title: ‘Primetime’ Cinematographer & Editor On Making Robert Pattinson Look Like A “Superhero” & Breakdown Viral Meme Catchphrase
1fvn26o.content:
In A24’s Primetime, the first predator confrontation unfolds in a bright, colorful home. For cinematographer David Bolen, that contrast was central to the scene’s tension. “This was like, we all felt a lot of anxiety about shooting this because we were like, ‘OK, this is the first predator encounter. This sets the tone for everything. So we have to make sure it’s good,’” he tells Deadline.

Director Lance Oppenheim was drawn to “really intense things happening in really brightly lit, beautiful homes,” Bolen says. “Someone’s life is kind of over, but it’s happening in this really bright, colorful space. So there’s an interesting dynamic there.”

As the film re-creates the To Catch a Predator standoff, Chris Hansen (newly minted James Bond actor Robert Pattinson) confronts a man (Tony Revolori) who thought he was meeting a teenage girl. Bolen says the brightness leaves the man nowhere to hide. “The light is shining directly on him, and no matter what, the cameras are going to capture him,” he says. “There’s an uneasiness about this happening that there’s no place for this predator to hide. Right now, Chris Hansen has him exactly where he wants him.”

RELATED: The James Bond Search Shows How Daunting The Process Is In An Age When Everyone On Social Media Is An Expert

Bolen and his gaffer pushed direct sunlight through the windows as Hansen descends the stairs, giving him a halo. “This in many ways is his superhero shot,” Bolen says. “He’s coming down from the stairs; he’s presenting himself as the full Chris Hansen for the first time. So early on with my gaffer, I decided, ‘OK, we’re going to backlight him really, really heavy with direct sunlight. There’s these windows above him right now, and we’re pushing giant sunlight streaks through him to give him that kind of angelic feel. And that was to play into this like, yeah, he’s a superhero in this moment. This is Chris Hansen.’”

Editor Daniel Garber found another way to stretch the unease in a moment that went viral on social media when Hansen confronted the predator, saying: “You see how this looks right?” Was Garber surprised by the internet craze or did he have an inkling beforehand? “In the edit, we’re also trying to establish a lot of that unsettling atmosphere through the rhythm of it,” he says. “There are a lot of moments where we’re holding on Chris as long as possible, really trying to milk the silences. And I think that draws out a lot of the uncanniness of this whole encounter.”

RELATED: A “Bad Call” Or “Can’t Wait”? Industry & Media React To Robert Pattinson’s Casting As James Bond

Garber adds: “Rob’s performance is one of the most amazing things that I got to deal with in this film. He was, I think, always thinking about Chris Hansen not necessarily as a real person, but as the persona who exists as a meme online at this point. And so a lot of that process of studying the meme of Chris Hansen, I think comes through in the way that he portrays Chris in these moments.”

Further describing the iconic line, Garber continues: “I think it went viral in part because Rob had developed all of these very specific physical performances that he knew would be the kind of moments that really stick in people’s heads. Rob probably knew from the get-go which moments were going to go viral, and I don’t know if I knew exactly, but I think we had a hunch.”

RELATED: Actors Who Have Played James Bond: Sean Connery To Daniel Craig

The kind of experimentation that this film required depends on deep trust. In The Process interview, Bolen and Garber explain that they have worked together for nearly a decade, building a shorthand that lets one department inspire the next. “We’re going to experiment, and we’re going to try things, and we’re not always going to be perfect, but we all support each other,” Bolen says. “Filmmaking’s really hard, and it can be tough on you personally, and when you feel like you have family around you in the collaborators, that’s really special.”

To learn more in-depth about the cinematography and editing involved in Primetime, watch the video above.

7zbe3r.content:
In a rare instance of humility and insight, Elon Musk admitted today he has expensive egg on his face out of MAGA‘s results in the midterm elections.

“I feel pretty foolish having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” the world’s sometimes richest man said Wednesday at the New York Times‘ Dealbook conference. “It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money. If I could rewind the clock I would have spent less.”

When the SpaceX boss says he could have spent less on the likes of now ex-Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in his unsuccessful Senate bid and the GOP’s Senate Leadership Fund, he is talking about a whooping nearly $500 million in donations. At the end of a race that saw the Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress and the Texas governorship, MAGA-linked Musk was the single largest donor of the off-year election.

In fact, Musk is now the largest individual donor in a specific election in American history. Ironically, the previous record holder was Musk himself for the money he doled out to help get Donald Trump back in the White House in 2024.

Appearing virtually from China where Musk is accompanying Trump to the APEC Summit, the X owner’s return to the Andrew Ross Sorkin hosted shindig saw an often rickety and rambling interview on a wide range of topics. Facing tough-ish questions about his role in Russia’s now four-year long invasion of Ukraine, Musk boldly alleged that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is “not always truthful” over his intentions with the South African born entrepreneur’s Starlink tech in pushing back Vladimir Putin’s forces.

Alternating between insights and inarticulation, Musk also touched on the fate of ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Hueng, his own desire to explore the stars, his need to scale up his companies, where AI company Anthropic is going next and where AI will lead us

Politics, however, in all senses dominated the conversation.

As did Musk’s apparent version reality distortion field, as they used to say of Apple’s Steve Jobs.

Insisting he is “not MAGA,” Texas-based Musk offered hope he could work with newly elected Gina Hinojosa when she takes over as governor. Stating “there are positives and negatives in both parties,” former DODGE leader and Trump advisor Musk remarkably said “I’m not sure what MAGA means, but if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.”

As but one example of that not jiving with reality, this is the individual who at an October 2024 Trump rally told the crowd (as he was wearing a black MAGA ball cap): “As you can see, I’m not just MAGA. I’m Dark MAGA.”

Today, with the new realities of power in DC and many once totally red states now run and won by the Dems, Musk added: “I do think that it’s good to have some balance of power. You know, like not have as a general rule have not not have the presidency, senate, and House, all be of the same party.” He continued: “What was my actual goal here …which failed, by the way, obviously, was to have the Senate be 51 Republican …obviously, the Republicans were routed in this in this election.”

Obviously

ds01vg.title: Elon Musk Admits He Feels 'Pretty Foolish' Having Spent $500M on Midterm Election Races Won by Democrats, Claims He Is 'Not MAGA'
ds01vg.content:
Elon Musk spent big backing Republicans in the 2026 midterm elections — which resulted in a sweeping defeat of the GOP as Democrats took over the House and Senate.

Musk spent nearly $500 million during the midterms, including $200 million to try to defeat Senator-elect James Talarico in Texas in his race against Lone Star State attorney general Ken Paxton.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” Musk conceded, “or maybe it would have been much worse without that.” Musk appeared virtually Wednesday at the New York Times’ 2026 DealBook Summit in New York City, connecting via videoconference from China, where the tech mogul is part of President Donald Trump’s American delegation to the region.

Earlier at the conference, Skydance CEO David Ellison said Musk — whose roles include founder, CEO and chief engineer of SpaceX and CEO of Tesla — has become an investor in Skydance, the company formed through the megamerger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. “[T]o have him as a shareholder is an honor and a privilege,” Ellison said. (The subject of Skydance did not come up in Musk’s appearance.)

On the topic of the midterms, Musk said he believes the newly elected Democratic governor of Texas, Gina Hinojosa, “I think is going to be quite moderate. I don’t think she’s sort of a far-left governor, and based on everything I’ve heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with [Hinojosa] as governor.”

Musk, who ranks as the world’s wealthiest individual, insisted that “I’m not MAGA” — even though he has worn “Make American Great Again” hats at multiple public events and served as head of DOGE, the Trump administration’s ad-hoc cost-cutting department, for several months in 2025 before he exited as a “special government employee” amid a dispute with Trump.

Said Musk, “I’m not sure what MAGA means” but “if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party then I certainly don’t have that. I think there are positives and negatives in both parties… but politics is very tribal. A lot of people cannot see any good in the other party, and they cannot see any bad in their own party because they’re more or less invested in their party like it’s their hometown sports team, and it’s just their team, and they won’t accept that there’s anything that the other team can do that’s good or anything that their team can do that’s bad.”

Musk last month said SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a potential merger. “There’s more and more areas of interaction or overlap with SpaceX and Tesla that that didn’t exist before,” he said at the DealBook conference. “So if you’d asked me five years ago, do I ever think there’s any purpose in SpaceX and Tesla getting together? I would have said ‘no.’” He continued, “really, it’s just a question of do SpaceX and Tesla execute better together and create more value than if they’re apart… and that would be up to the shareholders to decide.”

Musk also spoke about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation last week, after the revelation that he had engaged in several affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy and an Nvidia employee. Musk, who has suggested Huang be reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO, said Haung’s removal as chief executive of the AI company was like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team,” while also acknowledging that Huang “certainly made some mistakes.”

Musk, interviewed by the New York Times’ Andrew Ross Sorkin, discussed the controversy over Starlink’s recent restrictions on satellite internet access to the Ukrainian military amid the war being waged on the country by Russia. Musk said, “From the beginning, I’ve said that Starlink is a civilian system. It is not meant to to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people…. If you want to do that you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the U.S. government, but do not ask me as as a private individual to make kill decisions that sometimes result in the loss of innocent lives, not just soldiers.”

Musk appeared at the DealBook conference in 2023, where he accused advertisers who had pulled ads from X over his support of an antisemitic conspiracy theory of “blackmail” and told them — calling out Bob Iger, then CEO of Disney, by name — to “Go fuck yourself.”

bpooh7.title: Elon Musk says ousting Jensen Huang is like ‘kicking Michael Jordan off your team’
bpooh7.content:
Elon Musk has already been vocal about his disapproval of the Nvidia board’s decision to oust its founder and CEO Jensen Huang after a series of extramarital affairs were made public, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who is suspected of feeding sensitive information back to Beijing. At The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk elaborated on his thoughts about Nvidia’s leadership change.

“Jensen is an old friend of mine,” Musk said. “I would call Jensen, you know, Michael Jordan at his peak level, in terms of what he means to a team.”

On X, the social media platform he owns, Musk even said he would hire Huang.

“He’s one of the most talented entrepreneur-CEOs in history,” Musk said when asked about his X post. “Who wouldn’t want to hire Jensen?”

Musk also signed a petition, alongside over 200,000 other people, urging Nvidia to reinstate its former CEO. Nvidia’s board, however, confirmed it is not planning to bring Huang back.

“[It] doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me…,” Musk said of that decision. “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen.”

He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades,” Musk added. “He understands technology incredibly well. His team loves him… and many of them are there because of him, and have higher offers to go elsewhere, and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen.”

Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey also said that he thinks Nvidia is making the wrong decision by not reinstating Huang.

“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said earlier in the day at the DealBook event. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”

Musk also did not express concern over what Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could mean for U.S. national security.

“I don’t think he’s disloyal to the United States,” Musk said. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders.”

Other peers in the industry, like Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, reaffirmed their faith in Nvidia to move forward without its founder and CEO of 33 years at the helm.

“It’s the Nvidia board’s decision, but I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella said at DealBook. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”

123yi5d.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remains confident in Nvidia after Huang’s exit
123yi5d.content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella weighed in on former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unexpected departure amid a series of shocking controversies.

“It’s all sort of pretty tragic in the sense of, you know, Jensen is somebody I’ve known for a long time. I’ve admired what he’s done, and at this point, I kind of want to give him space to figure this out,” Nadella said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.

Huang stepped down last week from his CEO role, which he has held for 33 years. Huang’s leadership has been central to Nvidia’s ascent to one of the world’s most valuable companies, but his judgment was questioned after it was reported that he had an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy feeding information back to Beijing. It was also revealed that Huang was having affairs with two Nvidia employees, including one who was a direct report.

While the world waits to see what the long-term economic impacts of Huang’s departure might be, Nadella says he still has confidence in Nvidia, which is a close partner of Microsoft.

“I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella added. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO at Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I’m in touch with the same set of people I was in touch with before [Huang left], so I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”

Microsoft is not unlike Nvidia in that its founder Bill Gates inhabited a larger-than-life persona as CEO.

“Founders are unbelievable in the sense that they create something from nothing, so that is pretty magical… They’re singular, but they’re not gods, right?” Nadella said. “I used to say to Bill [Gates]… Founders also die, and so at some point, a company, if it needs to succeed, it has to have someone take over.”

19mpo00.title: В США гражданина России обвинили в слежке в Кремниевой долине
19mpo00.content:
Федеральное большое жюри присяжных предъявило обвинение гражданину России Игорю Дью (Igor D’iu) в связи с его предполагаемым шпионажем в Кремниевой долине. Об этом в среду, 18 ноября, сообщили в Минюсте США.

Мужчина подозревается в сговоре в роли агента иностранного правительства, в неуведомлении генпрокурора, пересечении границ штатов с целью преследования, а также в мошенничестве с документами, удостоверяющими личность.

Дью 2 ноября предстал перед федеральным судом и находится под стражей федеральных властей.

Незаконно въехал в США из Мексики

По данным обвинения, он незаконно въехал в США летом 2026 года после того, как был завербован через Telegram для слежки в отношении сотрудников крупной технологической и оборонной компании в Пало-Альто (штат Калифорния). Мужчина получил оборудование, финансовую поддержку и инструкции собирать информацию о сотрудничающей с военными компании, связанной с войной в Украине.

В США Игорь Дью прибыл в июне 2026 года из Стамбула через Мехико, где сообщник помог ему пересечь границу с Соединенными Штатами. Сообщники поручили ему приобрести ноутбуки, мобильные телефоны, оборудование для беспроводных сетей и программное обеспечение для удаленного доступа.Следил за сотрудниками в кафе

В Пало-Альто он должен был посетить кофейню рядом с офисом компании, выявить ее сотрудников и сфотографировать экраны их ноутбуков во время работы. Кроме того, ему якобы поручили разместить ноутбук рядом с офисом компании, чтобы сообщники по удаленному доступу попытались собрать необходимую информацию.

Позднее в круг обязанностей вошла слежка за сотрудниками компании и их местами проживания. Кроме того, 3 сентября, мужчина, как утверждается, преследовал одну из сотрудниц на внедорожнике Lexus, когда она ехала из офиса в Пало-Альто в направлении Сан-Франциско. Женщина позвонила в службу 911 и получила указание направиться к одному из полицейских участков в Сан-Франциско. По версии следствия, Дью прекратил преследование после того, как его жертва связалась с полицейским.

Мужчина позднее приобрел поддельные документы - паспорт США и карточку социального страхования - и продолжил свою деятельность.

Bloomberg: Объектом шпионажа могла стать компания Palantir

В октябре агенты ФБР провели обыски у Дью и в его доме в Ист-Пало-Альто, изъяли около 18 000 долларов наличными, два ноутбука, два iPhone, два российских паспорта, оборудование для беспроводных сетей и поддельные удостоверения. Агенты также конфисковали записную книжку с 10 адресами, многие из которых соответствовали местам проживания сотрудников компании, а также подробные досье на минимум трех работников, содержавшие личную информацию, имена членов семьи, данные об образовании и трудовом стаже, а также оценки их сильных и слабых сторон.

В Кремниевой долине расположены филиалы нескольких американских оборонных компаний. По данным агентства Bloomberg, объектом шпионажа могла стать компания Palantir. Она, в частности, разрабатывает программное обеспечение для анализа данных.

dcj9d1.title: ‘Yaga’ Creator Wanted To Sexualize Men “The Way Female Bodies Are Looked At” In Thriller Genre
dcj9d1.content:
As the dark mystery at the center of Yaga unfolds, the Crave series has turned up the steam with some guy-on-guy scenes.

Series creator Kat Sandler explained that “it definitely was a choice” to have “objectified” Charlie (Noah Reid) and Henry (Hudson Williams) in the episode “The Horns,” in the same “way that female bodies are looked at” in the thriller genre.

“We’re presenting these two stunning men in this way that you’re used to seeing women,” said Sandler on the show’s official podcast.

“You look at Basic Instinct—it’s not the same thing—but it’s a choice to look at male bodies in this show the way that female bodies are looked at it thrillers and in horrors and in mysteries, repeatedly,” she added. “So, it was definitely a choice, but I stand by that it’s important to the story.”

In Yaga, private investigator Charlie Rapp (Reid) is hired to find Henry Park (Williams), the heir to a commercial fishery who has gone missing, while suspicion grows around Dr. Katherine Hargrove (Carrie-Anne Moss), a university professor with an interest in the Slavic witch legend Baba Yaga.

New episodes of Yaga are available to stream Fridays on Crave in Canada and AMC+ in the US, with the final two episodes set for Nov. 27.

92duaw.title: GTA 6 Chapter 1 warning: Read this before finishing chapter 1 of GTA 6
92duaw.content: GTA 6 is finally rolling out around the world, and players everywhere are getting the first chance to spend time in Leonida.If you’re kicking off your adventure in Grand Theft Auto 6, then you should read this guide. GTA 6 Chapter 1 has a point of no return. While it’s only temporary, it does mean that there’s a sequence of missions in the game, that if you start them, you’ll be locked into them, and it will have a large effect on what you can do in GTA 6 for several hours.So read on to find our spoiler-free guide on when you’re approaching the point of no return in GTA 6 Chapter 1, and how long you’ll have to deal with the consequences.If you’re looking for in-depth walkthroughs, top tips and more on GTA 6, check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub. We’ll be constantly updating it as the week progresses, and eventually  it’ll be the most comprehensive place to read about GTA 6 around.Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.GTA 6 Chapter 1 Point of No ReturnThe point of no return in Chapter 1 is the mission Tourist Trap.In this mission, Jason and Lucia are tasked with going to collect a package from the visitor center. However, if you start this mission, what  you’re also doing is kicking off the end of Chapter 1.Chapter 1’s 3 final missions, Tourist Trap, Home Sweet Home, and Discharge Time are all connected. After you start this series of missions, something happens to Jason and Lucia that means that you won’t be able to roam the open world as both of them for several hours during Chapter 2.This also means that you’ll no longer have access to Jason’s vehicles that are part of the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition.So if you want to continue to explore before things change in Chapter 2, do not start the Tourist Trap. s41vvp.title: Michelle Monaghan, Justin Theroux to Star in ‘Sleepover’ for Blumhouse
s41vvp.content:
Michelle Monaghan and Justin Theroux are set to star in “Sleepover” from Blumhouse Atomic and Universal Pictures. The horror movie is set for theatrical release on Oct. 8, 2027.

“Insidious: Out of the Further” filmmaker Jacob Chase is directing the project from a script he co-wrote with “Night Swim” screenwriter Bryce McGuire. “Sleepover” is based on McGuire’s original short story. Plot details and further casting remain under wraps.

Variety exclusively reported in October that Parker Posey was set to star in “Sleepover,” but she has since dropped out of the project. Monaghan was cast in her place. Posey revealed the exit during a recent “Today” interview. When asked about the project, she told Craig Melvin, “I’m not doing it anymore … Something came up.”

Monaghan, known for roles in films like “Kiss Kiss Bang Bang,” “Source Code” and “Gone Baby Gone,” most recently starred alongside Robert De Niro and Adam Scott in the Netflix crime thriller “The Whisper Man.” Also for Netflix, she appeared in the buddy comedy “Little Brother” with John Cena and Eric Andre. On the horizon for Monaghan is Netflix’s hockey drama series “The Sticks,” which also stars Emilie Bierre and Shai Chase, and the third season of Apple TV’s “Your Friends and Neighbors.”

Theroux is no stranger to the horror genre. One of his best-known roles was playing the scorned movie exec Adam in David Lynch’s twisty masterpiece “Mulholland Drive.” More recently, he starred in “Beetlejuice Beetlejuice” as the manipulative TV producer boyfriend of Winona Ryder’s Lydia Deetz. His most recent big-screen credit was for “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” On the TV side, Theroux last starred in Netflix’s sports comedy “Running Point” and played the iconic post-apocalyptic capitalist Robert House in Prime Video’s “Fallout.” Upcoming projects for Theroux include “The Billion Dollar Spy” with Russell Crowe and Apple TV’s Siegfried and Roy miniseries “Wild Things.”

“Sleepover” reunites Chase and Blumhouse Atomic after “Out of the Further.” The sixth installment in the “Insidious” franchise opened in August to $60 million worldwide and went on to gross $169 million against an $18 million budget.

Jason Blum serves as producer. Chase and McGuire serve as executive producers, with Bea Sequeira serving as executive producer for Blumhouse and Lilly Tyson overseeing the project for the company. “Sleepover” is a Cinescape Entertainment production, presented by Universal Pictures and Blumhouse Atomic.

Monaghan is represented by Gersh, Anonymous Content, Entertainment 360, Narrative and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. Theroux is represented by CAA, Lighthouse Management & Media, Ingenuity Group and Toczek Suddleson Law Group.
