gh-1431547686.title: GitHub - galarianpikachu2021-hue/Racing-8-DX-Recomp: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe recompiled to run natively on your PC: no JIT, FSR 3.1 + frame generation, experimental DLSS, 720p to 4K output, HDR10. Bring your own game files.
gh-1431547686.content:
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, recompiled to run natively on your PC. Your own game, no emulator JIT, with modern upscaling and frame generation built in.
Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. You supply your own legally obtained game dump, keys and firmware; this project ships none of them,
and no recompiled game code either (see LEGAL.md). (KartRecomp is the launcher's name inside the project.)
Why it looks and runs better

Pick your resolution, natively
Output at 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4K, switched live from the in-game menu (F10, or both stick buttons). The game's own 3D scene is drawn at the size you choose, the HUD stays razor sharp, and textures follow the resolution (per-resolution LOD, bloom scaling).

Render scale 33% to 200%
Draw the 3D scene below native and upscale it for speed, at native with anti-aliasing (DLAA), or supersample up to 200%. The HUD is always drawn at full output resolution, after the upscale.

AMD FSR 3.1 upscaling
Temporal FSR 3.1 (AMD FidelityFX SDK, Vulkan) fed by motion vectors from the game's depth buffer and camera, plus exact per-object vectors for karts, characters and items from the game's own vertex shaders; camera jitter switches on automatically. Built-in FSR 1 and adjustable sharpening too.

FSR 3 frame generation, 2x
AMD's optical-flow frame interpolation on the HUD-free 3D image, with the HUD laid over each generated frame so it never smears. Measured in a scripted race: the game keeps its 58 to 60 fps, the display shows double. (Half a frame of added latency, like any interpolation.) A built-in interpolator is the fallback.

DLSS, experimental
DLSS upscaling and DLSS frame generation for NVIDIA RTX GPUs, through NVIDIA's public NGX SDK, as plugins you build yourself (plugins/dlss/). It is written and compiles, but our development machine has an AMD GPU: untested on real NVIDIA hardware so far, so expect rough edges and please report what you see.

HDR10 output
True HDR with adjustable paper white and peak brightness, tonemapped by us from the game's HDR scene, HUD kept at a sensible level.

Native renderer
The game's own graphics calls are translated straight to Vulkan (no emulated GPU): 60 fps races, 4-player split-screen, a sub-pixel jitter and depth-based motion vector pipeline that temporal upscalers need.

No JIT, ever
Every instruction of the game runs as ahead-of-time compiled code. A missing block is a bug to fix, never a fallback to a JIT.

Everything above is a row in the F10 menu. The launcher's Enhancements tab sets the starting values.
Honest status of each piece

Piece
State

working, used daily

FSR 3.1 upscaling plugin, FSR 3 frame generation plugin
working on AMD (RDNA 4) / Vulkan; the SDK is fetched, never committed

working

working (needs the display in HDR mode)

Windows: tested by the maintainer on an NVIDIA PC (you build the plugin yourself). Linux: the launcher's Set up NVIDIA DLSS button builds it on your PC; not yet run on an NVIDIA GPU on Linux

AMD's official Vulkan release (SDK 2.4.0, 2026-10-28): plugin in the Windows zip (AMD's signed DLLs, unmodified, with their licence), not yet run on an RX 9000; model select (FP8 / INT8 / lightweight INT8) in the in-game menu. See docs/WINDOWS_PLUGINS.md

Windows
supports Windows 10/11 64-bit (portable zip, built locally with MSVC)

How it works

Open the launcher (the AppImage on Linux). Its Setup page asks for your own files: the base game, the 3.0.4 update, optional DLC,
your prod.keys and your firmware. Each file is checked on the spot and a wrong one says why (an old 32-bit update, another game, a key
missing).

Build game turns them into the game on your PC. The AppImage carries everything it needs: the prebuilt engine, the exporter that
translates the game's AArch64 code into C, and a compiler. The tiered build (hot code optimised, cold code compiled fast) takes about
5 minutes on an 8-thread PC; a test boot then checks that every instruction runs as recompiled code (no JIT, ever) before Play
is enabled.

Nothing from the game is ever shipped: the translated code and your files stay in your own folders
(~/.local/share/kartrecomp, ~/.config/kartrecomp, ~/.cache/kartrecomp).

Play without the launcher (TV, controller, Steam): start it with --nolauncher (add -f or --fullscreen for fullscreen), e.g. Racing_8_DX_Recomp-x86_64.AppImage --nolauncher -f
or kartrecomp.exe --nolauncher (add that as a non-Steam game). The game starts with your saved settings; the in-game menu (F10, or
L3+R3 on a controller) has the graphics settings. The console language (the game's language) is on the launcher's Play tab.

The full recipe, including memory and time costs, is in docs/PIPELINE.md.

Building the launcher
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build

You need Qt 6 (Widgets, Network) and CMake 3.22 or newer.
Release builds: Linux packaging/linux/build-release-ubuntu2204.sh (podman, Ubuntu 22.04: engine, exporter, launcher and the AppImage);
Windows: built locally with Visual Studio 2022 and Qt 6.7 (steps in COOPERATE.md and docs/HANDOFF-WINDOWS.md). GitHub Actions only run by hand.
Credits
Built on the suyu/Eden emulator code (GPL-3.0), AMD FidelityFX (MIT) for FSR 3.1 and frame generation, NVIDIA's public NGX SDK for the DLSS
plugin (its libraries are never redistributed). Not endorsed by any of them.
Repository layout

patches/suyu/ our changes to the suyu fork (static explicit content + DLC, host hooks, native renderer)

gh-1387487521.title: GitHub - st4rwhx/Resident-Evil-4-Native-Port: Nightjar: Resident Evil 4 (GameCube) 100% native source port, byte-matching decompilation & standalone engine runtime for Android (32/64-bit), iOS (Metal), Windows, and Linux.
gh-1387487521.content:
Byte-Matching Decompilation, Standalone Engine Runtime & Multiplatform Port (GameCube)

Nightjar is a complete, 100% native source port, byte-matching decompilation, and standalone C++ engine runtime for Resident Evil 4 (Nintendo GameCube, G4BE08 / G4BP08) targeting modern mobile, desktop, and embedded operating systems: Android, iOS, Windows, and Linux.
There is no emulator. The original GameCube PowerPC code has been decompiled, matched byte-for-byte against the original compiler output, and recompiled into native machine code (AArch64, ARMv7-A, x86_64, x86) executing directly on bare metal. GameCube hardware subsystems (GX graphics, AX audio DSP, DVD, OS, Pad) are translated directly into modern platform APIs (OpenGL ES 3.0 / Apple Metal / OpenSL ES / AudioUnit / SDL2).

Important
Bring Your Own Game (BYOG) Policy
This repository contains NO copyrighted game assets, audio tracks, FMV cutscenes, textures, 3D models, or proprietary game binaries.
To play the game, users must supply their own legally dumped GameCube retail disc image (.iso, .gcm, or .rvz). The integrated Nightjar launcher verifies disc hashes against the Redump database (G4BE08 / G4BP08) and extracts the required data locally on your device.

Verified Uncut Live Proofs
To demonstrate real-world performance, stability, and zero-emulation execution, full playthroughs and development sessions were streamed live without cuts or scripts:

🎥 5h 39m Uncut Marathon Playthrough (Chapter 1 to Castle): Complete extended stress test with live frametime analysis and memory tracking.
🎥 2h+ Uncut Gameplay Session (Village to Chapter 2-3): Continuous uninterrupted playthrough on the release build with zero crashes.
🎥 UHD 2014 Texture Integration Live Stream: Live technical integration of high-resolution textures into the native runtime.
🎥 Drivable Police Car Mod Showcase: Demonstration of custom C++ gameplay modifications running in the native engine.

Emulation vs. True Native Port

Feature
Dolphin / Traditional Emulators
Nightjar Native Port

Execution Model
CPU JIT translation / Interpreter overhead
100% Bare-Metal Native Machine Code

Graphics Pipeline
Full GPU state emulation & shader compilation stutters
Direct GX $\rightarrow$ GLES 3.0 / Metal translation

Frametime
Variable 33–58 ms depending on room load
Halved to 16 ms in daytime village, 36 ms at night

Minimum Hardware
Modern high-end multi-core CPU & dedicated GPU
Runs at 30 FPS on a 2014 Galaxy S5 (ARM32)

Thermal Budget
High CPU/GPU drain, rapid thermal throttling
Extremely lightweight (~16 Mcycles/frame, console parity)

Door Transitions
Frequent 3–4 second freezes between rooms
0-second instant room transitions

Input System
Generic touch overlay mapping
Context-aware adaptive HUD + Direct Touch Inventory

Display Support
4:3 pillarbox or stretched widescreen
True native anamorphic 16:9 widescreen expansion

Audio Pipeline
Emulated DSP LLE/HLE threads
Multi-threaded native AX mixer with ADPCM decoding

Real Hardware Showcase

Running 100% natively on a 2014 Samsung Galaxy S5 (Snapdragon 801/805, 32-bit ARM) in the village, locked at 30 FPS with custom touch HUD.

Mobile Ergonomics & Adaptive Touch Controls

On Android and iOS, the virtual HUD adapts seamlessly based on the in-game state without cluttering the screen:

Exploration Mode: Floating virtual analog stick, double-tap auto-run, quick 180° turn button, contextual action/open button.
Combat & Aiming Mode: Over-the-shoulder free-aim touch zone, laser sight adjustment, fire and reload buttons.
Interactive QTEs: On-screen prompts morph dynamically to show only the exact action requested (e.g. boulder evasion, boss reaction triggers).
Direct Touch Attaché Case: Drag, drop, rotate, and organize weapons, herbs, and ammunition directly with your finger on the touchscreen.
Radial Quick-Equip Menu: Switch between primary weapons and equipment in real-time without pausing the action.

Modern Quality-of-Life Enhancements

True 16:9 Anamorphic Widescreen: Expanded horizontal field of view without black bars, stretching, or vertical cropping.
Wii Edition Pointer Free Aiming: Full mouse cursor aiming on PC and touch laser aiming on mobile, where bullets hit exactly where the reticle points.
Resolution Scaling up to 8x: Internal rendering resolution scales from original 480p up to full 4K / UHD.
Multi-Region & Format Support: Compatible with both Retail USA (G4BE08) and Retail Europe (G4BP08) Disc 1 and Disc 2 images directly in .iso, .gcm, and .rvz (Dolphin compressed format) without extraction.
Virtual Memory Card Parity: Seamless import and export of GameCube .raw memory card files, fully functional at all typewriters.
12 Built-in Languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, and more.
Gamepad Support with Vibration: Native rumble feedback for Xbox, PlayStation DualShock/DualSense, Switch Pro, and standard Bluetooth controllers.

Monorepo Architecture
Resident-Evil-4-Native-Port/
├── src/ # Byte-matching decompiled game logic (992 translation units)
├── include/ # Game structures, engine types, and SDK interfaces
├── port/ # Platform abstraction layer (OS, DVD, VI, Audio, GX/GLES hardware)
├── runtime/ # Nightjar engine runtime (Launcher, AX mixer, ImGui frontend)
├── android/ # Android NDK build system, RE4Activity, touch overlays
├── ios/ # iOS Xcode project, CAEAGLLayer Metal bridge, touch overlays
├── recomp/ # Static analysis and recompilation engine (njrecomp)
├── tools/ # Decompilation tools, symbol extractors, build verification
├── images/ # Project banner, screenshots, and visual documentation
├── CMakeLists.txt# Unified root build configuration
├── BUILDING.md # Step-by-step compilation manual
├── LEGAL.md # Bring Your Own Game (BYOG) policy & CC0 license
└── README.md # Project overview and documentation

Technical Pillars

Byte-Matching Decompilation (src/):

992 Translation Units: 673 units in main.dol and 319 units across 110 dynamically loaded REL overlays match byte-for-byte against the original compiler output (GCC 2.95.3 / SN Systems ProDG & CodeWarrior).
10,383 Debug Symbols: Recovered directly from the unstripped GameCube Debug Prototype (November 25, 2004) via custom symbol recovery pipelines.
Cross-Architectural Reference: Cross-referenced against the PlayStation 2 Review Debug ELF (.mdebug section with 12,658 procedures and 701,913 local symbols) and Wii Edition call graphs.
Strict Verification: Every translation unit is compiled and verified against original disc binaries using decomp-toolkit and objdiff.

Graphics Hardware Translation (port/gx/):

Direct Hardware Translation: Replaces Nintendo GameCube GX FIFO command lists with direct modern draw calls.
Custom TEV Shader Generator: Translates the GameCube's 16-stage Texture Environment (TEV) register combiners dynamically into optimized GLSL (OpenGL ES 3.0) and MSL (Metal) fragment shaders.
Accurate Texture Formats: Full native hardware decoding for GameCube CMPR (DXT1/BC1), RGB5A3, RGBA8, IA8, and I4 formats.

Multi-Threaded Audio Architecture (port/audio_port.cpp):

Replaces the GameCube Macronix DSP with an asynchronous, multi-threaded native software mixer.
High-performance decoding of GameCube 4-bit ADPCM audio streams directly in C++.
Full support for original stereo separation and Dolby Pro Logic II surround sound downmixing.

Quick Start (Playing)

Obtain a pre-compiled build for your platform:

Android: Install Nightjar.apk.
iOS: Sideload Nightjar.ipa using AltStore, TrollStore, or Xcode.
Windows: Run Nightjar.exe.
Linux: Launch ./nightjar.

On first launch, the Nightjar Launcher will prompt you to select your legal GameCube disc image (.iso, .gcm, or .rvz).
The launcher automatically validates disc integrity, extracts the necessary assets locally into your private application storage, and launches the native port.

Building from Source
Comprehensive build instructions for all supported operating systems are documented in BUILDING.md.
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/st4rwhx/Resident-Evil-4-Native-Port.git
cd Resident-Evil-4-Native-Port

# 2. Build for Windows (x86_64 / x86)
cmake -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64
cmake --build build --config Release

# 3. Build for Android (arm64-v8a or armeabi-v7a)
./android/build_apk.sh arm64-v8a

# 4. Build for iOS (arm64)
xcodebuild -project ios/RE4Native.xcodeproj -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos

# 5. Verify Decompilation Accuracy
python3 configure.py && ninja

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Is Nightjar an emulator?

No. An emulator runs a virtual PowerPC CPU and simulates GameCube registers and memory mapping at runtime. Nightjar is a native C++ port: the original code was reconstructed via byte-matching decompilation and compiles directly to native AArch64 (ARM64), ARMv7-A (ARM32), and x86_64 machine instructions. Hardware calls (GX, AX, DVD) are replaced by modern native APIs.

Do I need a high-end smartphone to play?

No. Nightjar was specifically engineered and profiled on a 2014 Samsung Galaxy S5 (Snapdragon 801/805, 32-bit ARM). Because there is no emulation overhead, the engine consumes only ~16 Mcycles/frame (the actual power budget of a GameCube). Modern devices run the game effortlessly with minimal battery drain and zero thermal throttling.

Can I import my saves from Dolphin or a real GameCube?

Yes. Nightjar reads and writes standard GameCube memory card raw image files (.raw). You can copy your existing Dolphin save file directly into the application's save folder and continue your playthrough.

Which game versions are supported?

Nightjar includes multi-region support in a single unified binary, supporting both Retail USA (NTSC-U, G4BE08) and Retail Europe (PAL, G4BP08) Disc 1 and Disc 2. Supported formats include uncompressed .iso, .gcm, and compressed .rvz.

Does Nightjar support mods and HD textures?

Yes. Nightjar includes an integrated texture replacement pipeline capable of loading high-definition textures by hash, as well as custom gameplay mods (such as the drivable police car mod).

1pqqbob.title: Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
1pqqbob.content:
Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO.

At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.

Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.

However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”

With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.

$104.8 billion. That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.

Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.

Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day.

28% stake to Amazon and Google combined. All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company. Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropic because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup, it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.

The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.

More than $1 trillion. As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.

Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030. And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.

All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future. This was a huge IPO. But it is a pricey business to run.

1k2e0as.title: Tyra Banks Taps Andy Vallentine To Direct Sally Hansen Film
1k2e0as.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Tyra Banks’ SMiZE Productions has tapped Andy Vallentine (The Mattachine Family) to direct the as-yet-untitled Sally Hansen feature, which Deadline announced was in development last year.

In addition to his directing work for Hollywood, Vallentine also has a background creating visually bold work for major beauty brands including Sephora and MAC Cosmetics, touts a release from SMiZE Productions. His experience fits into the Sally Hansen world of vintage Hollywood glamour, beauty, fashion, and color.

The film follows a team determined to uncover the woman — chasing clues, rumors, and myths to reveal the real Sally Hansen, while juxtaposing her untold story against today’s global nail obsession. Blending beauty with business intrigue, the film explores how Hansen built one of the industry’s most enduring empires decades before “beauty influencer” was even a phrase — and how her legacy still shapes the $50-billion nail market today.

“I’ve always been drawn to tenacious, impossible stories. Sally Hansen built a beauty empire, and like so many women before and after her, she was nearly written out of history anyway. I’ve spent my career directing campaigns for beauty brands like Sephora and MAC, and now I can’t wait to turn the camera around to tell her unbelievable story and the real-life search to find her,” Vallentine said.

Added Banks, “Andy has this incredible visual imagination and a deep understanding of storytelling, plus a real connection to the beauty world, to bring all of that to life. I want people to know Sally the woman, not just Sally the bottle.”

SMiZE Productions’ global slate includes scripted, unscripted, live theatre, and ice-cream-themed entertainment projects in the U.S., Canada, and Australia, with additional announcements slated through 2026.

Vallentine is repped by Heroes and Villains.

gh-1464619673.title: GitHub - CouldntFindit/korra-recomp: WIP - native Android and Windows port of The Legend of Korra (2014 PC) by static recompilation. Bring your own copy; source-only.
gh-1464619673.content:
Static recompilation of the 2014 PC release of The Legend of Korra
(PlatinumGames / Activision, LoK.exe, x86-32, Direct3D 9) into portable C.
LoK.exe ──pcrecomp lift32──▶ generated C ──▶ Win32 compatibility runtime
──▶ Direct3D 9 (DXVK-Native / Vulkan) ──▶ Windows x86 and Android arm64

No emulator, no interpreter for the game's own code: every function of the
original binary is translated ahead of time, and this project supplies the host
side (Win32, D3D9 surface, XInput, XAudio2, CRI/Wwise audio, Steam stubs).

Work in progress — pre-alpha. Nothing is playable yet and there are no
releases. The Windows host currently boots the engine and renders through the
intro movies; the main menu is not reached yet. The milestone table below is
the source of truth for what works today.

This repository contains no game content. You must own and supply your own
copy of the PC game. Builds are produced locally by each builder from their own
files; nothing derived from the game binary is published here.

Status
Last updated 2026-11-19. Current focus: M2 — the movie-to-menu transition and
the XAudio2 stub blocker.

Milestone
What it means
State

M0
Environment, toolchain pin, repo bootstrap, PE gate
done (2026-11-19)

M1
Seeds + function catalog + full lift to C
done: 37,029/37,029 functions, 0 lift failures — see docs/LIFT_REPORT.md

M2
Boots to the main menu on Windows (no Steam, silent, movies skipped)
intro movies, title screen and menus render; the pad drives them. Open: menu text does not draw, and the new-game transition crashes on a null manager (sub_00603C00). Ladder state in docs/HOST.md, log in docs/FINDINGS.md

M3
Boots and plays the first area on an Android arm64 device
not started (NDK not installed)

M4
Audio: Wwise + CRI behind a host mixer
spec ready (docs/audio.md), implementation not started

M5
Gameplay validation, framerate hooks, full playthrough
not started

Parallel research tracks (each has its own document):

Track
Scope
State

A
Audio stack inventory → the M4 spec
done + independently confirmed (44/44 assertions) — docs/audio.md

B
CPK archives + USM movies → M2.10 and optional movies
done + independently confirmed (45/45) — docs/assets.md

C
Ghidra subsystem triage → M2 hooks and M5 frame pacing
done — docs/quirks.md

D
Host shims: steam_api + silent XAudio2 2.7 COM
done, selftest 54/54 — docs/xaudio2_callsites.md

E
Publishing: mirror script, README/notices upkeep
done — docs/PUBLISHING.md

Exact toolchain pin and per-milestone findings: docs/TOOLCHAIN.md,
docs/FINDINGS.md. Working rules for contributors and
agents: AGENTS.md.
Building
Everything is generated from your own copy:
# 1. Toolchain: the pinned pcrecomp (commit + patch series, see docs/TOOLCHAIN.md)
git clone https://github.com/sp00nznet/pcrecomp.git ..\pcrecomp
cd ..\pcrecomp; git checkout -b korra-base 35548b8
# then apply the nfsu2 patch series 0001-0014 + the MP2 SEH patch
# (recipe and patch list: docs\TOOLCHAIN.md)

# 2. Analysis copy of the game binary. LoK.exe's relocation directory is already
# valid, so this verifies and copies it byte-for-byte; it would repair a
# binary that is not. The copy lands in work\ (gitignored).
python tools\prepare_analysis_exe.py "D:\Games\The Legend of Korra\LoK.exe" work\LoK.analysis.exe

# 3. Seeds, catalog, lift (about 15 minutes on this machine)
python scripts\run_korra_lift.py catalog work\LoK.analysis.exe work\seeds_all.json work\catalog.json
python scripts\run_korra_lift.py lift work\LoK.analysis.exe work\catalog.json src\recomp\gen

# 4. Windows host (needs the x86 C++ toolset)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build_host.ps1 -Jobs 8
build\korra_recomp.exe "D:\Games\The Legend of Korra"
Requirements: Python 3.12+ with capstone and pefile for the committed tools
(unicorn / keystone-engine are used by pcrecomp's own self-checks); Visual
Studio 2022 with the x86 C++ toolset for the Windows host; Android NDK r27+ for
the Android target (not set up yet). Details in
docs/TOOLCHAIN.md.
Publishing
Releases are source-only — no APKs, no binaries, no game data, no generated
recompiled code. This GitHub repository is the project's home and its hosted
copy; it is pushed at each milestone. A Codeberg failover script is kept in the
tree in case a second host is ever wanted:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\sync_codeberg.ps1 -DryRun # check
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\sync_codeberg.ps1 # push
It refuses a dirty tree, a non-Codeberg host, a non-fast-forward and any tracked
file the content guard rejects. Policy, setup, release checklist and
troubleshooting: docs/PUBLISHING.md.
Legal
Unofficial fan interoperability project. Not affiliated with Activision,
PlatinumGames, Nickelodeon or Viacom. The Legend of Korra is a trademark of its
respective owners. Original code here is GPL-3.0; see LICENSE and
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
Development
This project is developed with AI coding agents under human direction. Most of
the tooling, documentation and analysis here was agent-produced, then verified —
independently, against the shipped game files — and merged at the owner's
decision. The verification runs and their results are recorded in
docs/FINDINGS.md.

gh-1440373375.title: GitHub - springah/zuma_recomp: Zuma (Xbox 360/XBLA) static recompilation for PC on the ReXGlue SDK -- boots to the title screen; no game data included
gh-1440373375.content:
⚠️ Disclaimer — built with heavy use of AI. The recompilation, port code,
tooling, and documentation in this repo were developed largely with the assistance
of AI coding tools (large language models). It's a hobby project: verify things
yourself before relying on them, and expect rough edges. No warranty.

A static recompilation of Zuma (PopCap / Oberon Media, Xbox 360 XBLA, 2005)
for native PC execution, built on the ReXGlue SDK
(a Xenia-derived runtime + PPC→C++ recompiler).
Status: early, but it plays. On Windows with the Xenos D3D12 renderer the
port boots to the title and runs past it. Tested so far (2026-11-20, keyboard
only):

Adventure: stage select, the instruction pages and the first level —
aiming, shooting, matches, scoring and losing a life all work.
Gauntlet: plays through to its Game Over screen.
Menus: the main menu, pause menu, Options (both volume sliders, which are
saved) and Help work; Return to Arcade closes the game cleanly.
Achievements: the menu entry opens the achievements list (the D-pad or
left stick scrolls, B closes it).

Not tested yet: finishing a level, anything after the first level, and a real
controller. Known gap: Leaderboards only shows the game's own "Xbox Live
members only" message.
Three bugs have been fixed on the way: an FP-exception crash on host-side
threads (SDK fork), a libjpeg setjmp/longjmp round trip (routed through the
SDK's host jmp_buf), and a crash on exit when the game quits itself (SDK
fork) — plus the host VSync fix shared with the sibling ports (present_vsync).
Latest release: v0.1.3 (Windows), a pre-release bundle attached to the
GitHub release.
It contains no game data: unzip it and follow RUN.txt inside to add your own
package. The older v0.1.1 crashes on the way out when you choose Return to
Arcade or start it without game files; use v0.1.3. See
CHANGELOG.md.
No copyrighted game files are included. This tree excludes the extracted game
directory, default.xex, images and build outputs — you supply your own legally
obtained Zuma XBLA package. See Legal below.
This is one of a family of Xbox 360 recomps built on the ReXGlue SDK; zuma pins a
tagged SDK release as a submodule, like its sibling ports (daytona, futari, gh,
guwange, sdoj, sotn). Per-OS build and packaging notes are in PORTS.md.
Prerequisites

Tool
Version
Notes

CMake
3.25+

Ninja
any
winget install Ninja-build.Ninja

LLVM / clang
20+
Standalone LLVM; zuma builds with the clang++ (GNU) driver targeting the MSVC ABI

Python
3
runs scripts/extract_game.py

Git + Bash
any
scripts/regen.sh is a bash script

Windows: the clang++ build targets x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, so it needs the
MSVC headers/libs + Windows SDK on INCLUDE/LIB (a "x64 Native Tools" command
prompt sets these, or let build.ps1 enter one for you).
Linux: Clang 20+, GTK3 dev headers (libgtk-3-dev / gtk3), and X11/XCB
interop (libx11-xcb-dev / libx11 / libX11-devel). The SDK renders via XCB;
on Wayland, XWayland must be running.
Game files
Zuma on Xbox 360 is an XBLA title delivered as a single LIVE/STFS content
package. On your console's storage it sits at
Content\0000000000000000\584107EF\000D0000\<40 hex digits> (a file with no
extension whose first four bytes read LIVE). Copy that file into game/ and
extract it from the repository root:
python3 scripts/extract_game.py
This unpacks the package into extracted/ (the runtime game data, passed via
--game_data_root) and copies the shell executable to assets/default.xex (the
codegen input). game/, extracted/, and assets/ are gitignored. On Windows,
dragging the package onto extract_game.bat does the same, except that it
unpacks everything into assets/ beside the executable (the release-bundle layout).
The package this tree was prepared against: title ID 584107EF, 27557888 bytes,
sha256 10026be53823dcf3bf9718850cfa1802a2b1c6430d1847e3c89c74371e1d45b6
(default.xex 4038656 bytes).
Build
The short road (Windows): build.ps1
git clone -c core.symlinks=true --recurse-submodules https://github.com/springah/zuma_recomp
cd zuma_recomp
.\build.ps1 -GameSource "D:\path\to\your\content\package" -Run
build.ps1 (or a double-click on build.bat) does steps 1–4 below in one go:
it fetches missing submodules and repairs libmspack's symlinks, installs any
missing tool through winget, enters the x64 developer environment, builds the
ReXGlue CLI, extracts your package into extracted/ + assets/default.xex
(skipped when both already exist), runs scripts/regen.sh, and builds the
win-amd64-release preset. -Config Debug or RelWithDebInfo picks another
preset; -NoInstall reports missing tools instead of installing them.
1. Clone (SDK included)
git clone -c core.symlinks=true --recurse-submodules https://github.com/springah/zuma_recomp
The ReXGlue SDK is a submodule at thirdparty/rexglue-sdk, pinned at a tagged
release (currently v0.9.2 plus six commits, branch zuma/fpscr-host-threads of the
springah/rexglue-sdk fork; see PORTS.md). To develop against a live SDK checkout
instead, set REXSDK_DIR at configure time; when unset, the build uses the submodule.

Windows: clone with -c core.symlinks=true (as above) or the SDK's
libmspack submodule checks out its symlinks as plain text files and the build
fails in lzxd.c.

2. Build the ReXGlue CLI (for codegen)
cmake --preset win-amd64 -S thirdparty/rexglue-sdk -B thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/out/build/win-amd64
cmake --build thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/out/build/win-amd64 --config Release --target rexglue
# -> thirdparty/rexglue-sdk/out/win-amd64/Release/rexglue.exe (regen.sh finds it
# automatically, falling back to a ../rexglue-sdk sibling build)
3. Regenerate the recompiled code
scripts/regen.sh
This runs rexglue codegen zuma_manifest.toml, emitting generated/
(rexglue.cmake + generated/default/ with the recompiled C++). zuma is a
single-module title, so this is one codegen pass. Function-entry seeds the
analyzer can't discover on its own go in zuma_functions.toml. generated/ is
gitignored.
4. Configure & build
cmake --preset win-amd64-release # or linux-amd64-release / mac-arm64-release
cmake --build --preset win-amd64-release
out/build/win-amd64-release/zuma.exe --game_data_root=extracted
A zuma.ini is written next to the executable on first run (display, graphics,
storage and log settings).
Legal
This repository contains no game data. The recompiled output in generated/ is

1my35xx.title: Bill Hader Horror Movie 'They Know' Acquired by Black Bear
1my35xx.content:
Black Bear has acquired the North American rights to Bill Hader‘s feature directorial debut “They Know.” Hader also wrote and stars in the horror-thriller with Linda Cardellini.

Based on an idea from Hader and his “Barry” collaborator Duffy Boudreau, “‘They Know’ follows a divorced dad who becomes increasingly suspicious and paranoid that his ex-wife’s new mysterious partner is exerting a strange, unsettling influence on their children,” according to an official logline. Further plot details and casting remain under wraps.

Hader serves as producer with Bob Graf under his Hanarply banner. Alyssa Donovan is co-producer. MRC fully financed the film, which is currently in post-production. FilmNation Entertainment is acting as the worldwide sales agent. “They Know” marks the second collaboration between Black Bear and MRC following the studio’s acquisition of “Honeymoon/Funeral,” which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival.

“Bill Hader is a singular talent both in front of and behind the camera, and he has delivered a film in ‘They Know’ unlike anything we’ve ever seen,” said Michael Heimler, president of production & operations at Black Bear. “’They Know’ is authentic, original and bold filmmaking at the highest level, and we couldn’t be more excited to partner with Bill and re-team with our great friends at MRC, who consistently deliver boundary-pushing films that help define their genre.”

Hader, outside of his eight-season run on “SNL,” is best known for his HBO series “Barry.” The squirmy dramedy about a contract killer with dreams of becoming an actor won 10 Emmys over its four-season run. Hader served as the star and directed several episodes. His most recent big screen bout was voicing the Cat in the Hat in the Warner Bros. adaptation of the classic Dr. Seuss storybook.

Cardellini recently took home her first Emmy for her performance in HBO’s “DTF St. Louis.” She’s also newly leading the cast of Peacock’s “Friday the 13th” prequel series “Crystal Lake” as the soon-to-be-slasher Pamela Voorhees. Her last film role was in Netflix’s family comedy “Nonnas.”

Black Bear recently released the fantasy romance “Wicker,” starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård. The studio’s upcoming films include Guy Ritchie’s “Wife & Dog,” starring Benedict Cumberbatch, Rosamund Pike and Anthony Hopkins; David Leitch’s “Jason Statham Stole My Bike,” starring Jason Statham and Hannah Waddingham; Nahnatchka Khan’s “Honeymoon / Funeral,” starring Rebecca Ferguson and Greta Lee; “A Woman in the Sun,” starring Renée Zellweger and Sissy Spacek; “Jonah,” starring Lee and Cooper Hoffman; and “Atmosphere,” written and directed by Anna Boden & Ryan Fleck, based on the bestselling book by Taylor Jenkins Reid.

MRC recently released “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York” with John Turturro, “The Love Hypothesis” and “Wuthering Heights.” Upcoming MRC titles include “The Gallerist,” “A Place in Hell” and “Eloise.”

Deadline was the first to report Black Bear’s acquisition of “They Know.”

1gcm6z8.title: Lakers’ Photo Book Includes Magic Johnson Handprints: Shop Online
1gcm6z8.content:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

The Los Angeles Lakers’ $100 coffee-table book is getting a five-figure upgrade.

Luxury art-book publisher Taschen and the Lakers have unveiled two limited-edition versions of “Lakers: An Official History of the Purple & Gold,” featuring original handprints from Showtime-era legends, authenticated hardwood from the former Staples Center court and exclusive artwork signed by Magic Johnson and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.

The new releases, announced Thursday, are limited to 1,100 copies worldwide, with 1,000 Collector’s Editions priced at $2,400 each and just 100 Art Editions retailing for $9,600.

LIMITED RELEASE

Lakers: An Official History of the Purple & Gold

Both versions include the original 528-page book, housed in a custom leather clamshell box designed by Jeff Hamilton, the fashion designer known for his elaborate leather jackets commemorating the Lakers’ championship victories in 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2020.

Each box also contains an authenticated piece of hardwood from the original Staples Center floor, where the Lakers won five championships and Kobe Bryant played his final NBA game. Collectors will receive an original handprint from one of seven Showtime-era figures — Johnson, Abdul-Jabbar, James Worthy, Michael Cooper, Kurt Rambis, Byron Scott or Pat Riley — with the identity revealed upon delivery.

The $9,600 Art Edition takes things a step further, adding a large-format print of Ernie Barnes’ “Fastbreak,” originally commissioned by the Lakers in 1987. The 41-by-24.5-inch artwork depicts the team in the midst of its Showtime era and features seven signature plates hand-signed by the players and coach portrayed in the painting. Each print is numbered and authenticated by the Estate of Ernie Barnes.

The limited editions arrive nearly two months after Taschen released the standard version of the book in September. Abdul-Jabbar wrote the foreword, Lakers governor Jeanie Buss contributed the introduction and former coach Phil Jackson penned the afterword. Other contributors include Johnson, O’Neal, Pau Gasol, LeBron James, Luka Dončić, Jack Nicholson, Paula Abdul, Flea and Lou Adler.

“The Lakers have had an extraordinary impact on basketball and pop culture, and we wanted this book to capture the full scope of that influence, from the game itself to art, fashion, music, and beyond,” Tobak said in a statement. “The Limited Edition takes that vision a step further, bringing together rare memorabilia, artwork, and personal contributions from the people who helped shape the team’s history.”

Both limited editions are available now through Taschen’s website.

tnsoc9.title: Experimental compound burns fat without sacrificing muscle
tnsoc9.content:
A new approach to weight loss could help the body burn more fat while preserving muscle, potentially overcoming one of the major drawbacks of existing obesity treatments. Researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, have identified a compound that increases the amount of energy the body uses rather than simply reducing how much food a person eats.
In experiments with mice, the compound improved blood sugar regulation, reduced harmful blood fats, and helped obese animals lose fat without a significant reduction in lean muscle mass. It also increased energy expenditure by up to 18%, even though the mice did not become more physically active or experience an increase in body temperature.
The findings, published in Science Advances, suggest a promising new direction for treating obesity, diabetes, and fatty liver disease. The experimental compound also appeared to enhance the benefits of popular weight-loss medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy when the treatments were used together. However, its effectiveness and safety have not yet been established in humans.
A Different Approach to Weight Loss Than Ozempic
Over the past five years, medications known as GLP-1 drugs have transformed the treatment of obesity and other metabolic conditions, including diabetes and fatty liver disease. Drugs marketed as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound have helped many patients achieve substantial weight loss while improving their ability to regulate blood sugar.
Despite these benefits, the medications have important limitations. Nausea and other digestive problems can make treatment difficult for some patients. Because these drugs reduce appetite and food consumption, they can also increase the risk of inadequate nutrition and loss of muscle mass. Over time, losing too much muscle can contribute to weakness, frailty, and other health complications.
Berkeley researchers wanted to investigate a fundamentally different strategy. Rather than focusing on reducing calorie intake, they explored whether it would be possible to increase the amount of energy the body burns.

This process, known as energy expenditure, includes the calories used to maintain basic bodily functions, regulate metabolism, and support everyday activities. Increasing energy expenditure could potentially help people lose weight without relying exclusively on eating less.
"Body weight responds to two levers: taking in fewer calories, or spending more energy," said Anders Näär, a professor of metabolic biology and nutrition at UC Berkeley and senior author of the study. "GLP-1s work almost entirely on the first, so we went after the second."
A Compound That Burns Fat While Preserving Muscle
The researchers focused on a molecule called 5-tetradecyloxy-2-furoic acid (TOFA), which has an unusual combination of effects on the body's metabolism.
TOFA interferes with the production of lipids, a broad category of fatty substances that includes cholesterol and triglycerides. These molecules serve important functions, but excessive levels of certain lipids can contribute to metabolic disorders and cardiovascular disease.
At the same time, TOFA activates genes involved in taking up and burning fat for energy. This combination allows the compound to influence both how the body produces fat and how it uses fat as fuel.

In mice, treatment with TOFA produced several encouraging results. The animals became more sensitive to insulin, the hormone that helps move glucose from the bloodstream into cells. Improved insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to control blood sugar, an important benefit for people with diabetes or insulin resistance.
The compound also lowered triglyceride levels and improved characteristics of fatty liver disease, a condition in which excess fat accumulates inside liver cells and can eventually interfere with liver function.
Perhaps most notably, obese mice treated with TOFA lost weight primarily through reductions in body fat, without experiencing significant losses of lean muscle mass. This distinction could be especially valuable because maintaining muscle is important for strength, mobility, and long-term metabolic health.
How TOFA Increases Energy Burning by 18%
Although TOFA was originally discovered in the 1970s, the new research uncovered additional properties that could make it particularly useful for treating metabolic disease.
The compound belongs to a group of substances known as ACC inhibitors. These compounds interfere with enzymes that help the body manufacture fatty acids, effectively slowing the production of certain fats.
Other ACC inhibitors have previously advanced to mid-stage clinical trials, but none has been approved to treat metabolic diseases. One major obstacle has been an unexpected side effect: many of these compounds increase triglycerides in the blood, potentially raising the risk of heart problems.
The Berkeley team discovered that TOFA does more than inhibit ACC. It also activates two cellular receptors called PPARα and PPARδ, which help regulate the genes responsible for fat metabolism.
These receptors function as molecular switches. When activated, they stimulate processes that allow cells to absorb fatty acids and break them down to produce energy. In effect, TOFA simultaneously reduces the production of certain fats and encourages the body to burn fat that is already available.
In mice, this activity increased energy expenditure by as much as 18%, without requiring additional physical activity or raising body temperature. Unlike other ACC inhibitors, TOFA also did not cause triglyceride levels to rise, potentially because of its additional effects on fat metabolism.
"TOFA appears to engage a coordinated metabolic response," said study first author Justin Y. Lee, a postdoctoral student at UCSF who conducted the research as a Ph.D. student at Berkeley. "It is not simply blocking lipid synthesis. It is also activating energy expenditure pathways that may help the body handle excess lipid and glucose more effectively."
To understand whether these effects could be reproduced with separate treatments, the scientists gave mice a combination of two different compounds. One blocked lipid production, while the other stimulated energy expenditure.
Surprisingly, this two-compound approach was less effective at improving overall metabolic health than TOFA alone. The finding suggests that TOFA's ability to influence multiple metabolic processes through a single molecule may be an important part of its effectiveness.
Could TOFA Make Ozempic and Wegovy More Effective?
The researchers also investigated whether TOFA could improve the results of existing GLP-1 medications.
They tested the compound alongside semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, as well as tirzepatide, which is marketed as Mounjaro and Zepbound.
These medications primarily help people lose weight by reducing appetite and food intake. TOFA, by contrast, targets the other side of the energy balance equation by increasing how much energy the body expends.
When the researchers combined TOFA with these medications in mice, the results were more favorable than those produced by either treatment alone. The combinations led to greater improvements in body weight, blood glucose regulation, insulin levels, and triglycerides.
This suggests that treatments targeting calorie intake and energy expenditure could potentially work together to produce stronger metabolic benefits.
"In our combination experiments, TOFA worked additively or synergistically with the GLP-1 appetite-suppressing drugs, so we view it as complementary rather than as a replacement," Näär said.
In other words, the researchers do not necessarily envision TOFA replacing medications such as Ozempic or Wegovy. Instead, it could eventually become an additional treatment that helps address obesity and related metabolic conditions through a different biological mechanism.
A Promising Discovery, but Human Trials Are Still Needed
Despite the encouraging results, the researchers emphasize that TOFA remains an experimental compound. All the findings so far come from animal studies, and scientists have not yet established whether it is safe or effective in humans.
Further research will be necessary to determine whether the same metabolic improvements can be achieved in people and whether the treatment could offer meaningful advantages over existing medications.
To help move the research toward potential clinical applications, the Berkeley scientists have established a biotechnology company called ReRx Therapeutics. The effort has received support from the university's life sciences entrepreneurship network, including Nucleate and Berkeley SkyDeck.
If the findings eventually translate to humans, TOFA could represent an important addition to the growing range of treatments for obesity and diabetes. By encouraging the body to use more energy while helping preserve muscle, the compound points toward a potentially different way to achieve healthier weight loss.
The research was funded through discretionary resources provided by UC Berkeley, with additional support from the UCSF Liver Center and the University of Michigan Animal Phenotyping Core.
Additional authors include Chi Zhu, Melissa A. Boldridge, Rachelle L. Stark, Lei Xu, Federico Gonzalez, Xin Tang, Kaitlyn T. Dang and Kook Son of Berkeley; Gracia Bonilla, Kashish Chetal and Ruslan I. Sadreyev of Massachusetts General Hospital; Kosuke Watari and Michael Karin of the University of California, San Diego; Christina Papa and Bilal N. Sheikh of the Helmholtz Center Munich; Prabha Ibrahim of ReRx Therapeutics.

1c0u14x.title: Dermot Mulroney On How Filming ‘The Family Stone’ Sequel Feels Like Life Imitating Art: “So Moved”
1c0u14x.content:
More than 20 years later, The Family Stone sequel has become a real-life family reunion of sorts for the cast of the 2005 holiday movie.

Dermot Mulroney, who reprises his role as Everett Stone in the upcoming sequel The Families Stone, recently expressed that he’s “so moved to be reunited” with his “incredible, incredible” co-stars from the original Thomas Bezucha-written/directed film.

“Everybody’s had this remarkable career advancement and paths since we were all together,” he told Entertainment Weekly. “So we’re making a movie about a family returning all together for the first time in years and years, and we’re doing that in real life too, returning and reuniting with this incredible cast.”

Mulroney added of his onscreen brother, “Luke Wilson and I always had a real tight thing going, so that snapped right back into place.”

The Families Stone picks up 20 years after the death of Diane Keaton’s character, matriarch Sybil Stone — something that was depicted in the original film — as the Stone family again reunites for Christmas, only to face the season’s biggest surprise: their father (Craig T. Nelson) has unexpectedly invited the woman (Jean Smart) he’s fallen in love with to meet the family.

Following Keaton’s death at age 79 in October 2025, Bezucha revealed that he was writing the sequel, which was set at Searchlight in September and is now filming in New York. In addition to Mulroney, Nelson and Wilson, original cast members Claire Danes, Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker, Tyrone Giordano, Elizabeth Reaser, Paul Schneider and Brian White are returning.

5iy3uq.title: Lance Broadway Dead: ‘Agents Of S.H.I.E.L.D.’ Actor Was 43
5iy3uq.content:
Lance Broadway, a former Major League Baseball pitcher-turned-actor who appeared in Marvel’s “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.,” has died at 43.

Broadway was found dead on Nov. 17 in an apartment complex stairwell in Dallas, Texas, according to the Dallas County Medical Examiner. His cause of death is pending autopsy results.

Broadway was a pitcher who played for the Chicago White Sox and New York Mets. He made his feature film debut in 2013’s “Olympus Has Fallen” as Secret Service Agent O’Neill under President Benjamin Asher (Aaron Eckhart).

His television career included appearances on “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.,” “Lucifer,” “Saint George,” “Kevin From Work” and “Real Husbands of Hollywood.” His most recent credit was on two episodes of USA Network’s “Colony” in 2016-17.

Broadway was cast as Commander Linden in “Teleios,” which was later renamed “Beyond the Trek,” in 2014. The science fiction thriller was released as a TV movie in 2017. He was cast as Devon in the short film “Shattered Reflections” in 2015.

Born in Bryan, Texas, Broadway was an all-district baseball player in high school and went on to pitch for Dallas Baptist University. He transferred to Texas Christian University, where he was named conference pitcher of the year before being selected 15th overall by the Chicago White Sox in the 2005 Major League Baseball draft. He made his Major League debut in 2007 and was traded to the New York Mets in 2009. He signed a minor league deal with the Toronto Blue Jays that same year but never played for the team.

13n1evx.title: How to see if your bargain SD card or USB drive is fake on Ubuntu
13n1evx.content:
F3 (Fight Flash Fraud) is an open-source tool to check if a USB drive or SD card has the capacity it claims on the label. If you’ve used h2testw on Windows, this does the same thing on Linux.

Memory card and USB drive prices have more than doubled this year, and that makes cheaper listings more tempting. But buying low-cost storage has always carried a risk of fakes (not to mention low-quality or slow chips).

Dodgy brands and marketplace sellers often sell drives whose capacity is below what the labels says. Your computer falls for the trick, done in the storage device’s controller, and reports the falsified value, say, 512GB, even if it’s really only 32GB.

You only find out it’s fake when a file you thought you’d saved won’t open. Because most of these fake drives carry on accepting files even when it has nowhere to put them (it bins off what it can’t hold or writes over data it does hold), you won’t notice during transfer.

A Windows developer, peeved with countless counterfeit capacities, created h2testw in 2008 to help others detect the phoney flash.

If you need an h2testw alternative for Linux, F3 implements the same test algorithm in an open-source package, albeit lacking a GUI.

Install F3 on Ubuntu

F3 can be installed with one command on Ubuntu (Linux Mint, Zorin OS, et al):

sudo apt install f3

But as F3 is a set of command line utilities, not a desktop app with a GUI, you won’t find a shortcut for it in the application launcher.

F3 gives you two ways to check a drive.

You can use f3write and f3read in sequence. The first will fills your drive’s remaining free space with test files and the second verifies that all the data that should be there is. This method is a bit slower overall, and may increase write wear.

Working a bit faster is f3probe. This tests the drive directly, writing data in a different way to tell you if the capacity the controller reports is legit. This tool is more useful on larger storage devices (it can take a while to write 256 1GB files).

Regardless of which tool you try, if you are testing a device with contents you can’t afford to lose, copy off anything you want to keep before you begin – don’t just nod and think “sure”; do it just in case.

Do not COPY any example drive paths as yours will be different.

Run a quick check with f3probe

Checking for a fake USB drive on Linux

Plug your device in and make a note of its drive path via lsblk.

When using f3probe you need to pass it the full device path, not a partition mount, e.g., you’d give it /dev/sdb rather than /dev/sdb1 or /dev/sdb2.

sudo f3probe /dev/xyz

The process of checking can take up to 15 minutes depending on the memory’s write speeds, but in most cases it should be fairly brisk. Leave it to do its thing and, once it’s done…

If your device is all it should be, f3probe confirms this in the terminal with a “good news” string:

Good news: The device `/dev/xyz' is the real thing

If not, you’ll see a string that says:

Bad news: The device `/dev/xyz' is a counterfeit of type limbo

The counterfeit output will also show a command you can run to “fix” the drive, which creates a partition for its actual size, no the size the reprogrammed storage controller reports.

Run a fuller check to verify

Read and write is slower, but thorough

You can use f3write followed by f3read for a thorough test of your drive’s capacity. This writes to and reads out every available block.

When you use f3write and f3read you need to give it the drive’s mount point (the folder it shows up as in your file manager). This is often something like /media/username/DRIVE, and not the /dev/ path you use for f3probe.

As aways, you can look at the output of lsblk to see this.

Open your terminal and run:

f3write /media/device/

The device’s remaining free space is filled with 1GB files, named something like N.h2w. The CLI shows a progress bar so you know how long it’ll be before it completes. This method can be slower than f3probe on large capacity devices.

Once the writes are done, run f3read on the same mount point:

f3read /media/device/

Now, f3read reads those files back and checks them against what was written. Anything the drive discarded or overwrote to ‘pretend’ it’s larger than it is shows up as damaged or corrupted.

Once done, delete the test files off your device to get the space back.

And if the drive is fake?

If you see a different value to the one you’d expect… Well, I hope you kept the receipt or can claim a refund, as you haven’t received what you thought you’d bought.

If you want to keep the drive, but have its true value shown, the f3fix tool can create a partition that reflects the real capacity. The command to run for this is shown in the output of f3probe, but only if a counterfeit drive is detected.

Even so, it would be wise not to rely on a counterfeit card or stick if the capacity is off, as it’s more than likely the quality of the flash chips holding data is iffy too.

1mnkpeo.title: Playbill Apologizes for Casting Ad for 'George Floyd the Musical'
1mnkpeo.content:
Playbill is apologizing for running an ad for singers for a cast album called “George Floyd the Musical” from the Busted Broadway company.

The project drew numerous negative comments from Broadway stars and many others. Busted Broadway responded on its social media Thursday that “The project ‘George Floyd the Musical’ is NOT making light of, condoning, or mocking the horrific 2020 murder of George Floyd. It’s a satire on the CULTURE, rather than the person. Never judge a show by its title, as many who have never seen the script or score appear to be doing now.”

The theater publishing company Playbill wrote in a public apology, “Late yesterday afternoon, Playbill Jobs incorrectly approved a job listing that had no place on our site. Once leadership was alerted, the listing was immediately removed, and we began reviewing and revising our approval processes. We apologize unequivocally for giving this hateful listing any further air, and we promise to do better going forward. We at Playbill aim to lift up this community with empathy, consideration, and respect. We hope those who read and follow us do the same.

“We know this listing has upset and offended many, and the fact that it made it onto our site has disappointed those who trust us as an outlet,” the post continued.

“For that, we are sorry, and are committed to regaining your trust,” the apology concluded.

Busted Broadway “brings you musical cast recordings that are too ridiculous, too raunchy and too absurd to see the stage,” according to its website. “Busted Broadway is not for the mollycoddled or politically correct listener,” says the company which has produced projects for “Human Centipede: The Musical” and “Genghis Khan: The Musical.” The company lists that “George Floyd: The Musical” is coming soon, according to its website, with the tagline “The $20 bill that changed the world.”

Playbill said in a statement that going forward, it would ban Busted Broadway from posting ads and would not write about their projects, according to Deadline.

1hnb09q.title: Google’s 3D emoji has wild Android spec requirements: 10GB of free space, 6GB RAM
1hnb09q.content:
Google introduced 3D emoji on Pixel this year, and has just detailed the minimum specifications required to get them on your Android phone.

Noto 3D emoji goes from vector-based 2D emoji to a high-resolution bitmap font. This results in “high-resolution designs” for emoji “with more texture and dimension to characters and icons.” Google has an FAQ section about why the new emoji might look low resolution: 

Vector vs. bitmap rendering: Older Android emoji used 2D vector graphics, which scale infinitely to any size without losing resolution. The 3D emoji are bitmap graphics, which are pre-rendered pixel-based images. When these images are scaled up by an app or zoomed in, the pixels stretch, which can cause a softer or lower-resolution appearance.

The Google support article published this week lists the minimum specs your Android device must have to get 3D emoji:

Run Android 17 or later.

Be from supported manufacturers receiving system or Google Play services updates.

Have at least 6 GB of RAM

Have at least 128 GB of total storage & 10 GB of available space.

The last two bullet points are rather surprising. In fact, Google even lists instructions for checking how much memory and storage your device has: 

Check your RAM (Memory):

Open the Settings app and search for “RAM” or “Memory.”

Tap SystemDeveloper optionsMemory.

On some phones, you may have to tap Device care Memory.

Your device must have 6 GB of RAM or higher to use the 3D emoji.

Check your device storage:

Open the Settings app and search for “Storage.”

Tap Storage

Check your total storage and available space:

Total storage: Your device must have 128 GB of storage or higher

Available space: Your device must have at least 10 GB of available space

In terms of availability, Google says a supported device will “automatically download the 3D emoji when it’s on Wi-Fi and charging.”

At this time, there isn’t a way to force download the emoji.

Google announced 3D emoji in May, with the new design shipping on the Pixel 11 in August. It has since arrived on older Pixel devices.

In terms of OEM availability, Google explicitly says “Samsung devices use a proprietary emoji font and do not receive the 3D font update.” Additionally: 

This is also true for third-party messaging apps, such as WhatsApp, who use their own emoji fonts rather than relying on your device’s system font.

1o2i6sp.title: “I’m in Preparation for the End of Our World”: Golshifteh Farahani on Art, War and Her Tallinn Premiere
1o2i6sp.content:
Golshifteh Farahani (Alpha, Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales) is Leila, a young widow seeking a fresh start in Kabul, Afghanistan, in writer-director Chabname Zariab’s debut feature When She Hears the Bells (Les Clochettes de Kaboul).

The France-based Iranian actress is attending the 30th edition of Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF), where the film had its world premiere on Wednesday night in the First Feature Competition. On Thursday, she talked to The Hollywood Reporter about the film and its call to stand up for human rights.

After all, Leila soon finds out that the kitchen she works in is a so-called bacha bazi house. These are establishments in which boys and young men are forced to dress in women’s clothes and dance for entertainment — regularly followed by sexual exploitation. Set in 2021, the film also sees the Taliban moving ever closer to Kabul. Leila tries to flee while helping a group of boys escape before the city falls. Sayed Hashimi (13 Days, 13 Nights) co-stars in the thriller, which includes images actually shot in Afghanistan. Le Pacte is handling sales.

Farahani talked to THR in Tallinn about When She Hears the Bells, why the film can speak to the Western world and why she isn’t spending time thinking about her next project.

How did you find out about this film and decide to star in it?

Chabname wanted me for some time, but I wasn’t reading the script because I was thinking I’d done The Patience Stone [set in war-torn Afghanistan]. So, it’s a space for other actresses to do that. But she insisted and insisted and insisted, and at the end she said, “We’re not going to do the movie [without you].” So, I ended up accepting the part without reading the script. I called her and said, “Let’s do it.”

I couldn’t believe that this was Chabname’s first feature script and her directorial debut.

When I read the script, I was also really surprised. It was amazing. The script is as good as the movie.

When She Hears the Bells combines thriller elements with the humane and emotional elements. How hard is that combination for you as the star?

I’m happy that I could see that it works because I’m very objective when I watch my movies. I know when it’s bad and it doesn’t work, and I know when it’s good. Last night [during the premiere], I could feel this works because I constantly had goosebumps over goosebumps over goosebumps. I felt, “Yeah, the emotion works.” For one of my friends, it is impossible to watch a movie without checking his phone. It was the first time I watched him not touching his phone, and at one point he just [leaned] forward. He was really engaged, and that was the best sign. The movie works. It really works.

There are all sorts of dark issues and threats in When She Hears the Bells. There is the bacha bazi, the situation of women, the encroaching Taliban. Do you see these as sharing any common themes?

The way I always look at it is that you’re telling a story. It’s just that the story is about horrible things. I think about the character who is actually in that situation, which is terrible. From the outside, when you watch it, it is unbearable. But the character is in it, so, as the character, I don’t judge it as horrible. It’s just that I’m living in that horror.

As an audience, you say, “This is awful, this is horrible!” But as a character inside, you cannot say this is horrible. You just act on it.

Do you have any hopes for what audiences will take away from the film?

If the audience is moved by it and asks questions, if the movie is seen and appreciated, it’s enough because so many of these movies can be so boring and so much.

How so?

These subjects are too much for the white man to even comprehend. Because sometimes the horror is too much for the civilized world. They can’t even handle it. So they zap [it out] subconsciously.

But I think this movie works because it doesn’t show the actual horror. If you saw the horror [committed against] a little boy in the film, the audience would zap. But because it’s all left to the imagination, it keeps the white audience on a fine line of sitting and watching and feeling it, not blocking out the feeling.

This is the third year in a row that you have a film here at Tallinn. How much do you like the city and the festival?I love Tallinn, and I think the festival is great. I think people come here to watch movies, and the fact that this festival exists is a blessing because we all know the situation of the world and the budgets, and there are always challenges for these little festivals. But I come back to Tallinn anytime they ask me because I think it’s a great festival. I have had three movies here: Reading Lolita in Tehran, Oh, What Happy Days!, and this one.

Is there anything you can share about any potential next projects?

I’m a bit pessimistic, and I feel there’s a big war coming. So, in my head, I feel we just need to prepare for a war. My headspace is not much in the artistic world, because I feel the situation of the world is so bad, and I feel that humanity needs to be prepared for war. Especially in Europe, people have been so spoiled, and I think the first place that is going to be completely smashed is Europe. So, in my headspace, I’m in preparation for the end of the world, the end of our world. I think we’re going to enter a new order.

Who would start the war, or where?I just feel the world is going to go upside down. The world has become a minefield. No matter where you go, something is going to explode everywhere — every region you think of: America, Los Angeles, Florida, Africa, Europe, China, Taiwan. Everywhere you go, you might step on a mine, and it might explode. You just need to prepare.

gh-1359485937.title: GitHub - chiikabu/the-browsing-of-isaac: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ recompiled to WebAssembly, playable in the browser.
gh-1359485937.content:
The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+, playable in a browser tab.

This is the real Repentance+ game code, recompiled from the Windows executable
to WebAssembly. It's not a remake and not an emulator, so every item, synergy
and bug works the way it does on PC.
It runs on desktop and on phones, keeps your saves in the browser, and can
install mods from the game's own MODS menu.
On a phone

There are no extra buttons on screen; you play by touching the game.

Move, shoot
Left thumb, right thumb

Active item, card or pill, bomb
Tap it in the bar under the room

Swap items
Tap the small second item

Drop a card or trinket
Hold it

Map
Tap the minimap, or hold it to peek

Pause
The paper icon next to the map

Menus
Tap a row to pick it, tap it again to choose it; swipe to scroll

Back
The BACK note in the corner, or two fingers

Cutscenes
Tap to skip

Held upright, a pad under the picture also moves through the menus; tap it to
choose. Switching to another tab pauses the run.
Vibration follows the game's Rumble option.
On a keyboard

Key

W A S D
Move

← ↑ → ↓
Shoot

Space
Active item

Q
Card or pill

E
Bomb

Ctrl
Swap, hold to drop

Tab
Map

Esc
Pause

F
Fullscreen

`
Debug console, in a run (the key left of 1), once it is switched on

The debug console is the game's own (stage 5, giveitem c1, debug 3...). It is
off until you ask for it: in the game's Options list, go down to Console and
turn it on like any other option. (It takes the place of Streamer Mode, which is for
online play and does nothing here.) With it on your save still earns its
achievements; a run in which you use it is the game's to judge, as on PC.
On a controller
Plug in a controller (USB or Bluetooth), press any button so the browser sees it,
and start the run with it: the game gives player one to whichever device starts
the run. Buttons are the Xbox layout, sticks are analog, and rumble follows the
game's Rumble option. On the MODS screen, X opens the mod browser.

Mods

Mods from the Steam Workshop run here too, Lua and all. Open the game's
MODS screen and click MOD BROWSER (press B, or tap it on a
phone): search the catalogue, read what each mod does, and install it. The game
restarts with the mod loaded. A mod you already have can be added from a
.zip.
Saves
Saves stay in the browser you play in. EDIT FILE on the file select screen
exports a save or imports one, including a .dat save from PC. Deleting a file
asks first.
Browsers
Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers, on desktop or Android. If your browser
can't run it, the page says so.
Building it yourself
You need your own copy of the game; this repository has no game files in it.
docs/DEVELOPING.md covers the build.

y30rcm.title: How to make money in GTA 6
y30rcm.content: What is the best way to make money in GTA 6?GTA 6 is finally here and players around the world are getting a chance to jump in to the world of Grand Theft Auto 6 after 13 years. However in GTA 6, money isn’t easy to get early in the game, and as such players have been looking for a way to make money fast in GTA 6.In this guide we’ll list the best ways to make money and GTA 6 from early game stick-ups which you can do almost from the start of the game, to later-game bank robberies which will yield the highest rewards but are also the most difficult.If you are enjoying GTA 6 you should check out our GTA 6 Guides Hub and make sure you bookmark it. We will be updating that hub every day for the forseble future with new guides new walkthroughs and everything you need to know about Grand Theft Auto 6.Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.How to make money in GTA 6Stick-UpsRobbing groceries stores in Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the fastest ways to make money though you might not make a lot of it. Every groceries store in the game can be robbed. You can do this by going up to the cashier and sticking them up with a weapon. To do this approach, the cashier and hold the L2 button.This will aim your gun at the cashier without firing however at this point you can now interact with the cashier and threaten them which will cause them to open the cash register. You won’t get a lot of cash doing it this way, however there is little police response when you rob groceries stores. Some grocery stores also have a safe in the back room or you can access by kicking down the door or forcing the employee to open it for you.If that safe has a code you can often find the code on a post-it note located near the safe, or you can threaten the employee and you will get an option to ask them about the safe code. Eventually the police will be contacted and they will turn up at the store but by that point you should be long gone.It’s also worth noting that a lot of grocery stores have secret rooms of that sometimes include gang activity. you can tell if one of the grocery stores has a secret room by checking the minimap if there is a room that you haven’t accessed yet try picking the lock off the door or going back outside and checking another entrance.Gang Hideouts and DrugsWhen you first get the ability to sell drugs, you can start robbing gang hideouts which often contain large amounts of  various drugs that sell for a lot of money. This is by far one of the best ways to make money in GTA 6. The type of drug that the gang hideout is hiding has a huge effect on what it is worth for example things like weed are fairly cheap, but things like crystal and cocaine are far more expensive.You will know you are near a gang hideout because when will drive past and a yellow icon will appear on your map. At this point it is worth checking out what is there and if you check on the map you can also see the valuables that are available and that gang hideoutIf you steal drugs from a gang hideout you will have to physically take them to somewhere that you can sell them. However, later in the game if you do a lot of drug selling, some buyers will allow you to drop the drugs and a garage. Keep in mind, however, they will arrange a pick up and this means they will take a bigger cut of the money.Pawn Shops and Jewelry StoresRobbing jewellery stores and pawn shops is also a great way to make money in GTA 6. Howeverm these jewelry stores and pawn shops often have a high level of security so you are going to want to do some reconnaissance before you attempt to rob them.A lot of jewelry shops can be accessed from the back of the shop, where you will also be able to disable their security systems or if they have CCTV camera footage,  you can destroy it.  Doing this will delay the response time of the police, which is important because stealing from jewelry shops or pawn shops gets you a higher wanted level than stealing from a grocery store.Main Story MissionsOne of the best ways to make money and Grand Theft Auto 6 is by completing main story missions. Often these main story missions will give you a big chunk of cash, so it’s worth doing as many of them as you can.This also applies to side missions which often provide you with a lot of cash. Just remember to take it to the bank to put in your account or it could be a lost if you are arrested or die. If you don’t have a bank account yet, check out our guide to Buck Me. Selling CarsAnother great way to make money in GTA 6 is to sell cars. You will gain the ability to sell cars to Moses when you reach chapter 2 of GTA 6. He will take cars that do not have a tracker on them. On average you will get between $1000 and $5,000 dollars per car that you sell to Moses.After you sell a car to Moses there is a cooldown period where you can no longer sell cars to him however if you sleep at the safe house this cooldown period will elapse. Later in the game you can sell higher value cars to another prominent side character that is introduced and a later chapter .Bank RobberiesThe ultimate way to make money and Grand Theft Auto 6 is to rob a banks.  You won’t be able to rob banks straight away, in fact you will have to wait until you get the dye pack jammer during a mission where you rob a bank with a prominent side character. After this, you can rob banks whenever you like and it is by far the easiest way to make a huge amount of money in the game.Bank robberies are split up into several sections. There are basic cash drawers which you can get by threatening the tellers, there are safe which hide large numbers of marked bills, and then there are the bank vaults which house the largest amounts of money and in the game.With that being said, because of the amount of money you can get from robbing a bank, actually robbing a bank is also one of the most difficult things to do in the game. The police response is huge as soon as they are called so make sure you’re escape plan is well fought through because you will have a huge wanted level from the second that you leave the bank.
