5q7iwn.title: 'Outer Banks' Alum Madelyn Cline to Join New 'Serendipity' Movie
5q7iwn.content:
Madelyn Cline is in final talks to join the new “Serendipity” film in the works at for Amazon MGM Studios and Miramax, Variety has learned exclusively from sources.

The project is described not as a reboot of the 2001 romantic comedy but rather an update in a modern setting featuring new characters. Cline would join previously announced cast members Milo Manheim, Whitney Peak, Stephen Kalyn, and Auliʻi Cravalho. Exact character and plot details are being kept under wraps.

Reps for the studio declined to comment.

This would mark the latest major film role for Cline. She is also set to star opposite Glen Powell in the upcoming Judd Apatow comedy “The Comeback King,” which is slated to release in theaters on Feb. 5, 2027. She will also appear in “The Day Drinker” opposite Johnny Depp and Penélope Cruz, with that film hitting theaters March 26. Her past film credits include 2025’s “I Know What You Did Last Summer” and “Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery.”

In television, Cline is best known for her role in the hit Netflix drama “Outer Banks,” on which she starred as Sarah Cameron throughout the series’ six-season run at the streamer. She has also appeared in shows like “Stranger Things” and “Vice Principals.”

Cline is repped by CAA, Entertainment 360, Bold Talent Agency, imPRint, and Hirsch Wallerstein Hayum.

Michael Showalter is attached to direct “Serendipity.” Marc Klein, who wrote the original film, will pen the screenplay and executive produce. Showalter is also a producer alongside Jordana Mollick for Semi-Formal Productions. Simon Fields, who produced the original, is also a producer. Jonathan Glickman, Alexandra Loewy, and Thom Zadra will executive produce for Miramax. Arianna D’Andrea is overseeing the project for Miramax, while Emily Crook is overseeing for Semi-Formal.

The original “Serendipity” starred John Cusack and Kate Beckinsale. In the film, their characters meet one night in New York and decide to leave the chance of meeting again up to fate. They ultimately go searching for each other years later despite being in relationships with other people. The film was a box office success, grossing over $77 million on a reported budget of $28 million.

blkyl4.title: Hollywood’s Top 25 Legal Troubleshooters
blkyl4.content:
Skip to main content

Legal Eagles D4vd was flanked by attorneys Blair Berk (left) and Marilyn Bednarski.

Ted Soqui — Pool/Getty Images

Criminal charges, custody fights, contested fortunes — meet the lawyers who handle the problems agents can’t negotiate away

November 20, 2026

Logo text

In Hollywood, having a lawyer on speed dial can mean only one of two things. A deal is imminent, or a jury is deliberating. If it’s the latter, chances are the attorney on the other end of the line is on this list.

The 25 Legal Troubleshooters on these pages handle the problems agents can’t negotiate away: criminal charges, custody fights, contested fortunes and who gets to sell the Lakers. Their firms represent stars, moguls and heirs, although lately the L.A. Public Defender’s Office has been giving them unexpected competition. The lawyers themselves are attracting attention, too. Brian Steel has a Drake song named after him; Laura Wasser has a fashion campaign. Others spend their days explaining why a chatbot shouldn’t rewrite your trust.

All are worth keeping in your contacts. Just in case.

Marc Agnifilo, Karen Friedman Agnifilo and Teny Geragos

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (3)

Agnifilo Intrater LLP

Criminal Defense Litigation

This firmspent the year representing famous clients facing charges of murder, rape and sex trafficking. Agnifilo and Geragos followed their defense of Sean “Diddy” Combs with Harvey Weinstein’s third trial, which ended in a hung jury, while another client, Oren Alexander, Kim Kardashian’s former real estate broker, was convicted of sex trafficking alongside brothers Tal and Alon. (Tal was represented by Deanna Paul, now a partner at Geragos & Geragos.) Friedman Agnifilo, meanwhile, helped take the death penalty off the table for Luigi Mangione, then pressed to dismiss his state murder case on double jeopardy grounds following his federal plea. But the firm’s most incendiary client this year has nothing to do with Hollywood: Winston Lee is one of seven former Cornell fraternity members accused in a civil suit of drugging and gang-raping a fellow student.

Patrick Baghdaserians

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Baghdaserians Law Group Inc.

Family Law Litigation

Actor Olivier Martinez had Baghdaserians in his corner during his headline-grabbing custody battle with ex-wife Halle Berry. In October, the lawyer secured a temporary restraining order and primary physical custody of their 13-year-old son. The judge later dissolved the restraining order but kept Martinez the primary custodial parent. Martinez is now seeking increased child support and $240,000 in legal fees from Berry. Another custody client: Basketball Wives’ Clayanna Warthen, whose dispute involved former NBA player Andre Iguodala.

Blair Berk

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Berk Brettler LLP

Criminal Defense Litigation

Berk’s clients sit on both sides of criminal cases: She has represented stalking victim Jennifer Aniston and defended Harvey Weinstein. She says three-quarters of her practice involves preventing charges from being filed. But singer D4vd’s murder case was impossible to keep quiet. Berk defended him against charges of killing 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez before withdrawing Aug. 31, when he qualified for a public defender — a growing trend in Hollywood (see Alan Jackson).

Lisa Bloom

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Bloom Fudali

Civil Litigation

Two music cases, two different codas. Bloom’s firm settled Lauren Pisciotta’s harassment and assault suit against Kanye West in July, ending a two-year fight. But former Danity Kane singer Dawn Richard’s suit accusing Sean “Diddy” Combs of sexual assault and physical abuse was dismissed because most claims were filed too late. Bloom’s targets also include the FBI: Eight Jeffrey Epstein survivors she represents sued the bureau for allegedly failing to investigate reports of his abuse.

Richard S. Busch

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Adams & Reese LLP

Copyright Litigation

After winning “Blurred Lines” for Marvin Gaye’s family, Busch is taking on artificial intelligence. In October, he sued Anthropic on behalf of Elvis Presley’s rights holders, including Authentic Brands Group, alleging its Claude models trained on 274 Presley songs without permission. The demand: up to $41.1 million — or about $150,000 per song. Anthropic disputes the claims. Similar suits for music publishers Reservoir Media and Round Hill have made Busch a recurring adversary for the AI company.

Jeffrey Eisen

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Mitchell Silberberg & Knupp LLP

Trusts & Estates Law

More than 10 years after his death, Muhammad Ali is still one of Hollywood’s most active clients, and Eisen is the lawyer guarding his name. In January, the U.S. Postal Service issued an Ali Forever stamp, a milestone for an estate that the firm’s trusts and estates co-chair has helped steer through years of name-and-likeness deals. His firm’s other clients: Marilyn Monroe, Elvis Presley and Albert Einstein.

Drew Findling

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

The Findling Law Firm

Criminal Defense Litigation

Findling and co-counsel Brian Steel dismantled the government’s murder-for-hire case against rapper Lil Durk, winning acquittals on all five counts. Findling argued that Durk’s former assistant, testifying for the prosecution, was himself the “mastermind,” urging jurors to see a “tsunami of reasonable doubt.” Afterward, 50 Cent dubbed him the “Billion Dollar Lawyer.” His client list also includes Cardi B and President Donald Trump.

Bryan Freedman and Mitchell Schuster

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (2)

Liner Freedman; Meister Seelig & Schuster PLLC

Civil & Commercial Litigation

Freedman wielded the machete and Schuster the scalpel for actor-director Justin Baldoni in his battle with It Ends With Us co-star Blake Lively. His $400 million countersuit failed, but her harassment claims were dismissed, and the two sides settled without a payout. Lively later won $407,000 for defending against Baldoni’s defamation claim — just 5 percent of her $8 million legal-fee request, which Freedman called a “significant victory.”

Thomas Giuffra

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Rheingold Giuffra

Civil Litigation

The lawyer for accusers of Harvey Weinstein and Sean “Diddy” Combs is now representing the woman at the center of the Cornell fraternity rape case. Giuffra’s suit alleges seven fraternity members drugged and gang-raped her and that Cornell failed her. As the case exploded online, his client faced threats, doxing and swatting, while supporters rallied under #IAmJaneDoe to protect her identity. New York Attorney General Letitia James is overseeing a criminal investigation.

Shawn Holley and Kate Mangels

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Kinsella Holley

Civil & Criminal Litigation

An O.J. Simpson “Dream Team” alum, Holley represented pitcher Tyler Skaggs’ family in its wrongful death case against the Angels, arguing the team failed to stop an employee supplying players with drugs. The club settled during jury deliberations. Alongside Mangels, she also helped record label Del Records cut a proposed federal fine — for doing business with a sanctioned, cartel-linked concert promoter — from $6.7 million to $1.8 million. Restraining orders are also a specialty; the two have secured them for Cindy Crawford, Kaia Gerber and Lana Del Rey.

Ambika Kumar

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Davis Wright Tremaine

Technology & Media Litigation

When gamers take their grievances to court, Kumar represents the companies behind the screens. She reps Microsoft and Mojang, creator of Minecraft, in suits accusing game companies of hooking children. Her clients also include Tinder and Hinge, for which she secured dismissals in two cases alleging the apps failed to remove user profiles and messages. She also helped technology trade group NetChoice keep key provisions of California’s age-appropriate online design law blocked on appeal.

Alan Jackson (and the L.A. County Public Defender’s Office)

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Werksman Jackson

Criminal Defense Litigation

Jackson, who has defended Harvey Weinstein and Kevin Spacey, exited as Nick Reiner’s attorney in January. That notorious patricide-and-matricide case is now being handled by what’s rapidly turning into Hollywood’s hottest new legal shop — the L.A. County Public Defender’s Office. Not only is public defender Kimberly Greene now representing Reiner, but her colleagues Walid Kandeel and Lisa Roth took over singer D4vd’s murder defense from Blair Berk in August. Jackson, meanwhile, is teaming with former client Karen Read for a true-crime podcast, Read Between the Lines, debuting in early 2027.

Sarah Moses and Esra Hudson

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (3)

Manatt, Phelps & Phillips LLP

Civil Litigation

Hudson and Moses didn’t just get Justin Baldoni’s $400 million countersuit against Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds thrown out; they helped stick him with $407,000 of Lively’s legal bill, securing the first federal court award under California’s law protecting sexual harassment accusers from retaliatory defamation suits. Moses helped draft the motion; Hudson led Lively’s team. Lively’s own claims ended in a settlement without a payout.

Luke Nikas and Alex Spiro

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (2)

Quinn Emanuel

Criminal & Civil Litigation

Nikas won $102.2 million for the Morgan Art Foundation against publisher Michael McKenzie over unauthorized and altered works based on Robert Indiana’s LOVE — the familiar sculpture with the tilted O. He calls it the largest art-litigation verdict on record. His partner Spiro had more mixed results with client Elon Musk: Delaware’s Supreme Court reinstated his roughly $56 billion Tesla pay package, but a San Francisco jury found he misled Twitter investors.

Deanna Paul and Mark Geragos

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject; Gotpap/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images/Getty Images

Geragos & Geragos APC

Criminal Defense Litigation

Some brothers fared better than others. Paul defended celebrity realtor Tal Alexander against charges that he and his siblings drugged and sexually trafficked women. The jury convicted all three, and each received a 30-year sentence. Geragos had more luck with the Lyle and Erik Menendez, helping them secure a new parole hearing roughly 17 months ahead of schedule after the brothers were denied release last year. His TMZ appearances stirred up some controversy, though, with Geragos’ comments on the Cornell fraternity rape case prompted the accuser’s lawyer to allege that he was effectively assisting the defense team, which includes his daughter, Teny, at Agnifilo Intrater. Geragos denies it.

Kevin Reddington

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Kevin Reddington Law Office

Criminal Defense Litigation

He doesn’t represent Hollywood actors or battle for studios, but the 75-year-old Massachusetts attorney did become one of 2026’s biggest reality stars. His livestreamed defense of Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing her three children, inspired more than 16,500 TikTok videos under his hashtag, autograph requests outside court and fan-made “Better Call Kevin” merch. Reddington argued Clancy was not criminally responsible due to postpartum psychosis. The jury deadlocked in September.

Mathew Rosengart

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Greenberg Traurig LLP

Media & Entertainment Litigation

After helping Britney Spears escape her conservatorship, Rosengart fought for FKA twigs to reclaim her voice, winning an agreement lifting restrictions on discussing her sexual abuse allegations against ex-boyfriend Shia LaBeouf. He’s also defending Selena Gomez against investors who accuse her of failing to deliver on commitments to build and promote her mental health startup, Wondermind.

Kristina Royce

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Blank Rome LLP

Matrimonial & Family Law

Royce has handled splits for Arnold Schwarzenegger, Channing Tatum and Forest Whitaker. Now she’s representing Lori Loughlin, whose marriage to Mossimo Giannulli survived the college admissions scandal and prison terms for both but ended in separation after nearly 28 years of marriage, with Loughlin filing for divorce in September.

Martin “Marty” Singer

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Singer Weinsten

Entertainment & Business Litigation

A letter from Marty Singer has ruined many a Hollywood morning. In November, he accused filmmaker Yi Zhou of harassing Jeremy Renner after she alleged the actor sent explicit messages and threatened to call ICE. He also represented Priscilla Presley against former business partners who accused her of concealing a $25 million jewelry collection; they dropped that suit in February, retaining the right to refile. In March, Lavely & Singer became Singer Weinsten Wolf & Jonelis, adding three longtime partners to the firm’s name.

Brian Steel

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

The Steel Law Firm, P.C.

Criminal Defense Litigation

Most lawyers hope for a referral. Steel got a Drake song named after him. After representing Young Thug and joining Sean “Diddy” Combs’ defense, the Atlanta attorney teamed with Drew Findling to win Lil Durk acquittals on all five counts in his federal murder-for-hire trial. Fans swarmed him outside court after the verdict. Durk remains jailed ahead of a separate racketeering trial in August 2027.

Robert Strauss and Jonathan Forster

Weinstock Manion

Trusts & Estates Law

Strauss and Forster help Hollywood’s wealthy pass fortunes to the next generation, minimizing estate taxes and planning for the transfer of family businesses. Lately, some clients have acquired another adviser: a chatbot. Strauss told CNBC that clients are uploading trust documents to AI, then returning with suggested revisions that can take hours to review. “I have not actually received a single workable suggestion from that process,” he says. The firm is updating its contracts to warn that sharing confidential documents with AI “lawyers” could jeopardize attorney-client privilege.

Adam Streisand

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Sheppard

Trusts & Estates Law

After helping secure Lachlan Murdoch’s control of Fox and News Corp, Streisand moved to another family power struggle: Jeanie Buss versus her five siblings over whether to sell the family’s remaining 17.8 percent Lakers stake. Her brothers and sister want to cash out alongside billionaire Mark Walter, who bought control of the team in 2025 and has agreed to sell to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner at a $12.5 billion valuation. Buss wants to retain the shares. A hearing is set for Dec. 8.

Laura Wasser

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Wasser Cooperman & Mandles

Family Law

Wasser doesn’t just handle divorces; she models for them, fronting fashion label Reformation’s “Divorce Collection” campaign this year. For Sia, she filed an October settlement keeping the singer the primary custodial parent of her toddler with Dan Bernad, who receives $42,500 a month in child support. Her newest client is Hila Klein, who filed to divorce husband and H3 Podcast co-host Ethan Klein on Nov. 2 after publicly accusing him of an affair.

Douglas Wigdor

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Wigdor LLP

Employment Law

Wigdor is leaving no stone unturned in Julia Ormond’s ongoing sexual assault suit against Harvey Weinstein — pursuing Disney, Miramax and CAA for allegedly failing to protect her. His firm even won an order requiring former CAA chairman Michael Ovitz to answer questions under oath about the agency’s representation of the actress. Other clients include Cassie Ventura, whose rape and sex trafficking suit against Sean “Diddy” Combs settled a day after filing. The firm is also suing Leon Black, alleging the financier filed retaliatory lawsuits to intimidate lawyers representing his sexual assault accusers.

Laura Zwicker

Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject

Greenberg Glusker

Trusts & Estates

For Zwicker’s wealthy clients, moving away can be as complicated as passing a fortune down. Alongside estate planning for entertainers and multinational families, she advises on the tax consequences of changing countries. California, for one, doesn’t surrender its taxpayers easily. She told The San Francisco Standard that auditors examine ATM withdrawals and Apple Pay transactions to determine whether residents have really left — or just their tax bills. “They want to see all of the data on all of your devices,” she says.

1lc2tfr.title: Microsoft представила предварительную версию RDMA через USB4 для объединения ПК в локальный ИИ-кластер
1lc2tfr.content:
RDMA (удалённый прямой доступ к памяти) даёт одной системе возможность читать или записывать разрешённую память другой с меньшим участием операционной системы и процессора, чем при обычных сетевых соединениях. Microsoft адаптировала API Windows NetworkDirect для работы через USB4. В демонстрации используется форк llama.cpp, который распределяет выполнение модели между подключёнными компьютерами.
Практическая мотивация — модели с открытыми весами, которым требуется больше памяти, чем есть в одном настольном ПК или ИИ-системе. Разделение модели между машинами позволяет запускать более крупные нагрузки без переноса всей задачи в облако или создания серверного кластера. Совокупные GPU также вносят вклад в вычисления, хотя результат зависит от конкретных видеокарт, доступной памяти, пропускной способности и способности модели эффективно распределять работу.

Это предварительная версия для разработчиков, а не стандартная функция Windows. Для неё нужны совместимые сборки Windows, предварительные драйверы и поставщик NetworkDirect на каждом ПК. Компьютеры следует подключать напрямую в конфигурации «полная сеть»; последовательное соединение крайне не рекомендуется из-за резкого падения производительности.
Для двух ПК достаточно одного кабеля USB4 между ними. Для кластера из трёх систем потребуется два порта USB4 на каждом компьютере. Microsoft заявляет о поддержке портов 40 Гбит/с, а порты 80 Гбит/с (включая Thunderbolt 5) обеспечивают вдвое большую номинальную скорость соединения. Это скорости интерфейса, а не гарантированная пропускная способность приложений.
Есть и существенные ограничения по настройке и безопасности: инструкции требуют тестовой подписи, что влечёт отключение Secure Boot. Microsoft рекомендует использовать выделенные тестовые ПК, а не основные системы. Транспорт не переподключается автоматически при обрыве связи — приложениям нужно заново устанавливать соединение. Программное обеспечение экспериментальное и не должно рассматриваться как готовая функция ИИ для потребителей.
Анонс примечателен тем, что предлагает владельцам существующих ПК с USB4 собрать небольшой распределённый кластер. Однако технология не объединяет память физически так же, как единый чип с общей памятью, и не обещает линейного масштабирования производительности. На результаты повлияют задержка, пропускная способность передачи и программные накладные расходы. Тем не менее подход может дать энтузиастам и разработчикам более дешёвый способ тестировать более крупные локальные модели, объединяя уже имеющиеся машины.

ixkxai.title: UTA Hires Sam Yabrow As Talent Agent
ixkxai.content:
EXCLUSIVE: UTA has hired Sam Yabrow as a talent agent based in its Los Angeles office.

Yabrow joins from Buchwald, bringing nearly a decade of entertainment industry experience spanning casting and talent representation.

Clients expected to join him at UTA include Will Price (The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, The Chair Company), Igby Rigney (The Shards), Everett Blunck (The Plague, The Audacity) and Jaren Lewison (Eternally Yours).

Yabrow began his career in casting in New York before moving into talent representation at Abrams Artists Agency, later known as A3 Artists Agency. Following A3’s closure in 2024, he joined Buchwald, where he spent the past two and a half years. He relocated to Los Angeles earlier this year.

Originally from Georgia, Yabrow is a graduate of the University of Michigan.

bhnw3y.title: Украинские учебники сжигали. Экс-директор лицея в Олешках об оккупации
bhnw3y.content:
По случаю Всемирного дня ребенка, который отмечается 20 ноября, в Европарламенте состоялась дискуссия о нарушении прав украинских детей в условиях российской агрессии. Среди участников - бывшая директор Раденского лицея Олешковского городского совета Наталья Васильева, которая была свидетелем того, как российские оккупационные силы уничтожали систему украинского образования на захваченной части Херсонcкой области. О том, как это происходило, Наталья Васильева рассказала в интервью DW.

Deutsche Welle: Госпожа Васильева, когда после оккупации Олешек стало понятно, что россияне не просто захватили территорию, а пытаются установить контроль над украинским образованием?

Наталья Васильева: Буквально с первых дней захвата Олешек оккупационные власти занялись управлением образования. Они начали уверять педагогов в том, что российское образование лучше, что украинское образование не дает знаний нашим детям. И они хотят, чтобы мы открыли школы для детей и проводили обучение, но по российским стандартам.

Большинство учителей не перешли на сторону российских оккупантов, на работу никто не выходил, мы переходили на дистанционное обучение, и таким образом, поскольку у нас был интернет, работали с детьми и проводили занятия по украинским программам в режиме онлайн. Так продолжалось до лета 2022 года. Я как директор лицея ходила на работу, но потом они (представители оккупационных властей. - Ред.) приехали ко мне. Поскольку я не давала согласия на сотрудничество, у меня отобрали ключи от лицея и потом даже не разрешали заходить в помещение.

- Впоследствии школы все-таки открылись. Кто пришел туда работать?

- Школы открылись только тогда, когда оккупационные власти имели уже определенный состав людей, которые заменили украинских учителей, не согласившихся на сотрудничество. Хотя среди них было определенное количество тех учителей, которые предали свою родину. Но большинство - это были люди или вообще не причастные к системе образования, или привезенные из России.

- Что российские оккупанты сделали с украинскими учебниками и другими учебными материалами, которые оставались в школах?

- Все методические материалы они выбрасывали, уничтожали. Украинские учебники, украинский язык, литература, история Украины. Эти учебники практически сжигались. Из них устраивали так называемые "пионерские костры".

- Контролировали ли российские оккупанты, на каком языке общались дети?

- То, что дети должны были говорить по-русски, а общение на украинском не допускалось, было требованием, которое даже не обсуждалось. Поэтому дети должны были говорить по-русски, их заставлять учить и петь гимн России.

- Был ли в программе украинский язык как предмет?

- Я знаю, что позже был введен один час в неделю для предмета "Родная речь", это и был украинский язык. Что касается истории Украины, то она не преподавалась, потому что они сказали, что Украины как страны не существует, поэтому и истории Украины быть не может.

- Как готовили учителей для работы по российским образовательным программам?

- В нашей Олешковской общине они организовывали всех, кого пригласили на работу в школы, которые должны были открыть, и возили их на учебу в Краснодарский край и Крым, а потом они уже возвращались сюда, чтобы преподавать по российским стандартам.

- А как воспринимали дети это принудительное изменение образования?

- Для детей это было очень больно. Но ведь они не могут сопротивляться взрослым, тем более вооруженным. Школы были окружены российскими военными, и в учебное заведение пропускали только детей.

- Могли ли дети, остававшиеся в оккупации, продолжать обучение по украинской программе онлайн? Насколько это было доступно и безопасно?

- В то время и по сей день с интернетом довольно сложно, потому что украинского провайдера там нет с начала войны, а они своего провайдера не запустили так, как надо, поэтому со связью очень плохо. Нельзя связаться с людьми, чтобы, например, даже пообщаться. Так что с онлайн-занятиями было сложно и опасно. Родителей заставляли отдавать детей в школы, шантажировали, что иначе детей заберут в интернаты, будут штрафовать. Так что родители вынуждены были разрешать своим детям посещать школы, где преподавали по российским стандартам.

- Как вы думаете, какие последствия для детей будет иметь то, что их силой заставили кардинально изменить привычную для них образовательную среду?

- Для детей это, прежде всего, глубокая психологическая травма. Они до сих пор вспоминают эти события. А также это нарушение права ребенка знать традиции, культуру, историю своей страны, получать образование на том языке, на котором он хочет, в конце концов, права знать о своей идентичности, то, что ты - украинец. У ребенка забрали право свободно передвигаться по своей украинской земле. У них нет безопасного детства. Вот где можно купить, например, игрушки или детские книги? Куда можно поехать на оздоровление? Где тот кружок, в который ребенок привык ходить и заниматься любимым делом? Это все нарушено, просто нарушена вся жизнь.

- Что, по вашему мнению, нужно сделать сегодня, чтобы помочь детям, пережившим оккупацию? Возможно, чем-то могут помочь европейские партнеры?

- Думаю, нужно искать возможности договариваться о безопасных коридорах для эвакуации детей, которые остаются на временно оккупированных территориях. Если у зарубежных партнеров есть такая возможность, то приглашать вернувшихся с временно оккупированных территорий детей на оздоровление, чтобы дети могли как-то отвлечься от страшных событий, которые они пережили.

- Вы продолжаете сейчас преподавать?

- Нет, я уже не преподаю, а работаю детским психологом. Но три учебных заведения Олешковской общины функционируют дистанционно, и в них учатся дети, переехавшие на подконтрольную Украине территорию, или те, которые вместе с семьями выехали за границу. Они могут учиться со своими родными учителями. У них сохраняется хотя бы какое-то чувство коллектива, своего, родного, напоминающего о земле, где они родились.

8mxzql.title: Louis Garrel And Harry Lawtey Join Jeremy Allen White In Ben Stiller-Directed ‘Airman’ From Laika Live-Action And A24
8mxzql.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Louis Garrel and Harry Lawtey are set to join Jeremy Allen White in the Laika Live Action and A24 World War II survival thriller Airman directed by Ben Stiller.

Based on the New York Times bestseller The Lost Airman: A True Story of Escape from Nazi-Occupied France by Seth Meyerowitz, the film recounts the harrowing and remarkable untold story of Arthur Meyerowitz, who was shot down over Nazi-occupied France and evaded Gestapo pursuers for months before attempting a daring escape. The book was published in 2016 by Penguin.

The script is by Ben Shattuck and Stiller. Three-time Oscar winner Emmanuel Lubezki has been tapped as director of photography, Christian Goldbeck as production designer, Małgorzata Karpiuk as costume designer and Geoffrey Richman as editor.

Laika Live Action will lead production alongside A24, which will also handle domestic distribution and international sales. The film is a Le Grisbi Productions and Storyteller Productions production, in association with Red Hour Films and Nine Stories.

Stiller will produce for his Red Hour Films as will John Lesher for his Le Grisbi Productions, PJ van Sandwijk for his Storyteller Productions, Travis Knight and Matt Levin for Laika, and A24. Executive producers are Maryse Knight, Jeremy Kipp Walker and Zac Locke for Laika, Michael Lesslie and Marie Savare for Storyteller, Jake Gyllenhaal for Nine Stories and Miki Emmerich, Richard Whelan, Meyerowitz, Dan Bodansky and James Dixon. Gian Pablo Antonetti serves as co-producer for Le Grisbi.

“We’re thrilled to partner with A24, Ben and Jeremy on a film that embodies our commitment to bold, filmmaker-driven cinema,” said Matt Levin, Laika’s President of Live Action Film & Series. “Ben is an extraordinary talent with a singular creative vision, and we couldn’t be more excited to bring this incredible true story to life together.”

Stiller is represented by WME, VIE and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. White is represented by WME. Garrel is represented by UTA and Agence Adequat. Lawtey is represented by CAA, B-Side and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman, Smelkinson & Christopher.

4hxn2a.title: The Best 2026 Games to Gift a Steam Deck Owner This Holiday Season - Steam Deck HQ
4hxn2a.content:
If you haven’t yet, follow us on X (Twitter), Mastodon, or Bluesky to know when we post new articles, and join our Reddit or Subscribe to us on YouTube to check out our content and interact with our awesome community. Thank you for supporting us!

The holidays are fast approaching, and you may be thinking about getting a new game to treat yourself, or you may be looking for some games to get for friends or family. So, I wanted to go over some games I recommend checking out, and who may enjoy them.

For this list, I am focusing on games that were released this year. There are a ton of great games to enjoy on the Steam Deck that have been released previously, but I want to focus on newer releases for this one.

Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game – For Fighting Game Fans (SDHQ Review)

Avatar Legends is a masterpiece. It takes everything that makes fighting games special and executes it at an incredibly high level, while remaining welcoming to newcomers through its outstanding tutorials and accessibility options. Combined with its breathtaking 100% hand-drawn visuals that perfectly capture the spirit of the animated series, it stands as one of the most impressive and memorable fighting games we’ve ever played.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse – For Metroidvania Fans (SDHQ Review)

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse brings Castlevania back after a 12-year hiatus on an extremely high note. The peak level design and fluid combat elevate the experience even more than I remember from older games. Going with developer Evil Empire was the right choice for this kind of game, and I can easily blow off the minor issues and enjoy everything great this game has to offer.

You can get the game on Fanatical for $22.49 (25% Off) to save.

Dead as Disco – For Rhythm Game Fans (SDHQ Review)

What Dead as Disco already gets right is arguably the hardest part: it has a combat system that feels fantastic, and a musical backbone that elevates it beyond simple imitation. If you’ve ever loved the rhythm and flow of Arkham-style combat, this is a game that understands exactly why that worked – and then dares to remix it into something fresh.

Demon Tides – For Fans of 3D Platformers (SDHQ Review)

Demon Tides exceeded almost all of my expectations. The mechanics are tight and sound, with a great level of customization to modify our moveset in unique ways that cater to how we want to play. The open world and player-driven exploration make finding islands with platforming challenges more engaging, while the rewards for completing these were worthwhile and motivating. There are some minor issues here and there, but none of them take away from how well-built the game is.

Denshattack! – For Fans of Skateboarding Games (SDHQ Review)

Denshattack! surprised me in many ways. Its constant action, accessible mechanics, and vibrant, cinematic visuals create a magical experience that can’t be found regularly. Each stage offers something new, whether it be different objectives or completely different events that change how we play it out.

You can get it for $15.55 (22% Off) on Fanatical to save some money.

Dragon Quest VII Reimagined – For Fans of JRPGs (SDHQ Review)

Dragon Quest 7 Reimagined is a fantastic remake of the original that addresses many of its problems. The story has been streamlined with some great additions to make the other characters stand out more, while the combat has the accessibility settings and adjustments that the most recent games benefit from. It does feel a little too easy at times, which makes the strategic elements of battle feel less necessary, but it never fully detracts from the experience enough to regret playing.

You can get the game for $38.99 (35% Off) on Humble to save.

Esoteric Ebb – For Fans of CRPGs (SDHQ Review)

Esoteric Ebb is a tough game to pin down, but the closest I could describe it as is a CRPG with Visual Novel elements. A lot of burden is placed on the writing, and fortunately, the writing is really good. Almost all action is handled through the dialogue system, and the traditional CRPG mechanics work really well for conversations. As long as you can cope with the somewhat irritating combat mechanics and RNG, Esoteric Ebb is a fun time.

You can get the game for $21.99 (12% Off) to save some money.

Final Fantasy Resonance – For Fans of Octopath Traveler (SDHQ Review)

Final Fantasy Resonance brings Final Fantasy to the HD-2D style, and it ends up pushing what I thought this style could handle. The cinematic cutscenes elevate the fantastic story from Brave Exvius, with exceptional combat and interesting new ways to strategize. The minor nuisances from combat don’t impact the splendid experience that comes from the best HD-2D game I’ve played, and it has become one of my favorite Final Fantasy experiences.

Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library! – For Fans of Casual Simulators

This is a simple game about putting the correct books away on a shelf one by one, and while it’s tedious, it’s also very calming. As we keep playing, we will get new magical powers to help us sort and put books away faster, and it becomes extremely satisfying as we complete row after row and upgrade our powers. It runs like a charm on the Steam Deck, and it’s just a treat.

Mouse: P.I. For Hire – For Fans of First-Person Shooters (SDHQ Review)

Mouse P.I. For Hire is a solid shooter with a beautiful aesthetic and interesting story, but the combat can feel a little too generic. The expressive rubber hose animation works, wonders, and the great cast help bring the characters to life in this mystery thriller, but I found it difficult to stay interested for longer periods of time because it didn’t have that spark that other big shooters have. Still, it’s a fantastic shooter nonetheless, and a perfect one to take on the go.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword – For Fans of Action RPGs (SDHQ Review)

Onimusha: Way of the Sword is an incredible Action RPG with combat that feels unmatched. The actual fighting just feels incredible between the slashing, parrying, and dodging; everything just clicks where it needs to and made me want to seek out grunts to kill just so I could get more. There are a few nuisances here and there, like with locking on, and the voice acting isn’t always the best, but the story and world are enjoyable to experience.

You can get it for $57.39 (18% Off) on Fanatical to save.

PRAGMATA – For Fans of Third-Person Shooters (SDHQ Review)

I don’t give out perfect scores lightly, and I mulled over this for some time, but there was almost no part of PRAGMATA I disliked. The story had emotional weight and surprised me with its twists, and the combination of puzzle and action in real time made fights engaging, and the temporary weapons continually made combat feel dynamic. The simple progression was enjoyable, and I felt that every single collectible I could find held meaning that made me more powerful. This is a must-have game.

You can get the game for $47.99 (20% Off) on Humble to save.

Queen’s Domain – For Fans of RPGs

Resident Evil Requiem – For Fans of Survival Horror (SDHQ Review)

Resident Evil Requiem finds a way to bring the newer and older gameplay styles that have defined the franchise into an exceptionally enjoyable experience that is perfect for fans of the series. The meshing of Grace’s slower, stealthier gameplay with Leon’s action-packed killing works wonderfully, giving us the best of both worlds.

You can get it for $48.99 (30% Off) on Humble to save some money.

TAMASHIKA – For Fans of First-Person Shooters (SDHQ Review)

TAMASHIKA is a weird, fast-paced FPS that doesn’t need an overwhelming amount of content to prove its worth. The balance of visual craziness and audio cues turns each run into a skill-driven rush to kill every enemy on screen and get to the end of the level as fast as possible. And with how tight the core mechanics are, it’s hard not to love every second of it. The game is extremely small, and I mean, only one small, procedurally-generated level, but I still couldn’t stop myself from playing that same level over and over until the next day came and I could try a completely new level to top the leaderboard.

Warhammer Survivors – For Fans of Vampire Survivors (SDHQ Review)

Despite similarities to the game that defined its genre, Warhammer Survivors found its own identity. The Warhammer references throughout the game are exciting, and fans of the series will fall in love. And no matter how simple and repetitive the gameplay loop is, it’s always exciting and never gets old.

And those are the games I recommend checking out! All of them are awesome for one reason or another, and we loved them when we reviewed them. I’m sure there are a ton of great deals to find over the next few weeks, and there will be sales for sure, but I would look at these games and consider them no matter what.

If you enjoyed this article, check out the rest of the content on SteamDeckHQ! We have a wide variety of game reviews and news that are sure to help your gaming experience. Whether you’re looking for news, tips and tutorials, game settings and reviews, or just want to stay up-to-date on the latest trends, we’ve got your back.

58z0ll.title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
58z0ll.content:
Hackers used an autonomous AI agent platform called "Cairn" to discover a zero-day vulnerability in a medical imaging application and exploit it to take complete control of a server.

According to Amazon Threat Intelligence, the suspected Chinese-linked attackers simply instructed the AI agents to "obtain shell access," leaving them to independently discover and exploit the flaw.

Amazon Threat Intelligence uncovered the campaign after discovering that the attackers had left their Cairn instance publicly accessible without authentication, exposing their hacking operations.

According to the researchers, the attacks were launched by a Chinese-nexus threat actor between September 8 and 10, 2026, targeting mainly East Asian educational institutions outside China.

Cairn is a legitimate pentesting tool that can be used to coordinate multiple AI agents in cyber-operations, created for research and defense strengthening.

Gambit Security documented cases of Cairn abuse as part of a large-scale credit card stealing operation in September. More recently, Google reported it was deployed in an attack against an aerospace organization in the U.S.

During the campaign investigated by Amazon, the AI agents were not always successful. For example, a 16-hour and 148-action effort to take control of a Redis server failed.

In a separate case targeting a university GPU server, the agents tried over 30,000 credential combinations over six hours but failed to brute-force their way in.

Finding and using a zero-day

According to Amazon, Cairn's AI agents found a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging application that uses AI to help researchers label medical images.

The flaw enabled the agents to write files to arbitrary locations on the server, and within 11 minutes, they went from mapping the application's API to exploiting the vulnerability.

In a subsequent session, the AI agents used the flaw to write a Python reverse shell to the sitecustomize.py file that automatically loads when Python starts, then triggered an API endpoint to establish root access to the server.

After discovering the zero-day, the operator provided the agents with a proxy into a second university network running the same vulnerable software and directed them to target other machines.

Amazon reported the flaw to MONAI Label maintainers, and they released a security update to address it on November 18.

The researchers attributed the campaign to a Chinese-nexus threat actor with moderate confidence, based on the language of the retrieved prompts, the activity timestamps, and the choice of targets.

Amazon also shared two IP addresses associated with the campaign, observed between September 8 and 10, 2026:

142[.]4.98.145
142[.]4.107.34

Amazon warned that AI agents can find and exploit vulnerabilities faster than security teams can react, urging organizations to rely more on automated defenses rather than manual investigations.

Public humiliation reportedly considered a "rite of passage".

Image credit: Nvidia

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the company which has long played a major role in PC gaming.
Following Huang's departure, The New York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

Nvidia faced backlash this year when it revealed the generative AI-powered DLSS 5.Watch on YouTube

The report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, said everyone hoped they'd drop dead.Huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".
It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's said often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.
A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the New York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, said the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".
Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly said earlier this week that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

1sw2ref.title: Golden Globes Category Chaos: When ‘The Drama’ Is a Comedy…
1sw2ref.content:
The Drama is a comedy — or so say the backers of the film, about an engaged couple’s darkest secrets, in their submission for the Golden Globes, which requires all films be entered as either A) a drama or B) a musical or a comedy. And that’s not even one of this year’s more questionable submissions.

Other comedy entries include I Play Rocky, about the making of Rocky (which competed at the Globes as a drama); Obsession, about a young woman’s loss of agency; Tender Loving Care, about the frustrations of two young women, including the decline of one’s father; Artificial, about AI growing out of control; and Project Hail Mary, about a man sent into space against his will to try to stave off the end of the world. Meanwhile, Club Kid, about a man-child who ends up with a child — widely described as an elevated version of Adam Sandler’s comedy Big Daddy — has been entered as a drama.

Yes, all of the aforementioned musical/comedy submissions have moments of laughter and all of the dramas have elements of drama — but still, these classifications are pretty eyebrow-raising, begging the questions: What is going on? And is there a better way?

***

The first Globes were held in 1944. There were no genre-specific Globes categories until the eighth, when the lead acting categories were split into two, one for dramas, the other for musicals/comedies. The following year, the same split was implemented for best picture. That category was reunified for the 11th ceremony, but the split was brought back for the 12th and every year since, helping to attract more stars to the ceremony.

Until 2023, Globes category submissions were made by studios and reviewed by the HFPA’s reminders list committee, which rarely overturned anything, even as dramas with music passed as musicals (Ray, Walk the Line and Rocketman), dramas with few laughs passed as comedies (Ghost, The Tourist and My Week With Marilyn) and comedies passed as dramas (All About Eve, Born Yesterday, Harvey and Sunset Boulevard — all in the same year). Once in a blue moon, the committee would reject a submission (Promising Young Woman as a musical/comedy), but it usually deferred to studios’ preferences.

Frustrations burst into the open in 2015 after The Martian, a film about an astronaut stranded on Mars, was submitted and accepted as a musical/comedy. Judd Apatow, whose comedy Trainwreck was in contention that year, tweeted, “Trying to dominate the comedy category when you are really a drama afraid of dramatic competition is a punk move.” The Martian ended up beating Trainwreck for best picture, something Apatow was still smarting over when he presented at this year’s Globes: “My film Trainwreck lost best comedy to Ridley Scott’s The Martian. You know Ridley Scott, America’s favorite comedy director — director of such hilarious comedies as Gladiator, Blade Runner and Alien? I can’t wait till later tonight when best comedy is won by Hamnet.”

But ownership of the Globes had changed in 2023 (the Globes now share the same owners as THR), resulting in widespread reforms. This year’s rules declare: “Motion pictures shall be entered in the category that best matches the overall intent, tone and content of the film. Therefore, a motion picture that is primarily intended to have a serious or dramatic tone but contains comedic overtones or elements shall be entered as a drama as opposed to a comedy. Likewise, a motion picture that is primarily intended to have a comedic or satirical tone but contains dramatic overtones or elements shall be entered as a comedy as opposed to a drama.”

Once the film submission period ends (Nov. 24 this year), an eligibility committee comprising current Globes voters (the quantity and names are kept private) evaluates every submission for “potential misclassification issues.” If found, they “may contact the studio … to discuss those issues and to resolve them informally.” Eventually, the eligibility committee meets with a review committee to discuss any outstanding concerns, and those committees — or at least members of them who have seen a film in question — vote to determine if a change is necessary; two-thirds must favor a change for one to occur.

***

The Drama, starring Robert Pattinson and Zendaya, was submitted in the musical/comedy category for this year’s Golden Globes.

Courtesy of A24

Why do people try to game the Globes categories? Because the nationally telecast Globes ceremony provides the biggest spotlight for awards contenders before Oscar nominations voting (the 2027 Globes will take place Jan. 10, and Oscar nomination voting starts the next morning), making it highly valuable for a film or individual to be represented at the ceremony as a nominee or, better still, a winner.

There usually are fewer standout musicals and comedies than dramas, meaning it’s often easier to land a nom or win if a drama can pass as a musical/comedy. (This year’s aforementioned musical/comedy submissions surely wanted to get out of the way of The Odyssey.) Another motivation: Studios with multiple films prefer to not have them pitted against one another. (A24 probably wants Club Kid to compete as a drama because it already has The Invite and The Debut up for best musical/comedy, just as Neon probably wants Artificial to compete as a comedy because it already has All of a Sudden, Fjord and Paper Tiger up for best drama.)

It remains to be seen whether the Globes’ eligibility committee will overturn some of this year’s submissions. (Reports suggest it already rejected Michael as a musical/comedy.)

Moving forward, it would make everyone’s life easier if the Globes consolidated its genre-specific categories — picture, actor and actress — into single categories with 12 slots rather than divided categories with six each. Or, if the Globes prefers to continue to have multiple categories for each in order to yield twice as many winners, it might consider retaining the “drama” label for one but changing the other to “genre,” which would better describe recent musical/comedy nominees like Poor Things, The Substance and Bugonia.

This story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Click here to subscribe.

h9upqu.title: Том Харди, Пирс Броснан и Хелен Миррен приступили к съемкам в третьем сезоне "Гангстерленда"
h9upqu.content:
Как сообщает издание Variety, в Великобритании официально началось производство третьего сезона сериала «Гангстерленд» (MobLand). К своим ролям вернулись исполнители главных ролей: Том Харди, Пирс Броснан и Хелен Миррен.
Том Харди вновь воплотит образ Гарри да Соузы — опытного посредника («решалы»), работающего в криминальном мире. Ранее в этом году в СМИ появлялись сообщения о возможном уходе актера из проекта на фоне творческих разногласий с продюсером Дэвидом Глассером и сценаристом Джезом Баттеруортом. Источники утверждали, что Харди якобы опаздывал на съемочную площадку и настаивал на правках в сценарии. Однако режиссер Гай Ричи и руководство Paramount Studios были заинтересованы в сохранении актера в основном составе, и вскоре сторонам удалось урегулировать конфликт.
Хелен Миррен и Пирс Броснан вернутся к ролям Мейв и Конрада Харриганов — глав криминального клана, вокруг которого строится сюжет сериала.
Помимо них, в новом сезоне снимаются Пэдди Консидайн, Джоанн Фроггатт, Лара Пулвер и Тоби Джонс.

16hd8di.title: Dispatches from O'Reilly: Inside a software factory
16hd8di.content: [Ed. note: This article was originally published on O’Reilly Media’s blog, Radar. Republished with permission.]—————————-As a software engineer with more than seven years of experience before the coding-agent era, I never liked the idea of vibe coding. But I knew there was a clear line between it and using coding agents to generate clean, maintainable code. That line, where good software principles meet coding agents, is defined by software factories.That’s why, three months ago, I built my own software factory, Squid, to ship all of Decoding AI’s small and medium projects with minimal human intervention. The first version was so overbuilt I stopped using it.Meanwhile, I kept seeing people obsess over the next “_____ engineering” label, instead of focusing on actionable outcomes. Prompt engineering, then context engineering, then harness engineering. So far, so good. But in the last few weeks (July 2026 as I write this), things got off track with loop engineering and graph engineering, which already read more like marketing talk than like anything that solves real problems. Graph engineering overtheorizes how teams have built AI applications since the LangGraph era kicked off in ~2024. Don’t get me wrong. The terms aren’t wrong (Boris Cherny, who leads Claude Code at Anthropic, says, “My job is to write loops”), but we’re overexplaining intuitive things we started doing years ago.While you’re defining what counts as a loop, you’re not thinking about the processes that actually deliver software.The right frame is the software factory, which was one of the core themes at AI Engineer World’s Fair 2026, where Tereza Tížková (growth at Factory.ai) defined one as “the whole loop, the whole lifecycle of developing software with autonomy.”I bet you already have an intuitive sense of what a software factory is. In this article, I want to further formalize it and map it onto the software development lifecycle (SDLC). We’ll explore how big your software factory should be, and when to stop automating before it adds more friction than value. Most importantly, I want to highlight where the human belongs in this process, and where I believe they’ll still belong even in a world where all the code is generated by AI.So…what’s worth automating? Where does the human bring the most value? What’s worth building, and what’s worth buying?Like a physical factory, a software factory automates software creation with minimal human input. Raw work (bug reports, feature ideas, incidents) goes in. Shipped software comes out. It needs a few highly qualified people making high-leverage decisions, and defined gates that work can’t pass through without them.Factory.ai pitches “a self-improving system for your Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).” Addy Osmani frames the stack as loop, harness, factory: “The loop is the atom”; a factory is “an org chart made of loops.” Warp’s CEO, Zach Lloyd, states that “software engineering will become factory engineering.”The software factory line. Eight stages over one shared context layer, with production signals looping back as new tasks.The factory is made up of eight stages that can be divided into three buckets:What to build. Triage/intake classifies, deduplicates, and routes incoming work. Brainstorming finds high-impact features through market analysis, user data, and technical research. Planning, the most important stage, turns that research into a polished plan, refines it by letting the agent grill you, and tracks decisions in an ADR (Architecture Decision Record) log plus a glossary. The outputs of this stage are tickets backed by documentation that a team of agents can implement, which can be tracked in plain files or a project management tool, such as GitHub Issues, Linear, or Notion.At this stage, the agent plans in read-only mode, going through the code, the AGENTS.md file, and most importantly the context layer.Actual building and checking. Implementing is a software engineer and QA agent loop that goes through the tasks and supporting documentation. Review checks the PR diff against product, architecture, and code standards. Review-CI runs the test suite, and failures trigger a fixing agent. Release handles CD to staging/production with human deployment checks.Self-improving. Monitor/incident response feeds production signals (alerts, errors, incidents) back into triage as fresh input on what to build next, closing the loop.Orthogonal to the eight stages, we have the context layer. The layer is especially important at the front of the line. Brainstorming is limited to the data it sees: user analytics, competitor analysis, research, transcripts, and documentation. At this stage, a poor context layer directly limits the space of possibilities you can explore. It has a similar impact on planning, where transforming the raw idea into technical specs and tasks depends heavily on how good the examples in the context layer are. If you want to implement a new product-recommendation feature, and you have zero examples, the LLM will just predict the most common thing to do, which often isn’t the best solution for your product.The context layer can take many forms. One strategy that is becoming increasingly popular is the LLM Wiki, a term coined by Andrej Karpathy. It’s basically a strategy to transform your data into a structured knowledge base, just by using files, instead of a database. Factory, via its AutoWiki feature, transforms popular codebases into a structured knowledge base that agents can query instead of parsing the codebase itself. LangChain recently released OpenWiki, a CLI tool to manage wikis for agent memory. If you’re curious, in this article I detail how I turn my data from Obsidian, Readwise, and Google Drive into agent memory via LLM wikis.To see where the human belongs, let’s walk through the factory with an end-to-end example. We’ll build a feature for a shopping-assistant agent on an ecommerce platform similar to Amazon’s. The scenario is that usage data says users aren’t engaging with its recommendations, and we have to ship an improvement.Brainstorm is where taste lives. Agents do the grunt work: They analyze user activity, scan competitors’ assistants, and pull research into the knowledge base. Then a member of the technical staff starts looking at the data, understands why people are not engaging with the recommendations, explores how the competition implements their solution, and proposes a fix as a feature spec. At this stage, the spec solves a business problem. It doesn’t need to prescribe a technical solution yet.Plan is where a human, with the help of the software factory, transforms the feature spec into an implementation plan. Let’s assume that we want to make a change to the recommender engine algorithm. The human chats with the knowledge base, figures out whether it’s feasible, and thinks through architecture, interfaces, data flow, cost, and latency. They then let the agent scan the codebase and grill them until the plan is properly refined into something that fits the codebase. The output is a bunch of tickets plus an ADR explaining the algorithm change and an update to the glossary.The agent can help within these two stages by quickly scanning through a ton of data and improving the plan, but the human is still central.Use the strongest model (Fable) for brainstorming and planning. These stages burn fewer tokens than implementation itself, but everything downstream depends on them. A well-written plan lets cheaper models (Opus, Sonnet) execute without reasoning their way out of dead ends. A weak plan makes them retry until the extra tokens erase the price gap.With a weak plan, I’ve watched Sonnet on high reasoning out-cost Opus on the same task: The smaller model needs more attempts to reach the same goal. Total cost is tokens × price, not model tier. So more failures equals more reasoning, more tokens, and more cost.From here on, we move into “loop” and “graph” engineering territory.A strong planning session makes cheap executors actually cheap, while a weak plan makes them expensive.Implement runs a software engineer agent that picks up every ticket that’s ready to go. As the loop is scoped to a feature, it takes only the associated tickets. After each ticket is implemented, a QA agent tries to find bugs by stress-testing the application. As agents tend to have a positive bias towards their own work, the split between the software engineer and QA agents matters. As Addy Osmani puts it, the model that wrote the code is “way too nice grading its own homework.” This loop, at solo scale, can be as simple as a bunch of terminals pulling tickets. At larger scale, it runs on remote agents working 24/7.The loop only works if agents can interact with the app. The QA agent needs one command that starts the whole stack reproducibly. From there, it drives the app in the browser, calls the data or fine-tuning pipelines, or hits your server’s API. Whatever your app’s interface is, the agent needs access to it, the same way a human user would.The key idea is to integrate feedback loops as natively as possible into your software factory. Ideally, you want multiple levels, depending on how expensive it is to run them: linting, unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end tests. When the loop keeps failing, the root cause is almost always missing plumbing, not the agents.Review has three steps. Step one checks the product and architecture requirements against the ticket and the ADR. Any discrepancy becomes a new ticket passed back to the implement loop. Step two ensures code quality (modularity, naming) and guards against AI slop such as verbose comments or cryptic function names. Step three looks at the CI/CD pipeline. At every step, any failure auto-creates a task picked up by the software agent.Not every project needs all three steps. The “factory” ends with a PR that you as a human need to review and merge. But in reality, if you spend enough time creating a strong plan, the PR that reaches you is usually ready to ship as-is.The dynamics between what humans and agents own in the software factory line.So where does the human belong? You’re indispensable during brainstorming and planning, and you return for the final check. Agents own everything in between. OpenAI took this to the extreme: ~1M lines and ~1,500 merged PRs over five months with zero hand-written lines. Their framing is “Humans steer. Agents execute.”With my first Squid version (my own software factory), I got greedy and chased full autonomy: big remote workflows, parallel agents, and one grand pipeline running end to end. It worked, until something went off script. Which it usually does. I couldn’t debug it, couldn’t halt it mid-run, and couldn’t redirect it without throwing the run away. It was a big monolith that took me too far out of the loop, and I couldn’t control it.I realized you need two options. The first is granular commands that let you grill your plan, implement a specific task, or review one particular step. The second, for when you’re comfortable giving the agent 24/7 autonomy, is an end-to-end command that chains all the smaller ones into a fully autonomous graph, such as one big /plan and /implement-review-all command. Basically, each step is a “loop,” while the whole pipeline is the “graph” of your software factory. Still, note how planning and the rest are split into two different commands, as planning is, and always will be, human-driven (at least if you want the result to stay aligned with what you actually want).Bottom line. You need to be able to step in, halt it, redirect it, and interrupt it, while still having the option to go fully autonomous.The bottleneck is me, and that’s by design. To be honest, I’ve worked mostly solo since the AI coding agent boom, and I don’t understand who the people shipping 100 features in parallel are. Most of my features (per project) build on one another, which makes them impossible to parallelize. As the project grows, you can find more and more independent features that can be implemented in parallel, but I still believe that number is limited.That’s why, when I parallelize, I only use local agents, each running in an isolated codebase via work trees. So far, I’ve never felt the need for 24/7 remote agents, or wanted the overhead of managing them.A big team can justify more automation, but it has to earn it. So as with any other software product, start small, start by automating the most time-consuming bottlenecks, and add complexity gradually as people get comfortable with the system. Don’t be like me, with my Squid experiment.In all scenarios, you’ll start with a prebuilt coding harness. The most popular vendor-locked ones are Claude Code and Codex. Or go open source with OpenCode or Pi, which took off thanks to its minimalist, extensible architecture that lets you easily build on top of it.But picking a harness isn’t the same as knowing how to configure it and wire it into your software factory. That’s why everyone needs to know, at least intuitively, how a coding agent works under the hood: the agent loop running in your terminal, what changes when it runs remotely, how you evaluate it, and which context engineering strategies keep it cheap without making it dumber. If you want to learn more about building a coding agent from scratch, consider exploring my open source course on GitHub. Even if you never plan to build your own harness, that intuition is what lets you become a power user.For a small team, you’ll get extremely far just by defining a set of skills and agents that encode your process on top of the coding harness (a.k.a. your software factory). To keep it simple, this is what I did with Squid, which I use to implement all my projects.There are other off-the-shelf “software factories” powered just by skills and agents defined in .md files, such as Matt Pocock’s skills repository or the BMad method.But remember that the factory is mostly about processes, not tools: A factory that doesn’t fit how your team already works adds friction, never gets adopted, and ends up useless.You cross the buy line the moment engineers you don’t personally supervise run agents. Observability, tracing, cost tracking, and pay-per-token billing stop being optional and become someone’s full-time job. Agent swarms wired into Linear, Slack, and CI across distributed infrastructure are a logistical hell that isn’t your product. That’s when it makes sense to look into off-the-shelf solutions such as Factory.ai (that comes with the Droid agent), or Warp’s Oz. In Warp CEO Zach Lloyd’s words, “Most of the factory is not necessarily a new interface. It is an integration into people’s existing workflows.”At the other end of the spectrum, you cross back to building when the platform’s constraints cost more than the team it would take to replace it, as OpenAI’s report on its Codex-built product shows.The smallest builds, the middle buys, and the largest builds again.Someone is already coining next quarter’s “_____ engineering” term as we speak. But the software engineering processes you use to output real code won’t change that often. That’s why you should be open-minded but at the same time focus on actionable outcomes, not on overthinking how to label things.As Zach Lloyd suggests: Find one “annoying part of your job” and build the smallest loop that handles it.The harsh reality is that software factories are just at the beginning. They’re far from perfect, and especially far from being fully “autonomous.” Usually, when someone claims they’ve cracked the software factory problem, they either haven’t tested the idea enough or are trying to sell it to you. I’m confident we’ll reach the point where almost the entire software development lifecycle is automated (with the exception of brainstorming and planning), but at the moment we’re still figuring things out.But here’s what I’m wondering:Which stage of your factory still needs you the most?
